definition_zh: 语言的；语言学的；与语言运用有关的
definition_en: relating to language or to the scientific study of language
core_image: 一页写满分句与箭头的手稿，句子之间用细线连起，页边标着几个小号数
scene: 书桌上摊着一页写满分句与箭头的手稿，句子之间用细线相连。 The editors examined linguistic clues before they dated the manuscript.
sceneCN: 这里指「与语言特征有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及语言本身的）；句意为编者在为手稿定年之前，先检查了语言线索。可辨识物件：手稿、分句、箭头、细线。

pos.zh: 语言的；语言学的

senses.title: Relating to language itself
senses.definition: concerning the sounds, words and grammar of a language
senses.definitionCN: 涉及一种语言的声音、词汇与语法
senses.example: Linguistic change is usually gradual rather than sudden.
senses.exampleCN: 语言变化通常是渐进的，而不是突然的。
senses.why: the adjective simply attaches the Latin word for language to any feature of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把拉丁语表「语言」的词挂到语言的任何特征上。

senses.title: Relating to the discipline of linguistics
senses.definition: belonging to the scientific study of language as a field
senses.definitionCN: 属于把语言作为研究对象的科学领域
senses.example: The paper appeared in a linguistic journal, not a literary one.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文发表在一份语言学刊物上，而非文学刊物。
senses.why: the noun for the field and the adjective for it differ by one ending, so the same description covers both language and its study.
senses.whyCN: 学科名词与它的形容词只差一个词尾，因此同一描述既覆盖语言，也覆盖对语言的研究。

senses.title: Inner knowledge of grammar
senses.titleCN: 说话者内在的语法知识
senses.definition: describing the tacit knowledge a speaker has of the rules of a language
senses.definitionCN: 描述说话者对某一语言规则的默会知识
senses.example: Children's linguistic competence grows faster than their vocabulary lists suggest.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童的语言能力增长得比词汇表所显示的更快。
senses.why: the discipline drew a line between what a speaker knows and what a speaker does.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科在「说话者知道什么」与「说话者做什么」之间划了一条线。

senses.title: A minority defined by its tongue
senses.titleCN: 以语言划分的少数群体
senses.definition: naming a community distinguished by the language it speaks
senses.definitionCN: 指以所说语言而区分出来的群体
senses.example: Linguistic minorities won the right to local schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 语言少数群体争取到了地方办学的权利。
senses.why: a community can be marked out by the tongue it uses, and the adjective follows that marker.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体可以由其所用语言标记出来，形容词便跟着这个标记走。

senses.title: Variety across languages
senses.definition: describing the range of different languages and their features
senses.definitionCN: 描述不同语言及其特征的分布范围
senses.example: The region's linguistic diversity is greater than its biological diversity.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的语言多样性超过它的生物多样性。
senses.why: counting different tongues turns the adjective into a word about range.
senses.whyCN: 把不同语言计数，就让这个形容词变成关于「范围」的词。

senses.title: Classification by structure
senses.definition: used of the comparison and classification of language structures
senses.definitionCN: 用于语言结构的比较与分类
senses.example: Linguistic typology groups languages by how they build sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 语言类型学按造句方式给语言分组。
senses.why: to compare structures is to classify them, and classification is another face of the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 比较结构就是给结构分类，而分类是这个形容词的另一副面孔。

senses.title: A barrier caused by language
senses.definition: describing an obstacle that arises because people do not share a tongue
senses.definitionCN: 描述因人们不共用一种语言而产生的障碍
senses.example: The linguistic barrier mattered more than the border itself.
senses.exampleCN: 语言障碍比边界本身更要紧。
senses.why: where tongues differ, communication can fail, so the adjective also names an obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 语言不同处，交流可能失败，因此这个形容词也指障碍。

senses.title: Wording used as evidence
senses.definition: describing features of wording that can identify or date a text
senses.definitionCN: 描述可用于识别或为文本定年的措辞特征
senses.example: Linguistic evidence placed the letter in the late sixteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 语言证据把这封信定在十六世纪后期。
senses.why: wording leaves traces that can be read, so the adjective moves from language to evidence.
senses.whyCN: 措辞留下可读的痕迹，因此这个形容词从语言转到证据。

intro.en: Linguistic is a nineteenth-century adjective built on Latin lingua 'tongue, language' with the ending -isticus, probably through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是十九世纪形成的形容词，建在拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」之上，带拉丁形容词词尾，很可能经法语传入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue' and 'language'; its deeper origin is unsettled and is not demonstrated by any attested older form.
items.cn: lingua 兼指「舌头」与「语言」；其更深来源无定论，也没有任何可证实的更早形式。

items.en: The ending -isticus, taken from Greek, built adjectives meaning 'of or relating to a practice or field'.
items.cn: 这个源自希腊语的词尾构成形容词，意为「属于或关于某实践或领域的」。

items.en: French formed linguistique for the study of language in the early nineteenth century, and English took the adjective soon after.
items.cn: 法语在十九世纪初为语言研究造出相应形容词，英语随后借入。

items.en: As linguistics became a university subject, the adjective came to mean both 'of language' and 'of the discipline'.
items.cn: 随着语言学成为大学学科，这个形容词既指「语言的」，也指「语言学的」。

items.en: The twentieth century added phrases such as linguistic minority and linguistic evidence, extending the adjective into law and history.
items.cn: 二十世纪增加了「语言少数群体」「语言证据」等说法，把这个形容词扩展到法律与历史领域。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the root is unknown, and the exact first English printing of the adjective is not documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定：该词根在拉丁语之前的来源不明，这个形容词最早的英语印刷记录亦无确切文献。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root words that are easily swapped for the adjective; group two holds adjectives describing language matters.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、容易与这个形容词混用的词；第二组是描述语言事务的形容词。

entries.definition: The name of the discipline; the adjective describes something within it.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科名称；形容词则描述该学科之内的事物。

entries.definition: A person who studies language; it is a noun for a doer.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究语言的人，是表施动者的名词。

entries.definition: The system itself; the adjective cannot stand for the system.
entries.definitionCN: 指系统本身；形容词不能替代那个系统。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of the tongue' in anatomy or dentistry, not 'of language'.
entries.definitionCN: 在解剖与牙科中指「舌的」，而非「语言的」。

entries.definition: Relating to words as opposed to actions; it does not refer to grammar or language systems.
entries.definitionCN: 指以词语而非行动表达，不涉及语法或语言系统。

entries.definition: Concerned with meaning rather than structure; it is one part of what linguistic covers.
entries.definitionCN: 关注意义而非结构，是语言研究覆盖的一部分。

entries.definition: Concerned with grammar or with whether a sentence is well formed.
entries.definitionCN: 关注语法或句子是否合式。

entries.definition: Relating to the older study of texts and languages; it is historical where linguistic is general.
entries.definitionCN: 指较旧的文本与语言考据之学，偏历史，而「语言的」更宽泛。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective carries the same root as the noun for tongue, so it always points back to speech.
normal.cn: 这个形容词与表「舌头」的名词共享词根，因此总指向言语。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the fields: linguistic diversity, linguistic evidence, linguistic minority.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示领域：语言多样性、语言证据、语言少数群体。

normal.en: The adverb adds a manner: linguistically speaking.
normal.cn: 副词加上方式：从语言上说。

normal.en: The family runs language, linguist, linguistics, bilingual, multilingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「语言」「语言学家」「语言学」「双语的」「多语的」。

normal.en: A text marked with arrows between clauses is the picture to keep.
normal.cn: 在分句之间画箭头的那页文本，是要留住的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a fingerprint made of vowels instead of ridges.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚由元音而非纹路组成的指纹。

abstract.en: Picture a map whose borders follow the spread of words.
abstract.cn: 想象一张边界沿着词语传播而画的图。

abstract.en: Picture a fence built between two villages out of untranslated signs.
abstract.cn: 想象两个村子之间用无法翻译的标牌搭成的一道栅栏。

examples.en: Linguistic differences often survive political union by centuries.
examples.cn: 语言差异常常在政治统一之后还延续几个世纪。

examples.en: The court accepted linguistic analysis as evidence of authorship.
examples.cn: 法庭接受语言分析作为作者身份的证据。

examples.en: Linguistic minorities asked for bilingual ballots.
examples.cn: 语言少数群体要求提供双语选票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「林归斯提克」——林子里归拢来的那套说话规矩，就是语言的。

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」加源自希腊语的形容词词尾构成，十九世纪经法语进入英语，指「语言的」，后也指「语言学的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all attach the adjective to a different object: the language itself, the discipline, the speaker's inner rules, a community, a range of tongues, a classification, a barrier and a piece of evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把这个形容词挂到不同对象上：语言本身、学科、说话者的内在规则、一个群体、语言的范围、一种分类、一道障碍以及一份证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a manuscript page where clauses are linked by thin arrows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页手稿，分句之间用细箭头相连。

branches.en: THE SIMPLEST LINK: any feature of a language can take the adjective.
branches.cn: 最简单的连接：语言的任何特征都能带这个形容词。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the same adjective also marks work done inside the discipline.
branches.cn: 学科：同一个形容词也标记学科内部的研究。

branches.en: INSIDE THE SPEAKER: tacit grammatical knowledge is a linguistic fact too.
branches.cn: 说话者之内：默会的语法知识同样是语言事实。

branches.en: GROUPS AND RANGES: communities are defined by tongues, and tongues differ widely.
branches.cn: 群体与范围：社群由语言界定，而语言彼此差异很大。

branches.en: ORDER, OBSTACLE, PROOF: structure can be classified, difference can block, and wording can testify.
branches.cn: 秩序、障碍与证据：结构可被分类，差异会成阻碍，而措辞可以提供证明。

intro.en: The word is a Latin-rooted adjective with a Greek-derived ending, so it can be read as root plus ending.
intro.cn: 这是一个带拉丁词根与希腊来源词尾的形容词，可按「词根加词尾」来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua supplies the root; the ending came into Latin from Greek and later built many English adjectives of fields and practices.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 提供词根；词尾经拉丁语来自希腊语，后来构成许多英语中表领域与实践的形容词。

items.example: The root ties every sense back to speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把每个义项都系回言语。

items.structure: Greek-derived ending via Latin, 'of or relating to'
items.meaning: belonging to a field or practice
items.example: The ending turns a field into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把领域变成描述词。

items.example: Language is the object the adjective points to.
items.exampleCN: 语言是这个形容词所指的对象。

items.example: A linguist works on sound, grammar or meaning.
items.exampleCN: 语言研究者研究声音、语法或意义。

items.example: Linguistics has its own methods and journals.
items.exampleCN: 语言学有自己的方法与期刊。

items.example: The two regions are linguistically close.
items.exampleCN: 这两个地区在语言上很接近。

items.example: Bilingual education began in the border counties.
items.exampleCN: 双语教育从边境各县开始。

items.example: A multilingual staff serves the port.
items.exampleCN: 一支多语员工队伍服务这个港口。

definition_zh: 应对；应付；处理；承受；勉强维持
definition_en: to deal with a difficulty, a load or a demand using the resources one has
core_image: 一个人顶着风把伞撑开，伞骨被吹得反折，他没有松手，而是侧过身换了个角度继续往前走
scene: 急诊走廊里，护士推着车穿过人群，墙上的排班表被临时改写了好几处。 The night team must cope with twice the usual number of arrivals.
sceneCN: 这里指承受并处理超出平常的工作量（第 2 个义项：应付繁重的任务或需求）；句意为夜班团队必须应对两倍于平常的接诊人数。图中可辨识物件：急诊推车、改写过的排班表、候诊椅、走廊指示牌。

pos.zh: 应对；应付（不及物动词短语加介词，后接困难、压力或任务）
承受；勉强维持（后接负荷、开支或局面）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加动名词词尾构成，义为「应对方式；应对的」
去掉介词后的核心动词，义为「应付；对付」
核心动词的过去式与过去分词形式
由动词加施事词尾构成，义为「能应付的人」，较少用

senses.title: Handle pressure
senses.definition: to keep functioning under strain without breaking down
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下仍能运转而不垮掉
senses.example: Students must cope with the strain of three examinations in one week.
senses.exampleCN: 学生必须应对一周三场考试带来的压力。
senses.why: The verb came from a word for exchanging blows; coping is holding one's ground in a contest, not winning it.
senses.whyCN: 核心动词出自表示「交手、对打」的词；应对就是在较量中站住，而不是取胜。

senses.title: Manage a heavy workload
senses.definition: to deal with more work or more demand than is usual
senses.definitionCN: 处理超出平常的工作量或需求
senses.example: The small office can cope with a sudden rise in applications.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小办事处能够应付申请量的突然上升。
senses.why: Coping is holding one's ground when the work arrives faster than usual.
senses.whyCN: 当工作来得比平常更快，撑住就是应对。

senses.title: Respond to a crisis
senses.definition: to act effectively when an emergency breaks
senses.definitionCN: 紧急状况发生时能有效行动
senses.example: The hospital may cope with a flood of casualties only if extra staff arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 只有增援人员到达，医院才可能应对大量伤员涌入。
senses.why: A crisis is a blow one meets with whatever hands are free.
senses.whyCN: 危机是用手里现有的人手迎上的一击。

senses.title: Adapt to change
senses.definition: to adjust one's methods to a new condition
senses.definitionCN: 调整做法以适应新的条件
senses.example: Older workers should cope with new software if the training is patient.
senses.exampleCN: 如果培训足够耐心，年长的员工应能适应新软件。
senses.why: Coping with change is turning sideways rather than letting go of the umbrella.
senses.whyCN: 应对变化，是侧过身，而不是松手丢伞。

senses.title: Live with illness or disability
senses.definition: to carry on daily life while managing a long-term condition
senses.definitionCN: 在长期病痛或残障下维持日常生活
senses.example: Families may cope with a long illness by sharing the care.
senses.exampleCN: 家庭可以通过分担照护来应对长期的病痛。
senses.why: A long illness is a long contest, and sharing the care is how a family keeps standing.
senses.whyCN: 长期病痛是一场长久的交手，分担照护是家庭继续站住的方式。

senses.title: Get by on limited money
senses.definition: to manage daily needs with very little income
senses.definitionCN: 以很少的收入维持日常所需
senses.example: A family can cope with a small budget if housing costs stay low.
senses.exampleCN: 如果住房开支不高，一个家庭可以靠小笔预算维持。
senses.why: A small budget is a load one carries by leaving things out, not by winning.
senses.whyCN: 小预算是一副靠舍弃来承担的担子，而不是靠取胜。

senses.title: Bear a mechanical load
senses.definition: to carry a physical load without failing
senses.definitionCN: 承受物理负荷而不失效
senses.example: The old dam must cope with the weight of water after heavy snow.
senses.exampleCN: 大雪之后，这座旧坝必须承受水的重量。
senses.why: The everyday sense of managing a burden extends naturally to structures that must hold under load.
senses.whyCN: 日常「承担重负」的意思，自然延伸到必须承压的结构上。

senses.title: Balance competing demands
senses.definition: to keep several parties satisfied enough to proceed
senses.definitionCN: 使多方各自得到起码的满足以便推进
senses.example: A chair must cope with members who want opposite things.
senses.exampleCN: 主持人必须应付想要相反结果的成员。
senses.why: A chair meets opposite demands by standing between them rather than over them.
senses.whyCN: 主持人站在相反诉求之间，而不是压在其上。

senses.title: Endure an emotional loss
senses.definition: to continue living after a loss without being overwhelmed
senses.definitionCN: 在失去之后继续生活而不被压垮
senses.example: Children may cope with grief better when routines are kept.
senses.exampleCN: 若日常节律得以保持，孩子可能更好地承受悲伤。
senses.why: Grief is a blow that cannot be avoided, only stood through.
senses.whyCN: 悲伤是一击无法躲开，只能撑过去。

intro.en: The phrase joins a verb that once meant to strike or to trade blows with a preposition of accompaniment. Coping is meeting a difficulty head on and continuing to stand.
intro.cn: 这个短语把曾经表示「打击、交手」的动词与表示「与、同」的介词结合起来。所谓应对，就是正面遇上困难，并且继续站住。

items.en: Kolaphos meant a blow or a cuff, especially one given with the fist.
items.cn: 这个词意为「一击、一巴掌」，尤指用拳头打。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as colaphus, still naming a blow.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个词，仍然表示「一击」。

items.en: French shortened it to coup, a stroke or a blow, and built the verb couper, to strike.
items.cn: 法语把它缩短为「一击、一记」，并造出「打击」的动词。

items.en: English took the verb for meeting an opponent in combat, and only later for meeting any difficulty.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入这个动词，指在战斗中迎击对手，后来才指迎接任何困难。

items.en: The frame with the preposition of accompaniment fixed in the nineteenth century for managing burdens, loads and losses. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 与伴随介词搭配的框架在十九世纪固定下来，用于应对负担、负荷与丧失。最早书证年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the blow word or looks close to it; the second group holds other verbs for dealing with a difficulty.
note.cn: 第一组共享「打击」之词或形近；第二组是其他表示「处理困难」的动词。

entries.definition: Used alone, it means to manage or to get by; the preposition is what brings the specific difficulty into the sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时意为「应付、过得去」；正是介词把具体的困难带进句子。

entries.definition: It names the way a person manages, as in a coping strategy; the phrase names the encounter itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指一个人应对的方式，如应对策略；短语指遭遇本身。

entries.definition: It still means a stroke or a sudden seizure of power; it shares the blow word but not the sense of endurance.
entries.definitionCN: 仍指「一击」或「突然夺取政权」；共享「打击」之词，却不含「撑住」之意。

entries.definition: It comes from a Latin word for abundance, not from the blow word; the resemblance is only in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 它出自拉丁语表示「充裕」的词，与「打击」之词无关，相似只在拼写。

entries.definition: The common phrase for taking action on a problem; it says nothing about whether one has enough resources.
entries.definitionCN: 处理问题的常用短语，不涉及是否有足够资源。

entries.definition: It stresses skill in managing a situation, often with a lighter tone than the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 强调处理局面的技巧，语气常比本短语轻松。

entries.definition: It stresses lasting through pain without any implication of managing the cause.
entries.definitionCN: 强调在痛苦中撑过去，不含「处理成因」之意。

entries.definition: It suggests close, difficult struggle with a problem, and is more vivid than the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示与问题近身缠斗，比本短语更形象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the umbrella in the wind, the rewritten rota, the dam after snow and the shared care.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用风中的伞、改写的排班表、雪后的坝与分担的照护四个场景。

normal.en: An umbrella bent backward by wind, held on and turned sideways.
normal.cn: 伞被风吹得反折，人没有松手，只是侧过身。

normal.en: A rota rewritten three times in one night.
normal.cn: 一张排班表，一夜之间改了三次。

normal.en: An old dam holding back meltwater after a heavy snow.
normal.cn: 大雪之后，旧坝拦住融水。

normal.en: Two sisters sharing the care of an ill parent.
normal.cn: 两姐妹分担照护生病的母亲。

normal.en: A child whose bedtime stays the same through a family upheaval.
normal.cn: 家里天翻地覆，孩子的睡觉时间却没变。

abstract.en: Coping is not solving: it is continuing while the problem continues.
abstract.cn: 应对不是解决：问题还在，人还在往前走。

abstract.en: The word began as trading blows, and it still carries the stance of a fighter who has not fallen.
abstract.cn: 这个词最初指交手，至今仍带着「没有倒下」的姿态。

abstract.en: Resources decide what coping looks like: the same difficulty needs a different answer in a rich room and a poor one.
abstract.cn: 资源决定应对的模样：同一个困难，在富裕的屋里与拮据的屋里需要不同答案。

examples.en: Small firms must cope with delays that larger rivals can absorb.
examples.cn: 小公司必须应对大对手能吸收掉的延误。

examples.en: Coastal towns may cope with a rise in sea level only with new defences.
examples.cn: 沿海城镇只有建起新防线，才可能应对海平面上升。

examples.en: A bridge designed for horses must cope with modern truck traffic.
examples.cn: 为马车设计的桥，必须承受现代卡车的通行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「寇普 威兹」：把「交手」记成顶着风撑伞不肯松手——风还在，人还站着，这就是应对

root: 核心动词出自希腊语表示「一击、一拳」的词，经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，本义是「打击、交手」，后引申为「迎上困难并撑住」。介词为本族常用词，意为「与、同」。短语整体强调用现有资源继续对付，而不保证解决。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses meet a load and keep going: pressure, workload, crisis, change, illness, a small budget, a physical load, competing demands, and grief.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都是遇上一个负荷并继续前行：压力、工作量、危机、变化、疾病、小预算、物理负荷、相互冲突的诉求与悲伤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person holding an umbrella that the wind has bent backward, turning sideways rather than letting go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人撑着被风吹反的伞，侧过身继续走，而不是松手。

branches.en: THE INNER LOAD: exam strain and grief are carried without visible machinery.
branches.cn: 内在负荷：考试压力与悲伤在没有可见器械的情况下被承住。

branches.en: THE SUDDEN SURGE: an office absorbs extra applications, a hospital absorbs casualties.
branches.cn: 骤增：办事处吸收额外申请，医院吸收大量伤员。

branches.en: THE ADJUSTED STANCE: new software, opposite demands, a chair turning sideways.
branches.cn: 调整姿态：新软件、相反诉求，主持人侧身应对。

branches.en: THE LONG HAUL: shared care and a tight budget are managed day after day.
branches.cn: 长期支撑：分担照护与紧张预算，一天一天地维持。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL LOAD: a dam or a bridge must hold under weight.
branches.cn: 物理负荷：坝或桥必须在重量下撑住。

intro.en: The family is small and verbal; it grew from a word for a blow, and the endings name the manner and the person rather than a Latin technical vocabulary.
intro.cn: 这个词族人少且以动词为主；它从表示「一击」的词长成，词尾命名方式与人，而不是拉丁技术词汇。

latinIntro.en: Greek and Latin both supplied the blow word, French reshaped it, and English added its own endings.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语与拉丁语都提供了「打击」之词，法语加以改写，英语再加上自己的词尾。

definition_zh: n. 痢疾；细菌性痢疾；阿米巴痢疾
definition_en: an infection of the intestines that causes severe diarrhoea with blood and mucus, spread mainly through contaminated food and water
core_image: 野战医院病历卡上一天十几次带血黏液的腹泻记录；被洪水淹过的井边压水泵贴着「煮沸再饮」的告示；显微镜载玻片上一个圆形细胞里裹着红细胞；村口隔离棚的石灰线
scene: 野战医院的病历卡上记着一天十几次带血黏液的腹泻，医生在诊断栏写下病名，笔尖在纸上顿了一下。 The camp was hit by an outbreak of dysentery.
sceneCN: 这里 dysentery 指「引起带血黏液腹泻的肠道感染」（第 1 个义项：痢疾）；句意是营地暴发了痢疾。图中可辨识物件：病历卡、诊断栏、医生的笔尖。

pos.zh: 痢疾；细菌性痢疾；阿米巴痢疾

senses.title: An intestinal infection
senses.definition: an infection of the intestines causing severe diarrhoea with blood and mucus
senses.definitionCN: （名词）引起带血与黏液的重度腹泻的肠道感染
senses.example: The camp was hit by an outbreak of dysentery.
senses.exampleCN: 营地暴发了痢疾。

senses.whyCN: 一张野战医院病历卡把一天十二次带血排便划成正字计数。

senses.title: The bacillary form

senses.definitionCN: （名词）由细菌引起、经污染食物与水传播的类型
senses.example: Bacillary dysentery spread through the village after the well was flooded.
senses.exampleCN: 井水被淹之后，细菌性痢疾在村里蔓延开来。
senses.why: A hand pump beside a flooded latrine with a notice telling people to boil every cup.
senses.whyCN: 被淹的厕所旁有一台压水泵，告示上写着每一杯都要煮沸。

senses.title: The amoebic form
senses.definition: the form caused by an amoeba, often lasting longer and returning
senses.definitionCN: （名词）由阿米巴原虫引起、往往迁延更久且易复发的类型
senses.example: Amoebic dysentery kept returning until the parasite was finally cleared.
senses.exampleCN: 阿米巴痢疾反复发作，直到原虫被彻底清除。
senses.why: A microscope slide shows a round cell with a swallowed red blood cell inside it.

intro.en: Dysentery is Greek dys- meaning bad plus enteron meaning intestine; the same enteron gives enteric and enteritis, so the whole family names the gut and what goes wrong in it.
intro.cn: dysentery 由希腊语 dys-（坏）加 enteron（肠）构成；同一个 enteron 给出 enteric 与 enteritis，所以整个词族都在指称肠以及肠里出的问题。

items.en: The Greek prefix dys- means bad or difficult.
items.cn: 希腊语前缀 dys- 意为坏、困难。

items.en: Greek enteron means intestine, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: 希腊语 enteron 意为肠，是整个词族的词根。

items.en: Greek dysenteria joined the two parts into a name for the illness.
items.cn: 希腊语 dysenteria 把两部分合成病名。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek term unchanged for medical writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样借入这个希腊词，用于医学著述。

items.en: Middle English took the word from Latin and Old French.
items.cn: 中古英语从拉丁语与古法语吸收了这个词。

items.en: Medicine separated the bacillary form from the amoebic form.
items.cn: 医学把细菌性与阿米巴性两种痢疾区分开来。

note.en: Dysentery shares the prefix dys- with dysfunction and dyspepsia, and the root enter- with enteric and enteritis; its neighbours name other gut illnesses.
note.cn: dysentery 与 dysfunction、dyspepsia 共用前缀 dys-，与 enteric、enteritis 共用词根 enter-；它的近义词则指称其他肠道疾病。

dict_mnemonic.text: dysentery ＝ dys-（坏、困难）＋ enter-（肠，希腊语 enteron）＋ -ia（疾病）＝「肠子出了坏毛病」。记住 enter- 就记住一串：enteric 肠的、enteritis 肠炎、gastroenteritis 胃肠炎（gastr- 胃）。dys- 家族还有 dysfunction 功能障碍、dyspepsia 消化不良、dyslexia 读写困难。临床上分两型：bacillary dysentery 细菌性（志贺菌，经污染食物与水传播），amoebic dysentery 阿米巴性（原虫，病程更长易复发）。关键特征是带血与黏液的腹泻，普通 diarrhoea 只是稀便，未必带血。

root: 希腊语 dys-（坏）＋ enteron（肠）→ dysenteria → 拉丁语 dysenteria → dysentery（痢疾）

definition_zh: 巢；窝；（鸟、昆虫等的）巢穴；一窝（雏鸟、卵）；筑巢；嵌套；窝藏
definition_en: a structure built or hollowed out by an animal for laying eggs and raising young
core_image: 树杈间一只用泥与草茎抹成的碗，内壁被压得光滑，四枚带斑点的卵并排躺在正中
scene: 孩子在谷仓梁上发现了一个旧巢，里面还留着去年的一片蛋壳。 A sparrow's nest sat wedged against the beam, three eggs warm inside it.
sceneCN: 这里 nest 指「鸟巢、窝」（第 1 个义项：动物为产卵育雏而筑的结构）；句意为一只麻雀的巢卡在梁边，里面三枚卵还是温的；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 巢；窝；巢穴；一窝（卵或雏）
筑巢；巢居；嵌套；层层套放

senses.title: A structure built to hold eggs
senses.titleCN: 为盛放卵而筑成的结构
senses.definition: a structure of twigs, mud, grass or other material in which a bird lays and incubates eggs
senses.definitionCN: 用树枝、泥、草等材料筑成、鸟在其中产卵与孵卵的结构
senses.example: A sparrow's nest sat wedged against the beam.
senses.exampleCN: 一只麻雀的巢卡在梁边。
senses.why: the core sense is simply the object, because everything else the word names is derived from this built container.
senses.whyCN: 核心义就是这件物体，因为这个词命名的其它一切都是由这个容器引申出来的。

senses.title: The home of a whole brood
senses.definition: the place where a brood is reared, viewed as the young family's home
senses.definitionCN: 一窝雏被养育之处，被看作这个幼小家庭的家
senses.example: The whole nest begged whenever the adult landed.
senses.exampleCN: 成鸟一落下，整窝雏鸟都乞食。
senses.why: the container and its occupants merge, so nest may name the family inside as much as the structure.
senses.whyCN: 容器与其居住者合并，因此 nest 既可指结构，也可指里面的全家。

senses.title: A clutch counted as one unit
senses.definition: the set of eggs laid in one nest and incubated together
senses.definitionCN: 在同一巢中产出并一起孵化的一组卵
senses.example: Rangers recorded a nest of four eggs under the lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 巡护员在灯下记录到一窝四枚卵。
senses.why: counting by nests is convenient because the nest defines the set, so the container becomes the unit of number.
senses.whyCN: 以巢计数很方便，因为巢定义了这一组，容器于是成了计数单位。

senses.title: A hollow made by another animal
senses.titleCN: 由其它动物挖出的巢穴
senses.definition: a burrow, hole or cavity used by an insect, mammal or fish for young
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫、哺乳动物或鱼为育幼而使用的洞、穴或腔
senses.example: Wasps build a paper nest under the roof tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 黄蜂在屋瓦下筑成纸质的巢。
senses.why: once the word is applied beyond birds, the structure stops being woven and becomes any prepared cavity.
senses.whyCN: 一旦越出鸟类，这个结构就不再是编织的，而成为任何备好的腔室。

senses.title: To build and occupy a nest
senses.definition: to build a nest and use it for breeding
senses.definitionCN: 建造巢并将其用于繁殖
senses.example: Swallows nest every year in the same corner of the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 燕子每年都在谷仓同一个角落筑巢。
senses.why: the verb is simply the noun turned into an action, so it means to do what the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词转为动作，意为做出名词所指的那件事。

senses.title: To place one thing inside another
senses.titleCN: 把一物套进另一物内部
senses.definition: to fit objects or structures one inside another, as boxes or data tables
senses.definitionCN: 把物件或结构放进彼此内部，如盒子或数据表
senses.example: Nest the smaller boxes inside the larger crate.
senses.exampleCN: 把小盒子套进大板条箱里。
senses.why: the technical sense generalizes the shape of the bird's cup: something held within something else.
senses.whyCN: 技术义把鸟巢的形状一般化：一物被另一物容纳在其中。

senses.title: A graduated set that fits inside itself
senses.titleCN: 可以逐层套放的一组器物
senses.definition: a set of similar objects of decreasing size that store one inside another, as a nest of tables
senses.definitionCN: 一组大小递减、可以互相套放的同类物件，如套几
senses.example: The nest of tables slotted under the largest one.
senses.exampleCN: 套几收进最大的那张下面。
senses.why: the noun is applied to objects that imitate the containment of a nest, so the name follows the shape rather than the bird.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词被用于模仿「巢的容纳关系」的物件，因此名称追随形状而非鸟。

senses.title: A den of troublesome people or things
senses.titleCN: 滋生麻烦的人或事物之处
senses.definition: a place or group seen as a breeding ground for something harmful, as in a nest of thieves
senses.definitionCN: 被视为有害之物滋生地的场所或群体，如贼窝
senses.example: The yard had become a nest of infection after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水之后这个院子成了感染滋生地。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only the idea of a sheltered place where something grows, and that something is no longer young.
senses.whyCN: 比喻只保留「有遮蔽之处、某种东西在其中生长」的意思，而生长之物已不再是幼鸟。

intro.en: Nest is an Old English word, nest, with the same form in several old Germanic languages; its relation to Latin nidus is debated rather than settled.
intro.cn: nest 是古英语词 nest，在数种古老日耳曼语中形式相同；它与拉丁 nidus 的关系属争议，未有定论。

items.en: Old English nest named both the structure and the brood in it, and the word has kept that double reach.
items.cn: 古英语 nest 既指结构，也指其中的一窝，这双重范围一直保留。

items.en: Old Norse nest, Old High German nest and Middle Dutch nest show a common Germanic stock, so Latin borrowing is unlikely.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 nest、古高地德语 nest、中古荷兰语 nest 表明共同的日耳曼来源，因此不太可能是拉丁借词。

items.en: Latin nidus 'nest' looks similar and means the same, but most handbooks treat the resemblance as parallel; a shared Indo-European source is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 拉丁 nidus「巢」形似义同，但多数辞书把这种相似视为平行；共有印欧来源属重构形式。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): the pre-Germanic shape of nest is unresolved; the root commonly printed for it is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：nest 在日耳曼语之前的形式无定论；常印出的词根是重构形式，并非有证材料。

items.en: The verb nest appeared later, formed directly from the noun, and was extended to any placing of one thing inside another.
items.cn: 动词 nest 出现较晚，直接由名词构成，并被扩展到任何把一物放进另一物的动作。

items.en: Phrases such as empty nest and nest egg carried the word into family life and household finance.
items.cn: empty nest、nest egg 等短语把这个词带进家庭生活与家庭理财。

note.en: Group one separates the near-synonyms for animal homes; group two separates the words built on nest itself.
note.cn: 第一组区分表示动物居所近义词；第二组区分由 nest 本身构成的词。

entries.definition: The -ing form names the building and sitting; the bare nest names the object.
entries.definitionCN: -ing 形式指建与伏的行为；原形 nest 指物件。

entries.definition: A nestling is a chick too young to leave; it is the content of the nest, not the nest.
entries.definitionCN: nestling 是尚不能离巢的雏鸟，是巢中之物，而非巢。

entries.definition: A nester is the bird regarded as the one that nests, marked by -er.
entries.definitionCN: nester 是把鸟看作筑巢者，由 -er 标记。

entries.definition: Nested describes something already placed inside another; it is a state, not a place.
entries.definitionCN: nested 描述已被放进另一物之中的状态，是状态而非地点。

entries.definition: A burrow is dug into earth or sand; a nest may be built on a branch or in a hole.
entries.definitionCN: burrow 掘入土或沙；巢可能筑在枝上或洞里。

entries.definition: A den is a mammal's shelter, often a cave or hollow, and usually not built from gathered material.
entries.definitionCN: den 是哺乳动物的居所，常为洞穴，通常不由采集材料筑成。

entries.definition: A lair is where a wild animal rests, especially a predator; it carries no idea of eggs.
entries.definitionCN: lair 是野兽尤其捕食者歇息之处，不含产卵之意。

entries.definition: A hive is the home of a bee colony, a special case of an insect nest with a fixed architecture.
entries.definitionCN: hive 是蜂群的家，是昆虫巢的一种特例，结构固定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Germanic relatives, real compounds and real idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的日耳曼同族词、真实复合词与真实习语。

normal.en: The Germanic relatives are Old Norse nest and Old High German nest, not Latin words.
normal.cn: 日耳曼同族词是古诺斯语 nest 与古高地德语 nest，而非拉丁词。

normal.en: The family runs nest, nesting, nester, nestling, nested, nest box.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 nest、nesting、nester、nestling、nested、nest box。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: build a nest, leave the nest, nest of eggs.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：筑巢、离巢、一窝蛋。

normal.en: The idioms empty nest and nest egg show the word applied to family and savings.
normal.cn: 习语 empty nest 与 nest egg 显示这个词被用于家庭与储蓄。

normal.en: In computing, nest means to place one structure inside another.
normal.cn: 在计算机中，nest 指把一种结构放进另一种。

abstract.en: Picture a cup so exactly shaped that the sitter's body closes its opening.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗形制精准，伏者的身体正好封住开口。

abstract.en: Picture a house whose walls keep growing back after each departure.
abstract.cn: 想象一座屋子，每次有人离开后墙壁又重新长回。

abstract.en: Picture a set of bowls where the smallest is invisible until lifted out.
abstract.cn: 想象一套碗，最小的一只不被提起就看不见。

examples.en: The nest was rebuilt on the same branch after the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴过后，巢又在同一根枝上重建。

examples.en: She found an old nest in the rafters, empty and crumbling.
examples.cn: 她在椽子上发现一只空了的旧巢，正在崩解。

examples.en: Programmers nest these records inside a parent object.
examples.cn: 程序员把这些记录嵌进一个父对象里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nest（巢）」——树枝围成碗，卵卧其中 → 巢、窝；动作义为筑巢、套住

root: 古英语 nest「巢；一窝」，与古诺斯语、古高地德语、中古荷兰语 nest 同出日耳曼共有词；与拉丁 nidus「巢」形似义同，通常视为平行构词，共有印欧来源仅为重构形式，日耳曼以前词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape: a built cup holds something precious, and the word then names the occupants, the count, a prepared cavity, a den of trouble, the act of building, any placing of one thing inside another, and finally a set of objects made to slot together.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个形状展开：一只编成的碗托住贵重之物，词语随后指其居住者、计数单位、备好的腔室、滋生麻烦的窝、建造动作、任何把一物放进另一物的动作，最后指一组可以互相套放的器物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup woven at the branch fork, its inner walls smoothed by the body inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：枝杈分叉处编成的碗，内壁被其中的身体压得光滑。

branches.en: CUP AND FAMILY: the container and the family in it are named by the same word.
branches.cn: 碗与家庭：容器与其中的家庭由同一个词命名。

branches.en: COUNTED SET: the nest defines the clutch, so the container becomes the unit.
branches.cn: 可数的组：巢定义了这一窝，容器于是成了单位。

branches.en: A SHELTERED PLACE: any animal's cavity, and a den where trouble breeds.
branches.cn: 有遮蔽之处：任何动物的腔室，以及滋生麻烦的窝。

branches.en: DOING THE NOUN: the verb is the noun turned into an act.
branches.cn: 做名词所指的事：动词就是名词转为动作。

branches.en: SHAPE EXPORTED: a rule for holding one thing inside another, and objects made to nest.
branches.cn: 形状外输：一条「一物容另一物」的规则，以及照此造出的套叠器物。

intro.en: Nest is a bare Germanic root that takes English suffixes and compounds; it has no Latin prefix structure.
intro.cn: nest 是裸露的日耳曼词根，只接英语后缀与复合成分，没有拉丁前缀结构。

latinIntro.en: Nest itself has no Latin element; the Latin entries are the learned equivalents English borrowed separately for the same content.
latinIntro.cn: nest 本身不含拉丁成分；下列拉丁条目是英语为同一内容另行借入的学术词。

items.example: The nest held four eggs.
items.exampleCN: 巢里有四枚卵。

items.example: Nesting lasts about three weeks.
items.exampleCN: 筑巢期约持续三周。

items.example: Cavity nesters need old trees.
items.exampleCN: 洞穴筑巢者需要老树。

items.example: Nestlings cannot fly yet.
items.exampleCN: 雏鸟还不会飞。

items.example: The lists are nested.
items.exampleCN: 这些列表是嵌套的。

items.example: They used the bonus as a nest egg.
items.exampleCN: 他们把奖金当作储备金。

items.meaning: a home after the children leave
items.example: The empty nest felt too quiet.
items.exampleCN: 空巢显得太安静。

items.example: Volunteers hung forty nest boxes.
items.exampleCN: 志愿者挂上了四十只巢箱。

items.example: The ruling stirred a hornet's nest.
items.exampleCN: 这项裁定捅了马蜂窝。

definition_zh: 罪犯；违法者；违规者；冒犯他人的人；惹人反感的人；（事故或问题的）罪魁祸首
definition_en: a person who commits a crime or breaks a rule, or who gives offence to others; also the thing chiefly responsible for a problem
core_image: 一个人抬脚跨过地上那道白线，鞋底已经落在禁止的一侧，身上还别着写有名字的牌子
scene: 小区业主会上，大家讨论那位总把垃圾倒进邻家院子的住户，一致认为他是破坏规矩的人。 At the residents' meeting the neighbours agreed that the man who kept dumping rubbish over the fence was an offender.
sceneCN: 这里指「违反规矩、触犯他人的人」，对应第 1 个义项：实施了违法或违规行为的人；句意为业主会上邻居们认定那个反复往邻家院子倒垃圾的人就是破坏规矩者。画面要点：越过白线的脚、写有名字的牌子、倒在界外的垃圾。

pos.zh: 罪犯；违法者；违规者（可数，法律与日常通用）
冒犯者；惹人反感的人（由动词「触怒」加施事后缀而来）
罪魁祸首；主要祸源（可指事物，常用于环境、事故话题）

derivatives.zh: 去掉施事后缀后的动词原形，承拉丁 offendere「撞上、触犯」→ 由「撞到某物」转为「得罪人、违犯法度」
加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表行为或状态）→ 由「触犯」这一动作转为「所犯之事、违法行为」
美式拼写，同样来自名词后缀（拉丁语中表状态的词尾） → 由动作转为「罪错、犯规」，并引申出「进攻」义
加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向或性质）→ 由「触犯」转为「带有冒犯性的、令人不快的」
加否定前缀于 offensive → 由「会冒犯人」转为「不惹人反感的、无害的」

senses.title: A person who commits a crime
senses.definition: a person who has committed a crime, especially one identified in legal or police records
senses.definitionCN: 实施了犯罪行为的人，尤指被法律或警方记录在案者
senses.example: At the residents' meeting the neighbours agreed that the man who kept dumping rubbish over the fence was an offender.
senses.exampleCN: 业主会上，邻居们认定那个反复往邻家院子倒垃圾的人就是违法者。
senses.why: The Latin verb offendere meant 'to strike against' something, and -er names the one who does it; a criminal is literally the person who has struck against the line the law drew.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 offendere 意为「撞上某物」，这个后缀指做出该动作的人；罪犯字面上就是撞到法律所画那道线的人。

senses.title: A person who breaks a rule, not a law
senses.titleCN: 违反规章而非法律的人
senses.definition: a person who contravenes the rules of an institution, sport or workplace without necessarily committing a crime
senses.definitionCN: 违反机构、运动或工作场所规章的人，未必构成犯罪
senses.example: A student who copies another's essay is an offender under the school's honesty code.
senses.exampleCN: 抄袭他人文章的学生，按学校诚信守则属于违规者。
senses.why: The line crossed need not be a statute; any drawn boundary, from a school code to a game's rules, produces an offender when someone steps over it.
senses.whyCN: 被越过的那条线不必是成文法；从校规到比赛规则，只要有人踩过任何画出的界线，就产生一个违规者。

senses.title: A person who gives offence by words
senses.definition: a person whose remarks or behaviour wound or insult someone
senses.definitionCN: 因言语或举止刺伤、侮辱他人而冒犯对方的人
senses.example: His jokes made him an offender in the eyes of the older guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他的玩笑使他在年长宾客眼中成了冒犯者。
senses.why: To offend was also to strike someone's feelings; the same -er suffix turns that blow into a person, so offence is no longer a line on the ground but a wound in another mind.
senses.whyCN: offend 也有「击伤他人感受」之义；同一个施事后缀把这一击落回到人身上，冒犯便从地上的线变成他人心里的伤。

senses.title: A person who disgusts or annoys
senses.definition: a person who is widely regarded as unpleasant or troublesome
senses.definitionCN: 被众人视为讨厌、惹麻烦的人
senses.example: In the office he was the offender whom nobody wanted to sit beside.
senses.exampleCN: 在办公室里，他是那个谁都不愿挨着坐的讨厌鬼。
senses.why: The physical core survives as social discomfort: the one who keeps bumping into other people's comfort is felt as an offender even when no rule is written.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的核心意象转为社交不适：总撞到别人舒适区的人，即使没有明文规定，也会被感觉成冒犯者。

senses.title: The chief source of a problem
senses.definition: the thing most responsible for a fault, a pollution or an accident
senses.definitionCN: 对某一缺陷、污染或事故负主要责任的事物
senses.example: Plastic packaging is the biggest offender in household waste.
senses.exampleCN: 塑料包装是生活垃圾中最大的祸源。
senses.why: Once the label applies to causes rather than persons, the guilty party can be a material; what 'strikes against' cleanliness takes the role of the offender.
senses.whyCN: 当这一标签从人转向原因，肇事者可以是某种材料；撞向洁净之物的东西便顶上了祸源的角色。

senses.title: A player who commits a foul
senses.definition: an athlete who commits an illegal move and is penalised by the referee
senses.definitionCN: 做出违规动作并被裁判处罚的运动员
senses.example: The referee sent the offender to the bench for two minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判把犯规者罚到替补席上坐两分钟。
senses.why: A playing field is the clearest case of a line drawn on the ground, so the sports sense keeps the original picture almost unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 球场是最典型的「在地上画线」的场合，因此体育义几乎原封不动地保留了最初的画面。

senses.title: The person named in a charge
senses.titleCN: 指控文书中被点名的一方
senses.definition: the person identified in a legal charge before any finding of guilt
senses.definitionCN: 在尚未判定有罪之前，被法律指控文书点名的人
senses.example: The report names the alleged offender but protects the victim.
senses.exampleCN: 报道点出了被指控者，却保护了受害者的身份。
senses.why: Legal drafting needs a neutral noun for the party on the wrong side of the line; offender supplies it without yet asserting guilt.
senses.whyCN: 法律文书需要一个中性名词来称呼站在界线错侧的一方，offender 正好提供这一称呼，同时并不预先断定有罪。

senses.title: One who breaks a moral or sacred law
senses.titleCN: 违背道德或神圣律法的人
senses.definition: a person who transgresses a moral, religious or conscience-bound standard
senses.definitionCN: 违背道德、宗教或良心准则的人
senses.example: In the old sermon he was called an offender against heaven itself.
senses.exampleCN: 在那篇古老的布道中，他被称为连上天都敢触犯的人。
senses.why: The line can be drawn by God rather than by a state; the oldest use of offendere in religious writing already meant to stumble against a sacred order.
senses.whyCN: 这条线也可以由神明而非国家来画；offendere 在宗教文献里最早的用法本就指撞向神圣秩序而失足。

intro.en: Offender is English offend plus the agent suffix -er. Offend came through Old French from Latin offendere 'to strike against, stumble', a compound of ob- 'against' and a verb of striking. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: offender 是英语动词 offend 加施事后缀构成。offend 经古法语来自拉丁 offendere「撞上、失足」，由表「对着」的前缀与一个表「撞击」的动词复合而成。年代均为约数。

items.en: The prefix ob- meant 'toward, against, in the way of', and it marks the direction of a collision rather than its cause.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为「朝向、对着、挡在路上」，它标出撞击的方向，而非撞击的成因。

items.en: Offendere meant 'to strike against, hit, stumble', and by extension 'to commit a fault'; it was built from ob- plus a verb of striking.
items.cn: offendere 意为「撞上、击中、失足」，引申为「犯过错」；由一个表「对着」的前缀加一个表撞击的动词构成。

items.en: The participle offensa 'a striking against' supplied the noun for a fault, the ancestor of English offence and offense.
items.cn: 分词形式 offensa 意为「撞上」，提供表示过错的名词，是英语 offence 与 offense 的前身。

items.en: Old French took the verb as offendre and passed it to English in the fourteenth century with the sense 'to commit a sin or fault'.
items.cn: 古法语把该动词作 offendre 吸收，并于十四世纪传给英语，当时意为「犯下罪过或过失」。

items.en: Adding -er to the verb produced offender, first for a sinner before a court of law, then for any person who breaks a rule.
items.cn: 在动词后加施事后缀构成 offender，最初指在法庭上被审的罪人，后泛指任何破坏规则的人。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century statutes fixed phrases such as repeat offender and young offender, while environmental writing extended the word to things.
items.cn: 十九、二十世纪的法条固定了「惯犯」「未成年犯」等说法，环境类写作又把该词扩展到事物身上。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb of striking and shows how far its family spread; the second group offers near alternatives for a person who does wrong.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表「撞击」的拉丁动词，可见其词族分布之广；第二组是「做错事的人」的近义替代。

entries.definition: To break a law or to hurt someone's feelings; it is the verb from which the person-noun is built.
entries.definitionCN: 违反法律或伤害他人感情；它是派生人称名词所依托的动词。

entries.definition: The act of breaking a law or the feeling of being insulted; it names the deed, not the doer.
entries.definitionCN: 违法或冒犯的行为，也指被冒犯的感受；它指行为，不指行为人。

entries.definition: Causing resentment, or a military attack; the root idea of striking survives in both uses.
entries.definitionCN: 令人反感的，或指军事进攻；「撞击」的词根义在两种用法中都还在。

entries.definition: The party accused in a court case; it is built on defendere 'to ward off', the mirror image of striking against.
entries.definitionCN: 法庭上被指控的一方；由 defendere「挡开」构成，正是「撞上去」的镜像动作。

entries.definition: A person convicted of a crime; it states a legal category, while offender can merely name someone who broke a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 被判定有罪的人；它给出法律类别，而 offender 也可以只指破坏规则者。

entries.definition: The person responsible for a fault or mishap; it stresses blame rather than legal breach.
entries.definitionCN: 对过失或事故负有责任的人；它强调该受责怪，而非法律上的违犯。

entries.definition: A person who does something morally wrong; the judgement is ethical, not statutory.
entries.definitionCN: 做了道德上错事的人；其判断是伦理性的，而非法条性的。

entries.definition: A person who steps beyond a set limit or command; it keeps the image of crossing a line but sounds formal.
entries.definitionCN: 越过既定界限或命令的人；它保留「越过界线」的意象，但语体正式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real agent suffix and the real fixed phrases of law and sport.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的施事后缀，以及法律与体育中的真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Offendere is 'to strike against'; add -er and you have the one who strikes against the line.
normal.cn: offendere 意为「撞上去」；加上施事后缀就是那个撞向界线的人。

normal.en: The ob- in offend means 'against', the same direction seen in oppose and object.
normal.cn: offend 中那个表「对着」的前缀意为「对着」，与 oppose、object 中的方向感相同。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort people by repetition: first-time offender, repeat offender, habitual offender.
normal.cn: 固定搭配按次数给人分类：初犯、屡犯、习惯性违法者。

normal.en: Offence is the deed, offender is the doer, offensive is the quality: one root, three jobs.
normal.cn: offence 是事，offender 是人，offensive 是性质：一个词根，三种职务。

normal.en: In sport the offender is simply the player who crossed the line the referee watches.
normal.cn: 在体育中，犯规者就是那个越过裁判所盯那条线的球员。

abstract.en: Picture a chalk line on a pavement and a shoe sole landing just past it, the dust still rising.
abstract.cn: 想象人行道上一条粉笔线，一只鞋底刚落到线外，尘土还未落下。

abstract.en: Picture a name tag pinned on a coat before the wearer has even entered the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚名牌在本人还没进屋之前就已别在了外套上。

abstract.en: Picture a broken fence with a single footprint on the forbidden side of the grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一段破损的栅栏，草地禁入的一侧只有一个脚印。

examples.en: The police recorded the offender's fingerprints and released him pending trial.
examples.cn: 警方录下该罪犯的指纹，随后在候审期间将其释放。

examples.en: Any offender caught smuggling will lose the licence for good.
examples.cn: 任何被查获走私的违法者都将永久失去执照。

examples.en: The report calls the city's ageing sewers the main offender in the flooding.
examples.cn: 报告称城中老化的下水道是此次内涝的主要祸源。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，犯的」——哦，这事原来是他犯下的：跨过界线、犯下过错的那个人 → 罪犯、违规者

root: 拉丁语表「对着」的前缀 + 表撞击的词干 → offendere「撞上、失足、犯过」→ 古法语 offendre → 英语 offend；加表施事者的后缀 → offender，即「撞到界线上的那个人」；同族有 offence、offense、offensive、defendant。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses start from one picture: a person stepping over a drawn line. The line may be a statute, a school code, someone's feelings, a game's rules, a charge sheet or a sacred order; whenever it is crossed, the one who crossed it is the offender.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都始于同一幅画面：一个人跨过画好的线。这条线可以是成文法、校规、他人的感受、比赛规则、指控文书或神圣秩序；只要有线被越过，越线者就是 offender。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person whose shoe has just landed on the forbidden side of a chalk line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人的鞋底刚落在粉笔线外的那一侧。

branches.en: STATUTE: the line is a law, and the one who crosses it is a criminal in the eyes of the court.
branches.cn: 成文法：线是法律，越线者在法庭眼中即罪犯。

branches.en: RULES OF PLAY: school codes and referees' whistles draw thinner lines, yet crossing them still makes an offender.
branches.cn: 游戏规则：校规与裁判的哨声画出更细的线，越过它们同样成为违规者。

branches.en: SOCIAL WOUND: the line becomes another person's comfort, and the one who keeps bumping it is felt as offensive.
branches.cn: 社交伤害：线变成他人的舒适边界，反复撞上去的人便被视为冒犯者。

branches.en: BLAME SHIFTED: when the guilty party is a material or a practice, the word lends its blame to things.
branches.cn: 归责转移：当肇事者是材料或做法时，这个词把自己的责难借给了事物。

branches.en: FORMAL AND SACRED LABELS: legal drafting and religious language keep the noun for the party on the wrong side, before or beyond any trial.
branches.cn: 正式与神圣标签：法律文书与宗教语言把这个名词留给站在错侧的一方，无论审前还是超越审判。

intro.en: Offender is a transparent English build: a Latin verb of striking plus the agent suffix -er, with older relatives showing the same prefix at work.
intro.cn: offender 的构造清楚可拆：一个表「撞击」的拉丁动词，加上施事后缀；更早的同族词展示了同一前缀的作用。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around offendere includes offensa, offensio and the verb itself; the prefix ob- also appears in object and oppose.
latinIntro.cn: offendere 周围的拉丁词族包括 offensa、offensio 与动词本身；这个前缀也见于 object 与 oppose。

items.example: The prefix turns a neutral motion into a collision.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把中性的移动变成了撞击。

items.meaning: to strike against; to commit a fault
items.example: Loud remarks may offend a listener.
items.exampleCN: 大声的评论可能冒犯听者。

items.meaning: a person or thing that performs the action
items.example: The suffix is added straight to the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀直接加在动词词干之后。

items.meaning: a person who breaks a law or rule
items.example: The offender was charged the next morning.
items.exampleCN: 该违法者第二天早上被起诉。

items.meaning: several people who break the same line
items.example: Young offenders receive separate treatment.
items.exampleCN: 未成年犯会受到另行处理。

items.meaning: the act of breaking a law; a feeling of hurt
items.meaningCN: 违法行为；被冒犯的感受
items.example: Driving without a licence is an offence.
items.exampleCN: 无照驾驶是一项违法行为。

items.meaningCN: 引人反感的；用于进攻的
items.example: The poster used offensive language.
items.exampleCN: 那张海报用了冒犯性语言。

items.example: He kept the talk inoffensive.
items.exampleCN: 他让谈话保持在无害的范围。

items.example: The defendant denied the charge.
items.exampleCN: 被告否认了指控。

items.example: The team took a defensive stance.
items.exampleCN: 该队采取了防守姿态。

latinEntries.meaning: to strike against; to stumble; to commit a fault

definition_zh: 运行的；运营的；可投入使用的；操作层面的；（军事）作战的
definition_en: relating to the way something works in practice, or to the activities and costs of running an organization or machine
core_image: 一条生产线正在运转，指示灯全绿，工人各就各位，没有一处停着等修。
scene: 项目经理说系统已经通过测试，下周可以交给值班团队试用。 The system will be operational next week.
sceneCN: 这里 operational 是“已具备运行条件、可投入使用”（第 2 个义项）；句意：系统下周就可以投入运行；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 运行的；运营的；可投入使用的；操作层面的；（军事）作战的

senses.title: Relating to how it runs
senses.titleCN: 运行上的：与机器怎么转有关
senses.definition: relating to the working of a machine, system, or process
senses.definitionCN: 与机器、系统或流程如何运转有关
senses.example: The engineers separated design problems from operational problems.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把设计问题与运行问题分开处理。
senses.why: The suffix -al points to a domain: what happens while the thing is running, as distinct from how it was designed.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 指向一个领域：事物运转时发生的事，与它如何被设计区分开来。

senses.title: Ready to be used
senses.titleCN: 可投入使用：不是图纸，是能跑的
senses.definition: in a state of being able to work or be used as intended
senses.definitionCN: 处于能够按预期工作或使用的状态
senses.example: The new control tower is operational after two years of testing.
senses.exampleCN: 新控制塔经过两年测试后已可投入使用。
senses.why: Here the word answers a readiness question: the thing is not merely complete on paper, it can actually perform its function.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词回答的是“就绪”问题：事物不只在纸面上完成，它真能履行职责。

senses.title: The cost of keeping it running
senses.titleCN: 运营成本：让它每天转起来的钱
senses.definition: describing the expenses of running an organization or facility rather than building it
senses.definitionCN: 指维持组织或设施日常运转的开支，而非建设开支
senses.example: Operational costs rose with fuel and staff wages.
senses.exampleCN: 运营成本随燃料与员工工资上涨。
senses.why: Budgets split capital from operation: one pays to build, the other pays to keep the thing alive each day.
senses.whyCN: 预算把资本支出与运营支出分开：一笔付建设，另一笔付让它每天活下去。

senses.title: Defined by what you do
senses.titleCN: 操作定义：用做法代替概念
senses.definition: describing a definition that specifies the procedures or measurements used to identify something
senses.definitionCN: 指用识别某事物所需的具体程序或测量来下定义
senses.example: The study operationalised 'stress' as a rise in heart rate during the task.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究把“压力”操作化为任务期间心率上升。
senses.why: Some ideas cannot be seen directly, so science defines them by the operations that produce them, making the concept testable.
senses.whyCN: 有些概念无法直接看见，科学便用产生它的操作来定义，使概念可被检验。

senses.title: The mathematics of decisions
senses.titleCN: 运筹：把调度问题算清楚
senses.definition: describing the use of mathematical methods to improve the planning and running of complex activities
senses.definitionCN: 指用数学方法改进复杂活动的计划与运行
senses.example: Operational research cut the average waiting time at the depot.
senses.exampleCN: 运筹研究缩短了车站的平均等待时间。
senses.why: When an organization runs, its choices can be modelled; operational research treats scheduling as a problem with a best answer.
senses.whyCN: 组织一旦运转，其选择就可以建模型；运筹研究把调度当作一个有最优解的问题。

senses.title: At the level of action
senses.titleCN: 作战层面：战略之下、战术之上
senses.definition: describing the level of military activity concerned with planning and conducting campaigns
senses.definitionCN: 指军事活动中负责筹划与实施战役的层级
senses.example: Operational command decided where the units would meet before the battle.
senses.exampleCN: 作战指挥决定各部队在战斗前于何处会合。
senses.why: Military theory separates strategy (why to fight), operations (where and when to move), and tactics (how to fight the next hour).
senses.whyCN: 军事理论把战略（为何打）、作战（何时何地调动）与战术（接下来一小时怎么打）分开。

senses.title: Risk from daily running
senses.titleCN: 运营风险：不是市场，而是流程出错
senses.definition: describing the risk of loss from failed processes, people, systems, or external events
senses.definitionCN: 指因流程、人员、系统失效或外部事件造成损失的风险
senses.example: The bank holds capital against operational risk as well as credit risk.
senses.exampleCN: 银行不仅为信用风险，也为运营风险持有资本。
senses.why: Finance distinguishes risk from markets and borrowers from risk that arises simply because an organization must run every day.
senses.whyCN: 金融业把市场与借款人的风险，同“组织每天必须运转”本身带来的风险区分开。

senses.title: A circuit that computes
senses.titleCN: 运算放大器：让电路做算术
senses.definition: describing an amplifier designed to perform mathematical operations on signals
senses.definitionCN: 指为对信号执行数学运算而设计的放大器
senses.example: The operational amplifier summed the two sensor voltages.
senses.exampleCN: 运算放大器把两个传感器的电压相加。
senses.why: Early analogue computers used amplifiers to add and integrate; the name stayed even after the circuits became general-purpose components.
senses.whyCN: 早期模拟计算机用放大器做加法与积分；即使这些电路后来成了通用元件，名字仍保留下来。

intro.en: Operational is operation plus -al. Operation comes from Latin operatio, a working, from operari, to work, and opus, work.
intro.cn: operational 是 operation 加 -al。operation 来自拉丁语 operatio“劳作”，出自 operari“工作”与 opus“工作、作品”。

items.en: Opus meant work, a task, or a product of work. It survives in magnum opus and in the musical term opera.
items.cn: opus 意为工作、任务或劳动成果。它留在 magnum opus 与音乐术语 opera 中。

items.en: The verb meant to work, to labour, and to perform a task. It could describe both physical labour and the working of a power.
items.cn: 该动词意为工作、劳作、执行任务，既可描述体力劳动，也可描述某种力量的作用。

items.en: The noun named a working or an effect produced. Medieval Latin also used it for mathematical and medical procedures.
items.cn: 该名词指劳作或产生的效果。中世纪拉丁语也用它指数学与医学操作。

items.en: French operation covered work, a surgical procedure, and a military action. English borrowed all three.
items.cn: 法语 operation 涵盖工作、外科手术与军事行动；英语把这三层都借了进来。

items.en: Operational first meant 'of an operation' in surgery and mathematics, then extended to machines and organizations in the industrial age.
items.cn: operational 最初指外科与数学意义上的“操作的”， industrial 时代扩展到机器与组织。

items.en: The 20th century added operational research, operational definition, operational risk, and the operational amplifier.
items.cn: 20 世纪增加了运筹研究、操作定义、运营风险与运算放大器等用法。

note.en: The first group is the operate family; the second compares adjectives that describe readiness, function, and practical work.
note.cn: 第一组是 operate 词族；第二组比较表示就绪、功能与实际运作的形容词。

entries.definition: to work or control a machine, to run a business, or to perform surgery.
entries.definitionCN: 操作或控制机器、经营业务，或施行手术。

entries.definition: the act of working, a surgical procedure, or a military action.
entries.definitionCN: 工作行为、外科手术，或军事行动。

entries.definition: a person who runs a machine, or a company that runs a service.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机器的人，或经营某项服务的公司。

entries.definition: working as designed. It stresses purpose served, while operational can also stress the running process or its cost.
entries.definitionCN: 按设计正常工作；强调所服务的目的，而 operational 也可强调运行过程或成本。

entries.definition: useful in real situations rather than theoretical. It judges usefulness, not running status.
entries.definitionCN: 在真实情境中有用而非理论的；判断的是用处，不是运行状态。

entries.definition: in action or in effect. A system can be active without being fully operational.
entries.definitionCN: 正在行动或生效的；系统可以处于活动状态却尚未完全可运行。

entries.definition: relating to long-term aims. In military theory it is the level above operational.
entries.definitionCN: 与长期目标有关；在军事理论中位于“作战”之上。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: opus, work, plus operari, to work, then -ation and -al. Operational means 'of the working'.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：opus“工作”，加 operari“工作”，再加 -ation 与 -al。operational 就是“属于运转的”。

normal.en: Opus is work; operational is the adjective of work being done right now.
normal.cn: opus 是工作；operational 是“工作正在进行”的形容词。

normal.en: Design is the drawing; operational is the machine actually turning.
normal.cn: 设计是图纸；operational 是机器真的在转。

normal.en: Operational costs are the money paid every day, not the money paid to build.
normal.cn: 运营成本是每天都要付的钱，不是建造时付的钱。

normal.en: An operational definition says what you do, not what you mean.
normal.cn: 操作定义说的是你怎么做，而不是你指什么。

normal.en: All green lights mean the system is operational.
normal.cn: 指示灯全绿，就表示系统处于可运行状态。

abstract.en: 'Operational' is where plans meet friction: everything works on paper, and only some things work at three in the morning.
abstract.cn: operational 是计划撞上摩擦的地方：纸面上一切都能行，凌晨三点只有一部分真能行。

abstract.en: An operational definition trades depth for testability, and the trade is usually worth making.
abstract.cn: 操作定义用深度换可检验性，这笔交易通常值得。

abstract.en: The word hides the labour inside the system; what looks automatic is a schedule of people and maintenance.
abstract.cn: 这个词把系统里的劳动藏了起来；看似自动的东西，其实是一张排班表与维护表。

examples.en: The plant became fully operational only after the cooling system passed its safety test.
examples.cn: 冷却系统通过安全测试后，这座工厂才全面投入运行。

examples.en: Operational costs, not construction costs, decide whether the railway survives.
examples.cn: 决定这条铁路能否存续的是运营成本，而不是建设成本。

examples.en: The team agreed on an operational definition of 'success' before collecting any data.
examples.cn: 团队在收集数据之前先就“成功”的操作定义达成一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: operate（运行）+ ional（的）——能跑起来、正在运转的，都是 operational。

root: 由 operation（运行、操作，源自拉丁语 operatio“劳作”）加 -al 构成；词基为拉丁语 opus“工作”与 operari“工作”，故本义为“与运转、操作有关的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of operational, all concerned with work being done. The work may be a machine turning, a system ready to run, the cost of daily upkeep, a procedure that defines a concept, a mathematical plan, a military campaign, a process failure, or an analogue computation.
sensesIntro.cn: operational 的八个义项都与“正在做的工作”有关。这工作可以是机器转动、系统就绪、日常维护成本、定义概念的程序、数学调度、军事战役、流程失效，或模拟电路运算。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a production line running with every indicator green and nobody waiting for a repair.
core.cn: 核心意象：生产线正在运转，指示灯全绿，没有人等着维修。

chain: ENGLISH OPERATION THE ACT OF RUNNING
OPERATIONAL OF RUNNING OR READY TO RUN

branches.en: RUNNING AND READY: the process of working, and the state of being fit to work.
branches.cn: 运转与就绪：工作的过程，以及能够工作的状态。

branches.en: THE PRICE OF RUNNING: daily costs and the risks that arise from ordinary processes.
branches.cn: 运转的代价：日常成本，以及普通流程带来的风险。

branches.en: DEFINITION BY PROCEDURE: a concept replaced by the operations that measure it.
branches.cn: 以程序定义：用测量它的操作取代概念本身。

branches.en: PLANNING ACTION: mathematical scheduling and the military level between strategy and tactics.
branches.cn: 筹划行动：数学调度，以及位于战略与战术之间的军事层级。

branches.en: COMPUTING BY CIRCUIT: an amplifier named for the operations it performs.
branches.cn: 用电路运算：因执行运算而得名的放大器。

intro.en: Operational is operation plus -al. The family runs through operate, operator, and operation, with opus as the Latin base.
intro.cn: operational 是 operation 加 -al。词族包括 operate、operator、operation，拉丁词基为 opus。

latinIntro.en: The base is opus, work, and its verb operari. Latin operatio names the working or the effect produced.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 opus“工作”及其动词 operari。拉丁语 operatio 指劳作或产生的效果。

items.meaning: to work, control, or carry out an activity
items.example: Only trained staff may operate the crane.
items.exampleCN: 只有受过训练的员工可以操作这台起重机。

items.meaning: the act of working, or a planned action
items.meaningCN: 工作行为，或计划好的行动
items.example: The operation runs from six in the morning.
items.exampleCN: 这项作业从早晨六点开始运行。

items.meaning: relating to running, or ready to run
items.meaningCN: 与运行有关的，或已可运行的
items.example: The system is operational but not yet open to the public.
items.exampleCN: 系统已可运行，但尚未向公众开放。

items.meaning: from the point of view of running
items.example: Operationally, the two designs are almost the same.
items.exampleCN: 从运行角度看，两种设计几乎一样。

items.meaning: a person or firm that runs something
items.meaningCN: 操作者，或经营某项业务的公司
items.example: The operator stopped the line for a safety check.
items.exampleCN: 操作员为安全检查停下了生产线。

items.meaning: to work together toward a shared aim
items.meaningCN: 为共同目标一起工作；合作
items.example: The two labs cooperated on the trial.
items.exampleCN: 两个实验室在该试验上合作。

items.meaning: in effect or ready to act; also a surgical adjective
items.meaningCN: 生效的、可行动的；也用于外科语境
items.example: The new rule is operative from January.
items.exampleCN: 新规定自一月起生效。

items.meaning: a work, especially a large artistic or musical work
items.meaningCN: 作品，尤指大型艺术或音乐作品
items.example: The symphony became his best-known opus.
items.exampleCN: 这部交响曲成了他最著名的作品。

items.meaning: able to be operated or used
items.example: The hatch is operable from inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个舱门可从内部操作。

definition_zh: n. 榆树；榆木；行道榆
definition_en: a tall deciduous tree with rough toothed leaves and winged seeds; its hard timber
core_image: 村口一棵老榆树，树皮裂成深沟，树荫盖住半条路；孩子们把带翅的种子捡起来比谁抛得远；木匠刨着一块榆木，刨花卷成圈落在脚边
scene: 村口那棵老榆树的树皮裂成深沟，孩子们把带翅的种子捡起来比谁抛得远，树荫盖住了半条路。 An old elm shades half the village road.

pos.zh: 榆树；榆木；行道榆

senses.title: The tall shade tree
senses.definition: a tall deciduous tree with rough double-toothed leaves and winged seeds
senses.definitionCN: （名词）一种高大落叶乔木，叶缘有粗重锯齿，种子带翅
senses.example: An old elm shades half the village road.
senses.exampleCN: 一棵老榆树的树荫盖住了半条村路。
senses.why: A deeply furrowed trunk at a village corner with winged seeds on the ground.
senses.whyCN: 村口一根裂成深沟的树干，地上落着带翅的种子。

senses.title: The hard timber
senses.definition: the hard tough wood of this tree, used for furniture and boat parts
senses.definitionCN: （名词）这种树的坚硬木材，用于家具与船件
senses.example: The chair legs were cut from elm because it does not split easily.
senses.exampleCN: 椅子腿是用榆木切的，因为它不容易开裂。
senses.why: A carpenter plane curling off a pale block beside four turned chair legs.
senses.whyCN: 木匠刨着一块浅色木料，刨花卷成圈，旁边四条车好的椅腿。

senses.title: The avenue tree
senses.definition: elm grown along roads and avenues for shade
senses.definitionCN: （名词）为遮荫而种在道路与林荫道两侧的榆树
senses.example: The whole avenue was planted with elm before the disease reached the county.
senses.exampleCN: 在那场病害传到本郡之前，整条林荫道种的都是榆树。

intro.en: Elm is a native Old English word, elm, from a Germanic root shared with Dutch and German names; Latin ulmus names the same tree and gives the botanical genus Ulmus.
intro.cn: elm 是本土古英语词 elm，来自与荷兰语、德语名称共用的日耳曼词根；拉丁语 ulmus 指同一种树，给出植物学属名 Ulmus。

items.cn: 由甲虫传播的真菌在欧洲与北美杀死了大量榆树。

items.en: Breeders released elm varieties resistant to the disease.

senses.title: The process of ice covering the land
senses.definition: the growth and spread of glaciers over a landscape
senses.definitionCN: 指冰川在陆地上生成、扩张并覆盖地面的过程
senses.example: Glaciation begins where snow lasts all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 在积雪整夏不化的地方，冰川作用开始了。
senses.why: The noun ending turns the action of ice into a process that can be observed and dated.
senses.whyCN: 名词词尾把冰的作用变成一种可观察、可测年的过程。

senses.title: A glacial period
senses.definition: a episode in Earth history when ice sheets expanded far beyond their present limits
senses.definitionCN: 指地球历史上冰盖远远超出当今范围的一段时期
senses.example: The last glaciation ended about eleven thousand years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 末次冰期约在一万一千年前结束。
senses.why: A process repeated many times becomes countable, and each episode gets a name.
senses.whyCN: 同一过程反复发生便变得可数，每一次都可以命名。

senses.title: The extent of ice cover
senses.definition: the area or share of a region that was covered by ice
senses.definitionCN: 指某一地区被冰覆盖的面积或比例
senses.example: The glaciation of the plateau reached its lowest slopes.
senses.exampleCN: 高原的冰川覆盖一直延伸到最低的山坡。
senses.why: Mapping turns the process into a boundary on a map.
senses.whyCN: 制图把这个过程变成地图上的一条界线。

senses.title: Landforms made by ice
senses.definition: the set of features produced by moving ice, such as U-shaped valleys, moraines and polished rock
senses.definitionCN: 指移动的冰所造成的一组地貌，如槽形谷、冰碛与磨光岩面
senses.example: The valley's glaciation is read from its polished walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这条谷地的冰川作用可从磨光的谷壁读出来。
senses.why: The word can name the results as well as the cause, because the results are what survive.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既可指原因也可指结果，因为留存下来的正是结果。

senses.title: The geological record of past ice
senses.definition: the evidence in rock, sediment and landform that ice once covered an area
senses.definitionCN: 指岩石、沉积物与地貌中留下的、说明某地曾被冰覆盖的证据
senses.example: Scratches on the bedrock record ancient glaciation.
senses.exampleCN: 基岩上的擦痕记录了古老的冰川作用。
senses.why: Once the ice is gone, only traces remain, and the word shifts to the traces.
senses.whyCN: 冰退去之后只剩痕迹，这个词便转向这些痕迹。

senses.title: Alpine glaciation
senses.definition: glaciation confined to mountain valleys, where ice flows down existing channels
senses.definitionCN: 指局限于山谷的冰川作用，冰沿原有河道下流
senses.example: Alpine glaciation carves sharp ridges and deep cirques.
senses.exampleCN: 高山冰川作用刻出尖锐山脊与深冰斗。
senses.why: Mountain ice is channelled, so the landforms it makes are narrow and steep.
senses.whyCN: 山地冰川受地形约束，因此造成的形态狭窄而陡峭。

senses.title: Continental glaciation
senses.definition: glaciation by broad ice sheets that bury the landscape rather than follow valleys
senses.definitionCN: 指由宽阔冰盖造成的冰川作用，冰盖掩埋地景而不沿谷地下行
senses.example: Continental glaciation flattened the whole plain.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆冰川作用把整片平原削平。
senses.why: An ice sheet ignores the valleys beneath it, producing a very different signature.
senses.whyCN: 冰盖不理睬下面的谷地，留下的印记因而完全不同。

senses.title: The cooling that accompanies ice growth
senses.definition: the climatic cooling and drying associated with expanding ice
senses.definitionCN: 指与冰体扩张相关的气候变冷与变干
senses.example: Early glaciation lowered temperatures across the continent.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的冰川作用使整个大陆的气温下降。
senses.why: Ice both responds to climate and changes it, so the word carries a climatic echo.
senses.whyCN: 冰既响应气候又改变气候，这个词因此带上一层气候的回声。

intro.en: Glaciation rests on Latin glacies, ice, through the adjective glacialis and the Alpine word glacier. The noun with its process ending was formed in the nineteenth century, when geologists recognised that ice had once shaped whole landscapes; the exact coinage date is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词立在拉丁语 glacies「冰」之上，经形容词 glacialis 与阿尔卑斯山区表示「冰川」的词进入欧洲语言。带过程词尾的名词在十九世纪形成，当时地质学家认识到冰曾经塑造整片地景；确切造词年份不确定。

items.en: Glacies meant ice, the solid form of water.
items.cn: 这个词意为冰，即水的固态。

items.en: The adjective meant icy or frozen, and it survives in the English word glacial.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为冰的、冻结的，英语中表示「冰川的」形容词由它而来。

items.en: Alpine French used a word for the moving ice of a valley, and English borrowed it in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 阿尔卑斯山区的法语用某个词指谷地中流动的冰，英语在十八世纪借入。

items.en: The adjective entered geology for ice and for periods of ice growth.
items.cn: 这个形容词进入地质学，指冰的或冰期扩张的。

items.en: Geologists added the process ending to name the action of ice on a landscape; the first use is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 地质学家加过程词尾，用来指冰对地景的作用；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Twentieth-century work dated successive ice advances and retreats, making the word countable and cyclic.
items.cn: 二十世纪的研究为一次次冰进与冰退测年，使这个词变得可数并带有旋回意味。

note.en: The first group shares the ice root or a derived ending; the second group names the periods, the ice bodies and the debris.
note.cn: 第一组共享「冰」词根或派生词尾；第二组是时期、冰体与碎屑的说法。

entries.definition: A mass of ice that moves slowly down a valley or across a continent.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿谷地下行或横过大陆的缓慢移动冰体。

entries.definition: Relating to ice or to a glacial period.
entries.definitionCN: 指与冰或冰期有关的。

entries.definition: To subject a landscape to the action of ice.
entries.definitionCN: 指使地景受到冰的作用。

entries.definition: The retreat and melting of ice at the end of a glacial period.
entries.definitionCN: 指冰期结束时冰的退缩与融化。

entries.definition: A warmer interval between two glacial periods.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个冰期之间较温暖的间隔。

entries.definition: A long period when ice sheets were extensive.
entries.definitionCN: 指冰盖范围广大的漫长时期。

entries.definition: A single cold episode within an ice age.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个冰期内的一次寒冷阶段。

entries.definition: A broad dome of ice covering a continent.
entries.definitionCN: 指覆盖大陆的宽阔冰穹。

entries.definition: Debris carried and dumped by a glacier.
entries.definitionCN: 指冰川搬运并堆积的碎屑。

entries.definition: Unsorted sediment left directly by ice.
entries.definitionCN: 指冰直接留下的未经分选的沉积物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the Latin word for ice and the marks ice leaves.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着拉丁语的「冰」词与冰留下的痕迹展开。

normal.en: Ice plus a process ending: the work ice does to a landscape.
normal.cn: 冰加过程词尾，就是冰对地景所做的工作。

normal.en: A U-shaped valley and polished walls are the signature of mountain ice.
normal.cn: 槽形谷与磨光的谷壁是山地冰川的标志。

normal.en: Scratches on bedrock outlive the ice that cut them.
normal.cn: 基岩上的擦痕比刻出它的冰活得更久。

normal.en: An ice sheet ignores valleys and flattens everything beneath it.
normal.cn: 冰盖不理睬谷地，把下面的一切削平。

normal.en: Repeated advances make the word countable: one glaciation, then another.
normal.cn: 反复的冰进让这个词可数：一次冰期，又一次冰期。

abstract.en: Ice is a sculptor that leaves its tools behind as rubble.
abstract.cn: 冰是一位雕刻家，把工具留成了碎石。

abstract.en: A process can be named twice: once as an event, once as the shape it left.
abstract.cn: 同一过程可以被命名两次：一次作为事件，一次作为留下的形状。

abstract.en: What melts away can still be read in what it scratched.
abstract.cn: 融化消失之物，仍能从它划过的痕迹里读出。

examples.en: Continental glaciation buried the plain under a sheet of ice.
examples.cn: 大陆冰川作用把平原埋在一片冰盖之下。

examples.en: The cirque is a classic landform of alpine glaciation.
examples.cn: 冰斗是高山冰川作用的典型地貌。

examples.en: Dates of past glaciation come from rocks and sediments.
examples.cn: 历次冰川作用的年代来自岩石与沉积物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「格拉西艾申」——格拉西（冰）把山谷磨光又退走，留下一个冰期：冰川作用、冰期

root: 拉丁语 glacies「冰」经形容词 glacialis 与阿尔卑斯法语表示「冰川」的词进入英语；带过程词尾的名词于十九世纪形成，确切年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split the process from its episodes, its extent, its landforms, its traces, its mountain and continental styles, and its cooling effect.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把过程与其次序分开：过程本身、一次次冰期、覆盖范围、地貌、痕迹、山地与大陆两种样式，以及它带来的降温。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a retreating glacier exposing polished rock and ridges of loose debris.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条退缩的冰川露出磨光的岩石与成脊的碎屑。

branches.en: THE PROCESS AND ITS EPISODES: ice growing and spreading, then a named cold period.
branches.cn: 过程与阶段：冰生成、扩张，随后是一次具名的寒冷期。

branches.en: THE MAP: the area that ice covered.
branches.cn: 地图上的范围：冰曾经覆盖的区域。

branches.en: THE CARVING: landforms, in mountain valleys and under broad sheets.
branches.cn: 雕刻结果：山谷与冰盖之下形成的地貌。

branches.en: THE TRACES: scratches, sediment and erratics left after the melt.
branches.cn: 痕迹：融化后留下的擦痕、沉积物与漂砾。

branches.en: THE CLIMATE ECHO: cooling that accompanies the ice.
branches.cn: 气候回声：随冰而来的降温。

intro.en: The word is Latin ice with a process ending, plus a French word for the moving ice itself.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语的「冰」加过程词尾，另有法语词指流动的冰本身。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the noun for ice and the adjective for icy; French supplies the name of the moving mass.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供「冰」的名词与「冰的」形容词；法语提供流动冰体的名称。
