core_image: 一只戴着手套的手把两块原料按到一起，手套上印着小小的标签，说明这双手属于某个催化者
scene: 这里指「酶的」。 The enzymatic breakdown of starch begins in the mouth and continues in the small intestine.
sceneCN: 这里 enzymatic 指「酶促的、由酶完成的」（第 2 个义项：说明该过程依靠酶而非化学试剂进行）；淀粉的分解从口腔开始，到小肠继续。图中可辨识物件：戴手套的手、两块原料、催化剂标签、分解产物。

pos.zh: 酶的；酶催化的；由酶完成的（多作定语，修饰反应、水解、测定等）

senses.title: Belonging to an enzyme
senses.definition: relating to an enzyme as an object or a category
senses.definitionCN: 与酶这一对象或类别相关
senses.example: The enzymatic machinery of the lysosome is encoded by dozens of genes.
senses.exampleCN: 溶酶体的酶系统由数十个基因编码。
senses.why: the suffix adds a relation to the noun, so the adjective first answers 'whose?' or 'of what kind?'.
senses.whyCN: 后缀给名词加上关系，因此这个形容词首先回答「谁的」或「哪一类」。

senses.title: Carried out by an enzyme
senses.titleCN: 酶促的：由酶而非试剂完成
senses.definition: describing a reaction that is run by an enzyme instead of by heat or a chemical reagent
senses.definitionCN: 描述由酶而非加热或化学试剂推动的反应
senses.example: The conversion is enzymatic, so it happens at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这一转化是酶促的，因此在室温下即可发生。
senses.why: the adjective moves from the owner to the method: a reaction labelled enzymatic owes its speed to the catalyst.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从「所有者」转向「方法」：被标为 enzymatic 的反应，其速度归功于催化剂。

senses.title: The reaction as a category
senses.titleCN: 酶促反应的：作为一类过程
senses.definition: naming a whole class of reactions studied in biochemistry, as opposed to non-enzymatic ones
senses.definitionCN: 命名生物化学中一整类反应，以区别于非酶促反应
senses.example: Enzymatic reactions outnumber spontaneous ones in a living cell.
senses.exampleCN: 在活细胞中，酶促反应远多于自发反应。
senses.why: because the class is defined by its cause, the adjective can name the category rather than one event.
senses.whyCN: 由于该类由成因定义，这个形容词可以命名整个类别，而不是单个事件。

senses.title: Activity you can measure
senses.definition: describing the measurable activity of an enzyme in a sample
senses.definitionCN: 描述样本中可测定的酶活性
senses.example: Enzymatic activity fell sharply after the sample was heated.
senses.exampleCN: 样本加热后酶活性急剧下降。
senses.why: once the catalyst is assayed, 'enzymatic' also qualifies the quantity being measured.
senses.whyCN: 当催化剂被测定时，enzymatic 也用来限定被测定的那个量。

senses.title: Breakdown by enzyme
senses.definition: describing the splitting of a molecule into smaller pieces by enzymes
senses.definitionCN: 描述由酶把分子切成更小片段
senses.example: Enzymatic hydrolysis turns the protein into short peptides.
senses.exampleCN: 酶解把蛋白质变成短肽。
senses.why: digestion is the oldest use of catalysts, so the adjective attaches naturally to the cutting of bonds, as in enzymatic hydrolysis.
senses.whyCN: 消化是催化剂最古老的用途，因此这个形容词自然附着在断键上，如酶解。

senses.title: Assembly by enzyme
senses.definition: describing the building of a product with enzymes instead of chemical synthesis
senses.definitionCN: 描述用酶而非化学合成来制造产物
senses.example: Enzymatic synthesis avoids the toxic solvent used in the chemical route.
senses.exampleCN: 酶法合成避免了化学路线所用的有毒溶剂。
senses.why: the same catalyst that cuts can also join, so the adjective also marks a gentler way of building.
senses.whyCN: 能切的催化剂也能接，因此这个形容词也标记一种更温和的制造方式。

senses.title: Degradation by enzyme
senses.titleCN: 酶促降解的：被酶分解掉
senses.definition: describing the natural or engineered destruction of a substance by enzymes
senses.definitionCN: 描述某物质被酶自然或工程化地分解
senses.example: Enzymatic degradation removed the pesticide from the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 酶促降解把农药从土壤中清除。
senses.why: when the product must disappear, the adjective names the process that removes it rather than the one that makes it.
senses.whyCN: 当产物需要消失时，这个形容词命名的是清除过程，而不是制造过程。

senses.title: The control that has none
senses.titleCN: 对照义：与非酶过程相对
senses.definition: used contrastively, as in non-enzymatic, to mark what happens without a catalyst
senses.definitionCN: 用于对比，如 non-enzymatic，标记没有催化剂时发生的事
senses.example: The same sugar browned faster by the enzymatic route than by the non-enzymatic one.
senses.exampleCN: 同样的糖经酶促途径比非酶途径褐变得更快。
senses.why: science needs a control, so the adjective also lives in its negated form, defining the process by what it lacks.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要对照，因此这个形容词也活在否定形式中，用「缺少什么」来定义过程。

intro.en: Enzymatic is the English adjective on enzyme, with the suffix -atic, ultimately from Latin -aticus, itself from Greek -atikos. The base was coined in 1877.
intro.cn: enzymatic 是以 enzyme 为词干、加后缀 -atic 的英语形容词，-atic 源自拉丁 -aticus，后者又来自希腊 -atikos；词干造于 1877 年。

items.en: enzyme joins en- 'in' to zymē 'leaven'; the adjective inherits that compound without change.
items.cn: enzyme 把 en-「在内」与 zymē「酵素」结合；形容词原样继承这个合成词。

items.en: Latin -aticus formed adjectives of relation and manner, as in aquaticus and fanaticus; Greek -atikos is its model.
items.cn: 拉丁 -aticus 构成表示关系与方式的形容词，如 aquaticus、fanaticus；其原型是希腊 -atikos。

items.en: English keeps the suffix as -atic, so enzyme yields enzymatic beside the older enzymic.
items.cn: 英语把该后缀保留为 -atic，于是 enzyme 产生 enzymatic，与较早的 enzymic 并存。

items.en: The adjective appears soon after the noun in late nineteenth-century biochemistry; the first citation is approximate.
items.cn: 该形容词在 19 世纪后期的生物化学文献中随名词不久出现；最早书证年代为约数。

items.en: Assays and industrial processes fixed phrases such as enzymatic activity, enzymatic hydrolysis and enzymatic browning.
items.cn: 测定与工业流程固定了 enzymatic activity、enzymatic hydrolysis、enzymatic browning 等搭配。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English citation of the adjective is not recorded, and the choice between the -atic and -ic spellings has never followed a single rule.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：该形容词的最早英语书证无确切记录；-atic 与 -ic 两种写法并存的取舍亦无统一规则。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the stem but differ in part of speech or in what they name; group two holds adjectives used in the same experimental sentences.
note.cn: 第一组是共享词干、但词性或所指不同的词；第二组是出现在同一类实验句子中的形容词。

entries.definition: The catalyst itself. Enzymatic only qualifies; a countable thing needs the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指催化剂本身；enzymatic 只是限定语，指可数事物须用名词。

entries.definition: An older synonym of enzymatic, built with -ic. Both qualify the same nouns, but enzymatic is now the common form.
entries.definitionCN: enzymatic 的较早同义词，由 -ic 构成；二者修饰同样的名词，但现在常用 enzymatic。

entries.definition: An inactive enzyme form that must be cut to work; it shares zymē but names a precursor, not a property.
entries.definitionCN: 必须被切割才有活性的酶前体；共享 zymē，但指前体而非性质。

entries.definition: A small molecule assisting an enzyme; sharing the stem does not make it an adjective of relation.
entries.definitionCN: 辅助酶的小分子；共享词干并不意味着它是关系形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to catalysis of any kind, including inorganic catalysts; enzymatic specifies that the catalyst is an enzyme.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何催化，包括无机催化剂；enzymatic 明确催化剂是酶。

entries.definition: Relating to hydrolysis, the splitting of bonds by water, which may or may not involve enzymes.
entries.definitionCN: 与水解相关，即用水断键，可能涉及酶，也可能不涉及。

entries.definition: Relating to chemistry in living things generally; enzymatic names only the agent of the reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指生物体内的化学；enzymatic 只命名反应的推动者。

entries.definition: The negated form, marking what happens with no enzyme at all; it is a contrast term, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 否定形式，标记完全没有酶时发生的事；是对照词，不是同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: enzyme + -atic: the same relational suffix as in aquatic and dramatic.
normal.cn: enzyme + -atic：与 aquatic、dramatic 中的关系后缀相同。

normal.en: The family runs enzyme, enzymatic, enzymic, enzymatically, enzymology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 enzyme、enzymatic、enzymic、enzymatically、enzymology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: enzymatic reaction, enzymatic hydrolysis, enzymatic activity, enzymatic browning.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：酶促反应、酶解、酶活性、酶促褐变。

normal.en: The pair is easy: enzyme is the actor, enzymatic is the way the action is done.
normal.cn: 这组词很好分：enzyme 是行动者，enzymatic 是行动的方式。

normal.en: Food science uses enzymatic browning for the darkening of cut apples and potatoes.
normal.cn: 食品科学用 enzymatic browning 指切开苹果与土豆的变褐。

abstract.en: Picture gloved hands pressing two pieces together, with the glove carrying a small maker's mark.
abstract.cn: 想象戴手套的双手把两块料按到一起，手套上带着小小的制造者标记。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen that uses a living starter instead of a stove.
abstract.cn: 想象一间厨房用活的酵头代替炉火。

abstract.en: Picture a demolition crew that takes the building apart piece by piece instead of blowing it up.
abstract.cn: 想象一支拆除队把建筑逐块拆下，而不是炸掉。

examples.en: Enzymatic hydrolysis is gentler than acid hydrolysis for food proteins.
examples.cn: 对食品蛋白而言，酶解比酸解更温和。

examples.en: The researchers measured enzymatic activity every ten minutes.
examples.cn: 研究人员每十分钟测定一次酶活性。

examples.en: Enzymatic browning can be slowed by adding lemon juice.
examples.cn: 加入柠檬汁可减缓酶促褐变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「酶（enzyme）＋atic」——带酶属性的、靠酶完成的 → 酶促的、酶解的

root: 希腊 en-「在内」+ zymē「酵素」→ enzyme（1877）+ 拉丁 -aticus（希腊 -atikos）→ enzymatic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one relational suffix: the enzyme is the owner, then the method, then the category, then the measured activity, then cutting, then joining, then removing, and finally the control that lacks it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个表关系的后缀散开：先是所有者，再是方法、类别、被测的活性、切开、接上、清除，最后是缺少它的对照。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: gloved hands press two pieces together, and the glove carries the catalyst's mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：戴手套的双手把两块料按到一起，手套上带着催化剂的标记。

branches.en: OWNERSHIP: the plain relational sense, 'of an enzyme'.
branches.cn: 归属：最朴素的关系义，「酶的」。

branches.en: METHOD AND CLASS: a reaction run by the catalyst, and the whole category so defined.
branches.cn: 方法与类别：由催化剂推动的反应，以及由此定义的整类。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: the activity that can be read off an assay.
branches.cn: 测定：可从测定中读出的活性。

branches.en: CUT, JOIN, REMOVE: hydrolysis, synthesis and degradation all use the same adjective.
branches.cn: 切、接、除：酶解、酶法合成与酶促降解共用同一个形容词。

branches.en: CONTROL: the negated form defines the process by what it does without.
branches.cn: 对照：否定形式用「缺少什么」来定义过程。

intro.en: The adjective is the English noun enzyme plus the relational suffix -atic, from Latin -aticus and Greek -atikos.
intro.cn: 该形容词是英语名词 enzyme 加关系后缀 -atic，后者出自拉丁 -aticus 与希腊 -atikos。

latinIntro.en: Only the suffix is Latin; the base is Greek plus modern coinage. New Latin enzyma is a re-spelling, not an inherited word.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后缀是拉丁语；词干是希腊语加现代造词。新拉丁语 enzyma 只是改写拼写，不是传承词。

items.meaning: of an enzyme; done by an enzyme
items.example: The cleavage is entirely enzymatic.
items.exampleCN: 这次切割完全由酶完成。

items.example: The product is enzymatically degraded within hours.
items.exampleCN: 该产物在数小时内被酶促降解。

items.example: The enzyme is stable below forty degrees.
items.exampleCN: 该酶在四十度以下稳定。

items.example: Enzymic activity was measured in the extract.
items.exampleCN: 提取液中测定了酶活性。

items.example: Modern enzymology began with fermentation.
items.exampleCN: 现代酶学始于发酵研究。

items.example: Non-enzymatic glycation damages proteins.
items.exampleCN: 非酶促糖化会损伤蛋白质。

items.meaning: darkening of food catalysed by enzymes
items.example: Enzymatic browning spoiled the cut fruit.
items.exampleCN: 酶促褐变使切开的水果变坏。

items.meaning: a test that measures enzyme activity
items.example: The enzymatic assay needs a standard curve.
items.exampleCN: 酶法测定需要标准曲线。

latinEntries.meaning: relating to; of the nature of

definition_zh: 政治；政治活动；政治见解；政界；政治学；组织内部的权术运作
definition_en: the activity by which people govern, compete for office and settle collective decisions, also used for a person's views, the profession, the academic subject and internal manoeuvring
core_image: 旱季的村口，两派人围在水渠分水口争论，最后按人头重新排定用水次序
scene: 旱季的村口，两派人围在水渠的分水口争论，最后按人头重新排定用水次序。 Politics in the valley had always been about who controlled the water.
sceneCN: 这里指「治理与争夺权力的活动」，对应第 1 个义项：围绕公共资源由谁决定而展开的争夺；句意为这条山谷里的政治历来就是围绕谁掌握水源展开的。画面要点：分水口、两排站立的人、记名的木板；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 政治；政治活动（不可数，作主语时视为单数）
政治见解；政治立场（作此义时可用作复数）

forms.label: 本词（以复数词尾结尾，作学科或活动时视为单数）

derivatives.zh: 在政治方面；从政治角度
使政治化；把……变成政治议题

senses.title: The activity of governing and competing for power
senses.titleCN: 治理与争夺权力的活动
senses.definition: the activity by which groups decide who holds public authority and how it is used
senses.definitionCN: 各群体决定公共权力归谁掌握、如何使用的活动
senses.example: Politics decides who gets the water and who waits.
senses.exampleCN: 政治决定谁能先得水、谁只能等。
senses.why: the Greek root names the city and its citizens, so the word began as the business of the civic body rather than of private life.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的希腊词根指城邦及其公民，因此它最初指公民集体的事务，而非私人生活。

senses.title: A person's views or affiliation
senses.titleCN: 个人的政治见解或党派立场
senses.definition: the set of beliefs a person holds about how society and government should be run
senses.definitionCN: 一个人对社会与政府应如何运转所持的一整套信念
senses.example: Her politics are greener than her party's platform.
senses.exampleCN: 她的政治立场比本党纲领更偏环保。
senses.why: beliefs about governing are held by individuals, so the plural noun came to mean one person's stance and can take a plural verb in this sense.
senses.whyCN: 关于治理的信念由个人持有，因此这个以复数形式收尾的名词转指个人的立场，作此义时可用复数动词。

senses.title: The profession and world of politicians
senses.definition: the career, workplace and daily life of those who hold or seek public office
senses.definitionCN: 担任或谋求公职者的职业、职场与日常处境
senses.example: He went into politics after running the city hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 他管过市立医院之后进入了政界。
senses.why: an activity that occupies a career becomes a place one enters, hence phrases about going into or leaving politics.
senses.whyCN: 一项活动一旦占据一份职业，就变成可以走进去的场所，于是有了进入政界、退出政界这类说法。

senses.title: The academic subject
senses.titleCN: 政治学（学科名，英式常用）
senses.definition: the study of government and political behaviour as a university discipline
senses.definitionCN: 在大学里把政府与政治行为作为研究对象的学科
senses.example: She read politics before turning to law.
senses.exampleCN: 她先读政治学，之后转行学法。
senses.why: the Greek title of a book on civic affairs became the name of the school subject that studies them.
senses.whyCN: 一本论城邦事务的希腊书名，后来成了研究这些事务的学科名称。

senses.title: Manoeuvring inside an organization
senses.definition: the informal struggle for influence and favour within a workplace, club or family
senses.definitionCN: 在工作场所、团体或家庭内部为影响力与青睐而进行的非正式争夺
senses.example: Office politics kept the best engineer off the project.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室里的权术让最好的工程师进不了这个项目。
senses.why: the patterns of alliance and rivalry repeat at any scale, so the word is borrowed wherever a small group allocates scarce goods.
senses.whyCN: 结盟与对立的方式在任何规模上都会重演，因此只要小群体分配稀缺之物，这个词就会被借去用。

senses.title: Public contest over policy and office
senses.titleCN: 围绕政策与职位的公共竞争
senses.definition: the open competition of parties, campaigns and interest groups over what government should do
senses.definitionCN: 政党、竞选活动与利益团体围绕政府应当做什么而展开的公开竞争
senses.example: The politics of the budget turned on two marginal seats.
senses.exampleCN: 预算的政治角力集中在两个边缘选区上。
senses.why: when conflict is public and organised, the word names the contest itself rather than the general activity.
senses.whyCN: 当冲突公开且有组织时，这个词指的是竞争本身，而不是笼统的活动。

senses.title: The arena or system as a whole
senses.titleCN: 政治舞台与制度环境的总称
senses.definition: the whole institutional setting in which authority is won, used and lost
senses.definitionCN: 权力被赢得、使用与失去的整套制度环境
senses.example: Trust in politics fell after the expenses scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 报销丑闻之后，人们对政治这一套制度的信任下降了。
senses.why: the activity and the setting are named by one word, so the noun can stand for the entire arena in which the activity happens.
senses.whyCN: 活动与场所用同一个词表示，因此这个名词也能指活动发生的整个场域。

senses.title: Abstract: the negotiation of collective interests
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：集体利益的协商过程
senses.definition: in general use, any process by which a group with diverging interests reaches a workable decision
senses.definitionCN: 泛指利益分歧的群体达成可行决定的任何过程
senses.example: There is politics in every committee that must divide a budget.
senses.exampleCN: 凡是要分预算的委员会，都有政治。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the settling of divergent interests and lets the state and the ballot drop away.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只留下「摆平分歧利益」这层意思，国家与选票则退出了画面。

intro.en: Politics goes back through French and Latin to the Greek title of Aristotle's book on civic affairs, built on the Greek word for a city. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: politics 经法语与拉丁语上溯到亚里士多德论城邦事务那本书的希腊书名，其词根是希腊语中表示「城邦」的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Polis meant a city-state and the citizen body that made it; its deeper origin is not established, and the suggestion of a pre-Greek source is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: polis 指城邦以及构成城邦的公民总体；它更深的来源未得到证明，关于其源自前希腊语层的说法只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Polites meant a citizen, one who belongs to the polis and shares in its decisions, and from it came the adjective politikos 'of citizens, civic'.
items.cn: politēs 指公民，即属于城邦并参与其决定的人；由它产生形容词 politikos「公民的、城邦的」。

items.en: Ta politika meant 'the things concerning the city', the title of Aristotle's treatise on the government of states, and it named civic affairs rather than party strife.
items.cn: ta politika 意为「与城邦有关的事务」，是亚里士多德论国家治理那部书的书名，所指为公民事务，而非党派争斗。

items.en: Medieval Latin politica was coined from the Greek title to name the study of the state, and it passed through French into English in the late fifteenth century.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 politica 依那个希腊书名造出，用来指对国家的研究，并在十五世纪晚期经法语进入英语。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word spread to party competition, then to the internal manoeuvring of any institution, and finally to 'the politics of' almost any activity.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词先扩展到党派竞争，再指任何机构内部的权术，最后出现「某事背后的政治」这种几乎可用于一切活动的说法。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Greek city root that are easily confused with politics; group two holds terms for governing that do not carry the competitive sense.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊「城邦」词根、容易与 politics 混淆的词；第二组是表示治理、但不含竞争意味的术语。

entries.definition: A settled course of action adopted by a government or firm; politics is the struggle that produces or blocks a policy.
entries.definitionCN: 政府或机构采用的既定行动方案；政治则是产生或阻挠某项政策的那场争夺。

entries.definition: A politically organised society viewed as a unit, as in a federal polity; it names the body, not its activity.
entries.definitionCN: 被视作一个单位的有政治组织的社会，如联邦政体；它指共同体本身，而非其活动。

entries.definition: An older adjective meaning shrewd and tactful, as in a politic silence; it describes judgement, not government.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的形容词，意为精明得体的，如得体的沉默；它描述判断力，而非政府事务。

entries.definition: A person who holds or seeks office; the practice they live by is politics, and the two are constantly used together.
entries.definitionCN: 担任或谋求公职的人；他们以此谋生的活动就是政治，两者常连用。

entries.definition: The body that exercises authority in a state; government is the machine, while politics is the contest that drives it.
entries.definitionCN: 在国家中行使权力的机构；政府是机器，政治则是驱动机器的那场竞争。

entries.definition: The processes and rules by which decisions are taken, often used of firms and agencies; it is quieter and more technical than politics.
entries.definitionCN: 作出决定所依的流程与规则，常用于企业与机构；它比政治更平实、更技术化。

entries.definition: The art of conducting state affairs, especially foreign policy; it stresses skill and is used of leaders rather than of voters.
entries.definitionCN: 处理国家事务、尤其外交事务的技艺；强调技巧，多用于领导人而非选民。

entries.definition: A neutral term for matters of common concern and the work of dealing with them; it avoids the combative tone of politics.
entries.definitionCN: 对公共事务及其处理工作的中性说法；避开了政治一词的争斗意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is the Greek word for a city-state, so politics is literally the business of the city.
normal.cn: 词根是希腊语中表示城邦的词，所以政治字面上就是城邦的事务。

normal.en: The family runs political, politically, politician, policy, polity and politicize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括政治的、在政治上、政治家、政策、政体与使政治化。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the senses: go into politics, office politics, party politics, the politics of reform.
normal.cn: 固定搭配给各义项分类：进入政界、办公室权术、党派政治、改革的政治角力。

normal.en: The word ends in -s but takes a singular verb when it names the activity or the subject.
normal.cn: 这个词虽以表示复数的词尾结尾，但指活动或学科时作单数用。

normal.en: A politician lives by politics; a policy is what the struggle produces.
normal.cn: 政治家靠政治为生；政策则是这场争夺的产物。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd at a water channel, each faction counting heads before the gate is opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人围在水渠边，各派在开闸前清点人数。

abstract.en: Picture a table where five people must split one loaf and nobody wants the smallest piece.
abstract.cn: 想象五个人要分一只面包，谁都不愿拿最小的一块。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor where two groups whisper before entering the same voting hall.
abstract.cn: 想象走廊里两群人在进同一个投票厅之前低声商量。

examples.en: Politics in the region has long followed family lines.
examples.cn: 这个地区的政治长期沿家族脉络运行。

examples.en: She left politics to run a research institute.
examples.cn: 她退出政界，去主持一家研究所。

examples.en: He never discusses his politics at work.
examples.cn: 他在工作时从不谈自己的政治立场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「城邦的事务」——城里人一起商量谁说了算 → 政治

root: politics 经法语与拉丁语出自希腊 ta politika「与城邦有关的事务」，源头是 polis「城邦」与 politēs「公民」；polis 更深来源不确定，前希腊语来源仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses widen from one root: the business of the city becomes a career, then a set of personal beliefs, a university subject, the manoeuvring of any small group, an open electoral contest, the whole arena, and finally any settlement of divergent interests.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由同一个词根向外扩：城邦的事务先成为一门职业，再成为个人的一整套信念、一门大学学科、任何小团体内部的权术、公开的选举竞争、整个政治场域，最后是任何摆平分歧利益的过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: neighbours arguing at a water gate until a rule is agreed.
core.cn: 核心意象：邻人在分水口争论，直到商定一条规则。

branches.en: ROOT ACTIVITY: deciding who holds public authority, the oldest and widest reading.
branches.cn: 根本活动：决定公共权力归谁，这是最古老也最宽的读法。

branches.en: PERSONAL AND PROFESSIONAL: the same word covers what a private person believes and the trade a public person lives by.
branches.cn: 个人与职业：同一个词既指私人的信念，也指公开人物赖以谋生的行业。

branches.en: SUBJECT: the civic business turned into a course of study with its own methods.
branches.cn: 学科：城邦事务被变成一门有自身方法的研究。

branches.en: SCALE OF CONFLICT: quiet manoeuvring in an office and open contest at an election are the same pattern at different sizes.
branches.cn: 冲突的规模：办公室里无声的权术与选举中公开的竞争，是同一种格局的不同尺寸。

branches.en: ARENA AND GENERAL FORM: the whole stage where authority changes hands, then any group dividing what it needs.
branches.cn: 场域与一般形态：先是权力易手的整个舞台，后是任何分配所需之物的群体。

intro.en: Politics rests on a Greek noun for the city and its citizen body, a stem that also builds policy, polity and politician in English.
intro.cn: politics 立在一个表示城邦及其公民总体的希腊名词上，同一词干在英语里还造出政策、政体与政治家。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed the Greek stem as politicus and politica, the forms through which the word family reached English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊词干借作 politicus 与 politica，这个词族正是经这两种形式进入英语的。

items.example: The root names the unit within which decisions were made.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指出作出决定的那个单位。

items.example: The citizen, not the subject, is the base of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的基础是公民，而非臣民。

items.example: The adjective described matters that concerned the citizen body.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述与公民总体相关的事务。

items.structure: -ics (Greek suffix naming an art or study)
items.example: The suffix turns civic affairs into a named field.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把城邦事务变成一个有名称的领域。

items.example: The suffix marks the practitioner.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记从业者。

items.structure: Old French policie, from Latin politica
items.example: Policy is the settled plan, not the contest.
items.exampleCN: 政策是定下来的方案，而非争夺本身。

items.example: A polity can be a city, a state or a federation.
items.exampleCN: 政体可以是一座城、一个国家或一个联邦。

items.example: The budget dispute politicized the school board.
items.exampleCN: 预算争执把校董会政治化了。

items.example: The decision was political rather than technical.
items.exampleCN: 这个决定是政治性的，而非技术性的。

latinEntries.structure: politicus, politica, politicum (adjective, borrowed from Greek)
politica, politicae (f., first declension; from Greek ta politika)
politia, politiae (f., first declension; from Greek politeia)

definition_zh: 使康复；使恢复功能；改造罪犯使之重返社会；恢复名誉、权利或职位；使建筑物、生态恢复良好状态
definition_en: to restore a person to health, ability or a normal place in society, or to bring something back into good condition
core_image: 康复室里，病人双手扶着平行杠重新学迈步，治疗师在旁护着腰
scene: 事故之后，那名木工半年上不了脚手架，康复中心替他排了一套从抬腿到负重的训练。 The clinic designed a slow programme to rehabilitate the injured carpenter.
sceneCN: 这里指「通过训练使伤者重新恢复身体功能」，对应第 2 个义项：借助治疗与反复练习，把失去的动作能力一点点建回来；句意为康复中心为受伤的木工安排了一套循序渐进的训练。画面要点：平行杠、治疗师、重新迈出的第一步。

pos.zh: 使康复；改造；恢复（及物动词，宾语可为人、机构、建筑或生态）

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或结果）→ 由「使恢复能力」转为「康复、复权的整个过程」
加形容词后缀（表倾向或功能）→ 由「使恢复」转为「有助于康复的」
加过去分词词尾（转作形容词）→ 由「已使恢复」转为「已康复或已恢复资格的」
由拉丁词干（源自 habilis「能干的」）加动词词尾（源自拉丁语，表「使……」）→ 由「能干」转为「使具备能力、使合用」
habilitate 加名词后缀（表动作或结果）→ 由「使有能力」转为「取得资格的过程」
源自拉丁 habilis「易于掌握的、能干的」加名词后缀（表性质）→ 由「能干」转为「能力」这一性质

senses.title: Back to health: a sick body made well
senses.titleCN: 让病后的身体回到健康
senses.definition: to bring a person back to health after illness or injury through care and treatment
senses.definitionCN: 通过照料与治疗，使人在患病或受伤之后恢复健康
senses.example: The team worked for months to rehabilitate patients after the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 团队工作了数月，帮助火灾后的病人康复。
senses.why: The prefix re- means 'again, back', and the Latin base means 'to make able', so the core is not punishment but the return of a capacity that had been lost.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表示「再、回」，拉丁词干意为「使有能力」，因此这个词的核心不是惩罚，而是让一项失去的能力回来。

senses.title: Retraining a joint or limb: step by step
senses.titleCN: 一点一点练回关节与肢体
senses.definition: to train a specific movement or faculty until it works again
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一动作或机能反复训练，直到它重新正常工作
senses.example: She practised daily to rehabilitate her injured shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天练习，让受伤的肩膀恢复功能。
senses.why: The capacity is concrete: a shoulder, a knee, a step. The verb then names the slow drill that brings the movement back rather than the abstract idea of health.
senses.whyCN: 这里的能力很具体：一个肩膀、一只膝盖、一步路。动词因此指把这动作练回来的缓慢训练，而不是抽象的健康概念。

senses.title: Reform for society: not merely punish
senses.titleCN: 为重返社会而改造，而非只加惩罚
senses.definition: to prepare a convicted person for ordinary life through education, work and treatment rather than mere punishment
senses.definitionCN: 以教育、劳动与治疗帮助已定罪者过普通生活，而不是只施加惩罚
senses.example: The prison runs classes to rehabilitate young offenders.
senses.exampleCN: 这所监狱开设课程，帮助少年犯改过自新。
senses.why: A person who has lost their place in society is treated like a person who has lost a function: the task is to restore the ability to live among others, not to add pain.
senses.whyCN: 失去社会位置的人，被当作失去一项功能的人来处理：任务是恢复他与别人共同生活的能力，而不是增加痛苦。

senses.title: Rights and name restored: the legal sense
senses.titleCN: 恢复权利与名誉的法律义
senses.definition: to give a person back a former legal standing, office or good name
senses.definitionCN: 把某人原先的法律地位、职位或名誉归还给他
senses.example: The decree rehabilitated the officers who had been dismissed.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法令为那些被免职的军官恢复了名誉。
senses.why: This is the oldest use: re- means back, and the person is returned to a position that had been taken away, so the word speaks of standing rather than of the body.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的用法：前缀意为「回」，人被送回一个曾被剥夺的位置，因此这个词讲的是地位，而不是身体。

senses.title: Bricks made usable: buildings brought back
senses.definition: to repair and upgrade a building, district or facility so that it is usable again
senses.definitionCN: 修缮并提升建筑、街区或设施，使其重新可以使用
senses.example: The city plans to rehabilitate the old dock warehouses.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府计划修缮旧码头的仓库。
senses.why: The object shifts from a body to bricks, but the shape of the act is the same: something fallen into disrepair is made fit for use again.
senses.whyCN: 对象从身体换成了砖块，但动作的形状没变：一样陷入失修的东西被重新弄得合于使用。

senses.title: Land healed: an ecosystem restored
senses.titleCN: 让土地与生态恢复健康
senses.definition: to return damaged land, water or habitat to a healthy working state
senses.definitionCN: 使受损的土地、水体或栖息地回到健康的运转状态
senses.example: Volunteers rehabilitated the strip mine into a wetland.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者把露天矿坑修复成了湿地。
senses.why: Land, too, can lose its functions; the verb treats soil and water as a system whose capacities must be brought back, just as a body's are.
senses.whyCN: 土地也会失去它的功能；这个动词把土壤与水当作一套必须把能力恢复过来的系统，正如对待身体一样。

senses.title: Back in the post: an official reinstated
senses.titleCN: 让官员回到原来的职位
senses.definition: to restore an official to a post, rank or privilege that had been removed
senses.definitionCN: 使官员回到曾被撤销的职位、军衔或特权
senses.example: The board voted to rehabilitate the suspended director.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会投票决定恢复被停职董事的职位。
senses.why: When the lost thing is a seat at the table, the verb moves from bodily capacity to institutional membership, yet the 'making able again' remains.
senses.whyCN: 当失去的东西是桌边的一个席位，这个词就从身体能力转向制度中的成员资格，但「重新使有能力」这一层仍然在。

senses.title: A good name regained: ideas and works
senses.titleCN: 让作品与观念重获好评
senses.definition: to make a neglected or discredited idea, word or artwork respected again
senses.definitionCN: 使被冷落或已被否定的观念、词语或作品重新受到尊重
senses.example: Later critics rehabilitated the painter's early work.
senses.exampleCN: 后来的评论家为这位画家早期的作品恢复了声誉。
senses.why: Reputation is another capacity that can be lost, and the verb extends to anything whose good name has been taken away, from a person to a painting.
senses.whyCN: 声誉也是一种会失去的能力，这个词于是扩展到任何被夺去好评的东西，从一个人到一幅画都可以。

intro.en: Rehabilitate is not a native English construction: it comes from Medieval Latin rehabilitare, itself re- 'again, back' plus habilitare 'to make able', a verb from habilis 'apt, easily handled'. The same family contains ability and habilitate. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: rehabilitate 不是英语本土构造，而来自中世纪拉丁 rehabilitare：由表示「再、回」的前缀加 habilitare「使有能力」构成，后者又出自 habilis「易于掌握的、能干的」；同一词族还有 ability 与 habilitate。年代均为约数。

items.en: Habilis meant apt, handy or easily handled, an adjective built on habere 'to hold'; the idea was fitness for use.
items.cn: habilis 意为易于掌握的、顺手的、能干的，是由 habere「持有」构成的形容词，核心意思是「合用」。

items.en: Habilitare turned the adjective into a verb meaning to make able or to fit something for a purpose.
items.cn: habilitare 把这个形容词变成动词，意为使有能力，或使某物适合某一用途。

items.en: Re- 'again, back' was added to habilitare, and the compound was used in law and church language for restoring a person to a former right or rank.
items.cn: 表示「再、回」的前缀加在 habilitare 上，这个复合词用于法律与教会语言，指把某人恢复到原有的权利或地位。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth century, first in legal and ecclesiastical use for restoring standing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收了这个词，最初用于法律与教会语境，指恢复地位。

items.en: The medical and social senses developed later: restoring a patient's body, then preparing an offender for ordinary life.
items.cn: 医学与社会义后来才发展出来：先指恢复病人的身体，再指为罪犯重返普通生活作准备。

items.en: Contemporary usage extends the verb to buildings, districts, ecosystems and the reputation of ideas or works.
items.cn: 当代用法把这个动词扩展到建筑、街区、生态系统，以及观念或作品的声誉。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin ability stem or merely resembles the word in spelling; the second group offers near alternatives for bringing something back to a good state.
note.cn: 第一组或与本词共享拉丁「能力」词干，或只是拼写相近；第二组是「把某物带回良好状态」的近义替代。

entries.definition: To make someone able or fit; it is the base verb without the 'again' prefix, so it lacks the idea of restoring something already lost.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人有能力或合于用途；这是去掉「再」这一前缀的底层动词，因此不含「把已失去之物恢复过来」的意思。

entries.definition: To make someone weak; it is built on the same Latin ability adjective but through a prefix of removal, so it undoes capacity instead of restoring it.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人衰弱；它由同一个拉丁「能力」形容词经表「去除」的前缀构成，因此是拆掉能力而非恢复能力。

entries.definition: To sum up the main points again; it shares the re- prefix and the -ate ending but comes from Latin caput 'head', so it is merely look-alike, not a relative.
entries.definitionCN: 再次概括要点；它与本词共享「再」这一前缀和动词词尾，但出自拉丁 caput「头」，只是形近，并非同源。

entries.definition: The informal short form of rehabilitation, used chiefly for treatment programmes and centres.
entries.definitionCN: rehabilitation 的口语缩略形式，主要用于治疗项目与康复中心。

entries.definition: To bring something back to a former condition; it is broader and does not specify ability, health or standing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物带回原先的状态；范围更宽，不特别指明能力、健康或地位。

entries.definition: To put a person back into a post or right; it covers only the institutional sense of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人放回职位或权利之中；只覆盖本词的制度义。

entries.definition: To bring a person back into a group or society; it names the social goal rather than the training that achieves it.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人带回群体或社会之中；它指社会目标，而不是达成目标的训练。

entries.definition: To improve a person or institution by removing faults; for offenders it stresses moral change, while this word stresses restored capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 通过去除毛病来改善人或制度；用于罪犯时强调品德转变，而本词强调能力的恢复。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin ability stem, the real 'again' prefix and real derived words such as ability and habilitate.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「能力」词干、真实的「再」前缀，以及 ability、habilitate 等真实派生词。

normal.en: Habilis means apt or able, and the English word ability comes from the same Latin adjective.
normal.cn: habilis 意为能干的、合用的，英语 ability 正出自同一个拉丁形容词。

normal.en: The prefix re- means again or back, so the word says the ability is brought back.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「再、回」，所以这个词说的是把能力带回来。

normal.en: Habilitate is the base verb 'to make able'; rehabilitate adds the return to a former state.
normal.cn: habilitate 是底层动词「使有能力」，rehabilitate 则再加「回到原先状态」这一层。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: rehabilitate offenders, rehabilitate a building, drug rehabilitation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配展现范围：改造罪犯、修缮建筑、戒毒康复。

normal.en: The noun rehabilitation and the adjective rehabilitative both keep the idea of making fit again.
normal.cn: 名词 rehabilitation 与形容词 rehabilitative 都保留「重新弄得合用」这一意思。

abstract.en: Picture a patient gripping parallel bars and lifting one foot again.
abstract.cn: 想象病人握住平行杠，再一次把一只脚抬起来。

abstract.en: Picture a released prisoner handed a work badge at a factory gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一名获释的服刑人员在工厂门口接过工牌。

abstract.en: Picture a ruined brick warehouse with fresh scaffolding around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座破败的砖砌仓库四周搭起了新的脚手架。

examples.en: Therapy helped rehabilitate her knee after the operation.
examples.cn: 治疗帮助她的膝盖在手术后恢复功能。

examples.en: Programmes that rehabilitate offenders cost less than long sentences.

examples.cn: 该基金会希望用新证据为这个已被否定的理论恢复声誉。

root: 拉丁语表「回、再」的前缀 + habilitare「使有能力」（← habilis「易于掌握的、能干的」← habere「持有」）→ 中世纪拉丁 rehabilitare「使恢复能力与资格」；同族词有 ability、habilitate、rehabilitation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep the same movement: something that once had a capacity lost it, and the verb brings that capacity back. The capacity may be health, a movement, a place in society, a legal right, a building's usefulness, a landscape's fertility, a post or a good name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守着同一个动作：某样东西本来具有一项能力，后来失去了，这个动词把它带回来。这项能力可以是健康、一个动作、社会位置、法律权利、建筑的可用性、土地的生机、一个职位，或一份好评。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands on parallel bars, one foot lifted again after a long pause.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手扶住平行杠，停歇很久之后那只脚又一次抬起来。

branches.en: THE BODY: health returns first as a general condition, then as a single joint or step trained back into use.
branches.cn: 身体：健康先以整体状态回来，随后又以某个关节或某一步被练回可用。

branches.en: THE PLACE AMONG OTHERS: an offender is fitted for ordinary life, and an official is put back into a lost post.
branches.cn: 人群中的位置：让罪犯重新适合普通生活，也让官员回到失去的职位。

branches.en: THE LEGAL NAME: rights and reputation are handed back by formal decision.
branches.cn: 法律上的名分：权利与名誉经正式决定被归还。

branches.en: THE MADE WORLD: bricks and land are repaired until they can work again.
branches.cn: 人造与自然之物：砖石与土地被修整到能重新运转。

branches.en: THE GOOD NAME OF THINGS: even a discredited idea or artwork can be given its standing back.
branches.cn: 事物的好评：连一个被否定的观念或作品，也能重新得到它应有的地位。

intro.en: Rehabilitate is assembled from Latin pieces: a prefix of return, an adjective stem meaning able, and a verb ending, with English noun and adjective suffixes added later.
intro.cn: rehabilitate 由拉丁成分拼成：一个表示「回、再」的前缀、一个意为「能干」的形容词词干，以及一个动词词尾；英语的名词与形容词后缀是后来才加上去的。

latinIntro.en: Latin habilis 'apt' came from habere 'to hold', and it also produced habilitare, rehabilitare and the English word ability.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 habilis「合用的、能干的」出自 habere「持有」，它还衍生出 habilitare、rehabilitare 以及英语的 ability。

dict_mnemonic.text: elicitation ＝ elicit（引出）＋ -ation（名词后缀，表行为／过程）＝「引出这件事」。动词 elicit ＝ e-（向外）＋ licit（来自拉丁 lacere「引诱」，注意不是 licere「允许」）＝用诱饵把东西引出来。关键辨析：elicit 与 illicit 读音几乎一样，但 illicit 是形容词「非法的」（il- 不 ＋ licit 合法），拼写差一个字母，考试常考。三个高频术语直接背：requirements elicitation 需求获取（软件工程）、knowledge elicitation 知识获取（专家系统）、elicitation technique 启发式提问（语言教学）。近义 extraction 靠用力拔（extract a tooth 拔牙），evocation 靠唤起记忆情感，prompting 靠给提示。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）＋ lacere（引诱）→ elicere（引出）→ elicit ＋ -ation → elicitation（引出；诱出）

definition_zh: 耕作的；人工栽培的；（人）有教养的；后天培养出来的
definition_en: (of land) prepared and used for crops; (of plants or organisms) grown under human control; (of a person, taste or skill) developed by deliberate training
core_image: 一块行距笔直的田，作物比野地里的同类更壮；田边站着一位举止从容、说话有分寸的人
scene: 田里的行距被绳子量得笔直，苗高一致，杂草清得干净，主人说话轻缓而有分寸。 The cultivated field yields more than the wild plot beside it.
sceneCN: 这里指「经人工耕作与照管的」（第 1 个义项：耕地）；句意为这块耕作过的田比旁边的荒地收成更多。

pos.zh: 耕作的；人工栽培的；有教养的；后天培养的

cultivate + -ar（园艺名词后缀）→ 栽培品种

senses.title: Land that has been tilled
senses.definition: describing land that has been broken, worked and used for crops rather than left wild
senses.definitionCN: 描述经过翻耕、整治并用于种植作物、而非任其荒芜的土地
senses.example: Cultivated land stops where the slope becomes too steep.
senses.exampleCN: 耕地到坡度过陡处为止。
senses.why: The past participle of cultivate turns the action into a state, so land carries the mark of having been worked.
senses.whyCN: cultivate 的过去分词把动作转为状态，因此土地带着「已被耕作」的印记。

senses.title: Field crops grown on purpose
senses.titleCN: 有目的种植的田间作物
senses.definition: describing crops that people have planted and tended in fields, as opposed to wild plants
senses.definitionCN: 描述人们种在田里并加以照管的作物，与野生植物相对
senses.example: Cultivated wheat shatters less easily than its wild ancestor.
senses.exampleCN: 栽培小麦比其野生祖先更不易落粒。
senses.why: Once a plant depends on people for sowing and weeding, it is described by the participle of the care it receives.
senses.whyCN: 一旦植物依赖人播种与除草，就用它所受照管的分词来描述。

senses.title: Garden plants from chosen stock
senses.titleCN: 由选育种苗栽培的园艺植物
senses.definition: describing ornamental or fruit plants raised from selected stock in a garden or nursery
senses.definitionCN: 描述在园圃或苗圃中由选育种苗育成的观赏或果树植物
senses.example: The cultivated rose has lost the scent of the wild briar.
senses.exampleCN: 栽培玫瑰已失去野蔷薇的香气。
senses.why: Garden plants are the clearest case of human choice: the stock itself, not only the soil, has been selected.
senses.whyCN: 园艺植物是人类选择最清楚的例子：被选的不仅是土壤，还有种苗本身。

senses.title: Grown in a laboratory medium
senses.titleCN: 在实验室培养基中培养的
senses.definition: describing microorganisms or cells grown under controlled laboratory conditions
senses.definitionCN: 描述在受控实验室条件下培养的微生物或细胞
senses.example: Cultivated cells behave differently from cells taken straight from tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 培养细胞的行为与直接从组织取出的细胞不同。
senses.why: Laboratory growth is deliberate cultivation, so the participle marks anything raised in a dish rather than in a body.
senses.whyCN: 实验室培养是有意的培育，因此这个分词标记一切在培养皿而非体内长成的东西。

senses.title: A person polished by education
senses.titleCN: 受过教育而举止得体的人
senses.definition: describing a person whose manners, speech and judgment have been refined by education and good company
senses.definitionCN: 描述举止、言谈与判断经教育与良好交往而变得优雅的人
senses.example: He was a cultivated man who never raised his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他是一位有教养的男士，从不提高嗓门。
senses.why: The agricultural metaphor turns social: a person, like a garden, can be tended into a better shape.
senses.whyCN: 农业比喻转向社会：人如园子，可以被照料成更好的形状。

senses.title: A taste acquired by exposure
senses.definition: describing an appreciation that has been learned through repeated exposure rather than possessed naturally
senses.definitionCN: 描述经反复接触而学会、而非天生拥有的鉴赏力
senses.example: Her cultivated taste for opera began with film scores.
senses.exampleCN: 她对歌剧的后天品味始于电影配乐。
senses.why: Taste is not planted in a person at birth; it is grown by exposure, which is why the participle fits.
senses.whyCN: 品味并非与生俱来，而是靠接触长成，因此适合用这个分词。

senses.title: A skill built by training
senses.definition: describing an ability developed through deliberate practice rather than given by nature
senses.definitionCN: 描述经刻意练习发展出来、而非天赋所赐的能力
senses.example: His cultivated voice carried across the hall without strain.
senses.exampleCN: 他训练有素的嗓音毫不费力地传遍大厅。
senses.why: The contrast with native gifts is the point: what is cultivated was not there to begin with.
senses.whyCN: 与天赋的对照正是要点：被培养出来的东西起初并不存在。

senses.title: A relationship kept up on purpose
senses.definition: describing a friendship or contact that is deliberately maintained over time
senses.definitionCN: 描述长期被有意维持的友谊或人脉
senses.example: Their cultivated ties survived two changes of government.
senses.exampleCN: 他们经营的关系挺过了两次政府更替。
senses.why: A tie that is kept up is literally cultivated, and the participle records the effort behind its survival.
senses.whyCN: 被维持的关系确实是「被栽培」的，这个分词记录了它存活背后的投入。

intro.en: Cultivated is the past participle of cultivate used as an adjective. The verb came from Medieval Latin cultivare, and the adjectival use is recorded from the sixteenth century, with the social sense following in the eighteenth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cultivated 是 cultivate 的过去分词作形容词。这个动词来自中世纪拉丁 cultivare，形容词用法在十六世纪已有记录，社会义则在十八世纪出现。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cultivare meant to till or tend; its past participle cultivatus supplied the form that English turned into an adjective.
items.cn: cultivare 意为耕作或照管；其过去分词 cultivatus 提供了英语转化为形容词的形式。

items.en: The first English adjectival uses describe land and plants that have been worked, keeping close to the participle's literal force.
items.cn: 最早的英语形容词用法描述被耕作过的土地与植物，贴近分词的字面力量。

items.en: Enlightenment writing applied the word to people, manners and taste, so a cultivated man became one whose mind had been tended.
items.cn: 启蒙时期的写作把这个词用于人、举止与品味，于是有教养的人成了心智受过照料的人。

items.en: Microbiology adopted the participle for organisms grown in a medium, giving the word a second technical life.
items.cn: 微生物学采用这个分词指在培养基中生长的生物，使这个词获得第二种技术生命。

items.en: Modern English keeps both readings side by side: cultivated land and a cultivated accent, one literal and one figurative.
items.cn: 现代英语把两种读法并置：耕作的田地与有教养的口音，一为字面，一为比喻。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): dictionaries date the adjectival use only approximately, and the exact path from agricultural to social meaning is not documented in detail.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：辞书对形容词用法的年代只有约数，从农业义到社会义的具体路径也缺乏详细记载。

note.en: Group one holds participles and adjectives from the same root that are easily swapped; group two holds adjectives for a polished or trained person or thing.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该词根、极易互换的分词与形容词；第二组是描述「被磨得精致、受过训练」的人或物的形容词。

entries.definition: From culture, not cultivate: it can mean refined in manners or grown in a medium, as in cultured pearls.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 culture 而非 cultivate：既可指举止优雅，也可指在培养基中生长，如养殖珍珠。

entries.definition: The plain opposite: land never worked, or a person without training; it denies the participle rather than naming a new quality.
entries.definitionCN: 直接的反义：从未耕作的土地，或未受训练的人；它否定该分词，而不命名新性质。

entries.definition: Able to be cultivated, whether or not it actually is; cultivated land has already been worked.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被耕作，无论实际是否已耕；而 cultivated 的土地已经耕过。

entries.definition: The noun for a way of life or a growth medium; it names the field, while cultivated describes what came out of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指生活方式或培养基的名词；它命名场域，而 cultivated 描述从中产生的结果。

entries.definition: Purified or made elegant by taking away what is coarse; cultivated stresses the care that grew the quality, refined stresses the removal of roughness.
entries.definitionCN: 通过去除粗劣部分而变得纯净或优雅；cultivated 强调培育出该品质的照料，refined 强调去除粗糙。

entries.definition: Having received formal instruction; cultivated is broader and includes manners and taste acquired outside school.
entries.definitionCN: 受过正式教育；cultivated 范围更广，包含在校外获得的举止与品味。

entries.definition: Made manageable by domestication; it applies to animals and wildness, not to land care or personal polish.
entries.definitionCN: 通过驯化而变得可控；适用于动物与野性，不用于土地照料或个人修养。

entries.definition: Carefully prepared for a particular role or appearance; cultivated can be wider and less career-directed.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定角色或外表精心准备；cultivated 可以更宽，未必指向职业。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: cultivate plus -ed: the action is finished, and what remains is a state.
normal.cn: cultivate 加 -ed：动作已完成，留下的是状态。

normal.en: The family runs cultivate, cultivation, cultivator, cultivable, cultivar, cultivated.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cultivate、cultivation、cultivator、cultivable、cultivar、cultivated。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: cultivated land, cultivated plants, a cultivated man.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：耕地、栽培植物、有教养的人。

normal.en: The laboratory says cultivated cells; the garden says cultivated roses.
normal.cn: 实验室说培养细胞，园子说栽培玫瑰。

normal.en: The contrast is always with wild, native or untrained.
normal.cn: 它的对照项总是野生、天生或未受训练。

abstract.en: Picture a field whose straight rows are themselves a record of years of decisions.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田，笔直的行距本身就是多年决断的记录。

abstract.en: Picture a voice that has been sanded smooth by decades of practice.
abstract.cn: 想象一副被数十年练习打磨光滑的嗓音。

abstract.en: Picture a friendship with visible stitching, mended each time it frayed.
abstract.cn: 想象一段带着明显针脚、每次磨损都被补好的友谊。

examples.en: The cultivated slope supports three crops a year, while the wild one supports none.
examples.cn: 这块被耕作的坡地一年能种三季，而荒地一季也没有。

examples.en: Cultivated mushrooms are grown on sterilised straw.
examples.cn: 栽培蘑菇种在消过毒的秸秆上。

examples.en: His cultivated manner made even bad news easier to hear.
examples.cn: 他有教养的举止让坏消息也变得容易听进去。

dict_mnemonic.text: cultivate（耕作、培养）+ -ed（已完成）→ 已被耕过的、已被培养成的；土地、植物、细胞、人与品味都能用。

root: cultivate + -ed；cultivate 来自中世纪拉丁 cultivare「耕作」，再上溯 cultiva「耕过的土地」与 colere「耕作、居住、敬奉」，更早词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one participle: what people have worked on carries the mark of that work, whether it is soil, a crop, a cell, a person, a taste, a skill or a tie.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个分词展开：凡被人经手照料过的东西都带着那份劳作的印记，无论是土壤、作物、细胞、人、品味、技能还是关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field with straight rows and a person with measured speech are both surfaces that show the marks of long care.
core.cn: 核心意象：行距笔直的田与说话有分寸的人，都是显示出长期照料痕迹的表面。

branches.en: THE GROUND: the participle's oldest and most literal use.
branches.cn: 土地：这个分词最古老、最字面的用法。

branches.en: THE PLANTS: field crops and garden stock, both chosen and tended by people.
branches.cn: 植物：田间作物与园中种苗，都由人选择并照料。

branches.en: THE DISH: laboratory growth is cultivation made visible under glass.
branches.cn: 培养皿：实验室里的生长是隔着玻璃可见的培育。

branches.en: THE PERSON AND THE SKILL: polish of manner and training of ability.
branches.cn: 人与技能：举止的优雅与能力的训练。

branches.en: TASTE AND TIES: both are acquired slowly and kept by repetition.
branches.cn: 品味与关系：两者都缓慢获得，并靠重复维持。

intro.en: Cultivated is a participle-adjective, so its parts are the verb cultivate and the ending -ed, with the rest of the family built from the same root.
intro.cn: cultivated 是分词形容词，其组成部分是动词 cultivate 与词尾 -ed，词族其余成员也由同一词根构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin cultivare supplies the verb; the English ending -ed marks the completed state, while -ation, -or, -able and -ar build the related family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cultivare 提供动词；英语词尾 -ed 标记完成状态，而 -ation、-or、-able 与 -ar 构成相关词族。

items.example: People cultivate the plant for its oil.
items.exampleCN: 人们为取其油而栽培这种植物。

items.example: The ending turns an action into a finished state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动作变成完成状态。

items.meaning: the work of tilling or tending
items.example: Cultivation began with the first ploughing.
items.exampleCN: 培育从第一次犁地开始。

items.structure: cultivate + -or (one who acts or a tool)
items.example: The cultivator passes between the rows.
items.exampleCN: 中耕机在行间穿行。

items.example: The cultivable strip is only ten metres wide.
items.exampleCN: 可耕种的地带只有十米宽。

items.example: Each cultivar ripens at a different time.
items.exampleCN: 每个品种的成熟时间都不同。

items.example: Uncultivated ground held the old wildflowers.
items.exampleCN: 未开垦的地里留着旧日的野花。

items.example: The recultivated strip yielded a poor first crop.
items.exampleCN: 重新耕作的地带第一季收成很差。

latinEntries.structure: cultivare, cultivavi, cultivatum (verb, first conjugation, Medieval Latin)

definition_zh: 以分析的方式；从分析上；通过对整体的拆解；（数学）解析地（求得精确解）
definition_en: in a manner that uses analysis, by breaking a whole into its parts, or by means of an exact analytical method rather than an approximate one
core_image: 不是绕着整台机器猜，而是把零件逐一摊开、顺着咬合处往下查
scene: 工程师没有画图试凑，而是在纸上解出方程，直接得到曲线的精确交点。 Instead of plotting and guessing, the engineer solves the equation analytically and gets the exact intersection.
sceneCN: 这里 analytically 是「解析地、用精确解法」（第 9 个义项：用解析方法求得闭式精确解，而不是数值近似）；句意：工程师没有画图试凑，而是在纸上解析求解，直接得到精确交点。场景要点：草稿纸上的方程、被划掉的数值表、铅笔写出的根号解、合上的计算器。

pos.zh: 以分析的方式；从分析上；解析地

collocations.zh: 用分析的方法处理问题
解析地求解（求得精确解）
对某事件作分析性考察

derivatives.zh: 分析的；善于分析的；解析的
分析的；解析的（同义变体）

senses.title: In an analytical manner
senses.definition: in a way that uses analysis rather than intuition, habit, or mere description
senses.definitionCN: 以使用分析、而非直觉、习惯或单纯描述的方式
senses.example: The committee examined the proposal analytically, point by point.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会逐点地、以分析的方式审查了这项提案。
senses.why: The -ly suffix turns the adjective into a manner adverb: whatever analytical describes, analytically tells you how it is done. The default sense is simply 'by analysis', with no special field attached.
senses.whyCN: -ly 后缀把形容词变成方式副词：analytical 描述什么，analytically 就说明这件事是怎样做的。默认义项就是“通过分析”，不附带特定领域。

senses.title: By taking the problem apart
senses.definition: by separating a complex problem into smaller parts and dealing with each part in turn
senses.definitionCN: 把复杂问题拆成较小部分，并依次处理每一部分
senses.example: Instead of reacting to the whole crisis, they worked analytically through each cause.
senses.exampleCN: 他们没有对整个危机作出反应，而是分析性地逐一处理每个成因。
senses.why: This makes the core image explicit: the whole is loosened before anything is said about it. The adverb marks the order of work — parts first, whole later — rather than the topic.
senses.whyCN: 这里把核心意象说清楚了：在谈论整体之前，先把它松开。副词标记的是工作的顺序——先部分、后整体——而不是话题。

senses.title: With step-by-step reasoning
senses.definition: by reasoning from premises to conclusion in explicit, checkable steps
senses.definitionCN: 以明确、可核查的步骤从前提到结论进行推理
senses.example: She argued analytically, showing how each claim followed from the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 她以分析的方式论证，说明每个论断如何从证据推出。
senses.why: Analysis produces parts, and reasoning links them. When the links are laid out one by one, the manner is analytical in the argumentative sense, close to 'logically' but with the added image of decomposed steps.
senses.whyCN: 分析产生部分，推理连接部分。当这些连接被逐一摆出时，这种方式就是论证意义上的 analytical，接近 logically，但多了一层“步骤被拆开”的意象。

senses.title: By chemical analysis
senses.definition: by means of analytical chemistry, identifying or measuring the components of a sample
senses.definitionCN: 借助分析化学，鉴定或测量样品的组成成分
senses.example: The water was tested analytically for lead and nitrate.
senses.exampleCN: 水样经过分析检测，测定了铅和硝酸盐。
senses.why: In the laboratory the loosening is literal: reagents and instruments separate the sample into measurable components. Analytically here tells you the method used, not the frame of mind.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，松开是字面意义上的：试剂与仪器把样品分离成可测量的成分。这里的 analytically 说明所用方法，而不是心态。

senses.title: From an analytical discipline's perspective
senses.definition: in the manner or perspective of an analytical discipline, such as linguistics or philosophy, rather than a descriptive or historical one
senses.definitionCN: 以分析学科（如语言学或哲学）的方式或视角，而非描述性或历史性视角
senses.example: The novel has been studied analytically by linguists interested in tense.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说被关注时态的语言学家以分析的方式研究过。
senses.why: A discipline trains its members in a method, and the adverb then names the perspective they bring. The same object can be studied historically, descriptively or analytically; the last one asks how its parts are put together.
senses.whyCN: 一个学科用某种方法训练成员，副词随后命名他们带来的视角。同一个对象可以被历史地、描述地或分析地研究；最后一种追问它的各部分如何拼合。

senses.title: Listening in a probing way
senses.titleCN: 以探究、拆解的方式倾听
senses.definition: of a person, in a manner that sorts claims from evidence and tests what is being said
senses.definitionCN: 指人以区分论断与证据、检验对方所说内容的方式
senses.example: He listened analytically, separating what was known from what was assumed.
senses.exampleCN: 他以分析的方式倾听，把已知与假定分开。
senses.why: When the method becomes a personal habit, the adverb describes behaviour rather than procedure. The listener is not cold; he is dividing the speech into claims that can be checked.
senses.whyCN: 当方法变成个人习惯，副词描述的就是行为而非程序。这样的听者并不冷漠；他只是把对方的话分成可核查的论断。

senses.title: In a dissecting written style
senses.definition: of writing or speech, in a style that lays out components and relations instead of narrating or describing
senses.definitionCN: 指写作或言谈以铺陈成分与关系、而非叙述或描写的风格
senses.example: The report describes the policy analytically, with each assumption exposed.
senses.exampleCN: 报告以分析的方式描述这项政策，把每个假设都暴露出来。
senses.why: A style can carry a method. When the sentences are arranged by parts and relations rather than by time or scene, the writing is said to proceed analytically; the adverb modifies the texture of the text.
senses.whyCN: 风格可以承载方法。当句子按部分与关系、而不是按时间或场景排列时，这种写作就被说成以分析的方式展开；副词修饰的是文本的质地。

senses.title: In the manner of analytic philosophy
senses.definition: by the methods of analytic philosophy, clarifying concepts and arguments through logical and linguistic analysis
senses.definitionCN: 以分析哲学的方法，通过逻辑与语言分析澄清概念和论证
senses.example: The question was treated analytically, beginning with the meaning of 'cause'.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题被以分析的方式处理，先从“原因”一词的意义开始。
senses.why: Here the adverb invokes a named tradition. The loosening is applied to concepts: a word is separated into its uses, and a question is answered only after its terms are clarified.
senses.whyCN: 这里的副词唤起一个有名有姓的传统。松开被施于概念：一个词被分成各种用法，问题只有在术语被澄清之后才被回答。

senses.title: By an exact mathematical solution
senses.definition: in mathematics, by obtaining an exact closed-form solution through analysis, as opposed to a numerical approximation
senses.definitionCN: 在数学中，通过分析得到闭式精确解，而不是数值近似
senses.example: The equation can be solved analytically, so no iteration is needed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方程可以解析求解，因此不需要迭代。
senses.why: In this technical contrast, analysis means deriving the answer from the structure of the equation, not sampling numbers. The adverb marks the route to the result: exact derivation rather than stepwise approximation.
senses.whyCN: 在这一技术性对照里，分析指从方程的结构推出答案，而不是取数值样本。副词标记通往结果的路线：精确推导，而非逐步逼近。

intro.en: Analytically is analytical plus the adverbial suffix -ly. Analytical came into English in the 1520s from Medieval Latin analyticus, from Greek analytikos, whose base analyein means 'to loosen, release' (ana- 'up, back' + lysis 'a loosening'). The adverb therefore says 'in the manner of that loosening'. The suffix -ly is native English, not Greek or Latin: it goes back to Old English -lice and Proto-Germanic *-liko-, cognate with lich 'body' and like.
intro.cn: analytically 是 analytical 加副词后缀 -ly。analytical 于 16 世纪 20 年代从中世纪拉丁语 analyticus 进入英语，再上溯希腊语 analytikos，其词基 analyein 意为“松开、释放”（ana-“向上、向后”加 lysis“松开”）。因此副词说的是“以那种松开的方式”。后缀 -ly 是英语本族成分，不是希腊语或拉丁语：它上溯古英语 -lice 与原始日耳曼语 *-liko-，与 lich“身体”和 like 同源。

items.en: The base adjective analytical is first recorded in English as 'employing analytic methods', via Medieval Latin analyticus from Greek analytikos. The adverb depends on this adjective, so its history begins here.
items.cn: 基础形容词 analytical 最早记录于 16 世纪 20 年代，意为“使用分析方法的”，经中世纪拉丁语 analyticus 来自希腊语 analytikos。副词依附于这个形容词，因此它的历史从这里开始。

items.en: The adverbial -ly comes from Old English -lice, from Proto-Germanic *-liko-, and is cognate with lich 'body' and identical with like (adj.). The modern form emerged in late Middle English, probably under the influence of Old Norse -liga.
items.cn: 副词后缀 -ly 来自古英语 -lice，再上溯原始日耳曼语 *-liko-，与 lich“身体”同源，并与形容词 like 同形。现代形式出现于中古英语晚期，可能受古北欧语 -liga 的影响。

items.en: Analytically is the regular manner adverb from analytical. The etymonline entry for the adverb itself could not be retrieved for this batch because the site returned a bot-check page; the analytical entry lists 'Related: Analytically' but gives no separate date, so the first recorded date of the adverb remains uncertain (unconfirmed here).
items.cn: analytically 是由 analytical 规则构成的方式副词。本批检索时，etymonline 的副词条目因网站返回人机验证页而未能取得；analytical 条目只列出“Related: Analytically”，未给单独年代，因此该副词的首见年代在本批中仍属存疑（未获确认）。

items.en: The adverb spreads with the sciences. Mathematics contrasts solving a problem analytically (exact derivation) with solving it numerically, and analytical chemistry makes 'tested analytically' a laboratory phrase.
items.cn: 这个副词随科学扩展。数学把“解析地求解”（精确推导）与“数值地求解”相对，分析化学则让“以分析方式检测”成为实验室用语。

items.en: Academic English uses analytically for the perspective of a discipline: a text can be read analytically rather than historically or descriptively. Analytic philosophy and analytical psychology supply two named traditions in which the adverb is routine.
items.cn: 学术英语用 analytically 表示某一学科的视角：一部文本可以被分析地阅读，而不是历史地或描述地阅读。分析哲学与分析心理学提供了两个有名有姓的传统，副词在其中是常规用法。

items.en: The adverb is a manner word, not a separate lexical root. It must not be confused with analogically, which comes from analogy and logos 'ratio', or with analytics, a data noun from analysis + -ics. Both look close and neither shares the lysis element.
items.cn: 这个副词是方式词，不是独立的词根。它不能与 analogically 混淆——后者来自 analogy 与 logos“比例”；也不能与 analytics 混淆——后者是 analysis + -ics 的数据名词。两者形近，且都不含 lysis 成分。

note.en: The first group separates the adjective base, its short variant, the data noun analytics and the look-alike analogically; the second compares adverbs that also describe careful thought but do not mean 'by decomposition'.
note.cn: 第一组区分形容词基础、其短变体、数据名词 analytics，以及形似而不同源的 analogically；第二组比较同样描述细致思考、却不含“拆解”之意的副词。

entries.definition: using analysis. It describes a method, mind or account, while analytically describes how an action is performed.
entries.definitionCN: 使用分析的。它描述方法、头脑或论述，而 analytically 描述动作怎样进行。

entries.definition: the shorter form of the same adjective, common in terms such as analytic geometry. It is not the adverb and cannot replace analytically.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的较短形式，常见于 analytic geometry 等术语。它不是副词，不能替换 analytically。

entries.definition: the systematic analysis of data. It is a noun from analysis + -ics, not an adverb and not the plural of analytic.
entries.definitionCN: 对数据的系统分析。它是 analysis + -ics 的名词，不是副词，也不是 analytic 的复数。

entries.definition: by analogy, or in a manner based on analogy. It looks almost identical in shape but comes from logos 'ratio', not from lysis 'a loosening'.
entries.definitionCN: 以类比的方式，或基于类比的。它的词形几乎相同，却来自 logos“比例”，而不是 lysis“松开”。

entries.definition: in a way that follows the rules of valid reasoning. Logically stresses the correctness of inference, while analytically stresses the decomposition that supplies the steps.
entries.definitionCN: 以遵循有效推理规则的方式。logically 强调推理的正确性，而 analytically 强调提供这些步骤的拆解。

entries.definition: in an ordered, methodical way that covers everything according to a system. Systematically can be mechanical, while analytically requires taking the subject apart.
entries.definitionCN: 按体系有序、周全地。systematically 可以是机械的，而 analytically 要求把对象拆开。

entries.definition: in a careful, step-by-step manner. Methodically stresses orderly procedure, not the separation of a whole into parts.
entries.definitionCN: 以谨慎、逐步的方式。methodically 强调有序程序，而不强调把整体分成部分。

entries.definition: in a way that examines and judges merits and faults. Critically adds evaluation, while analytically can remain a neutral dissection.
entries.definitionCN: 以审视并评判优缺点的方式。critically 多了一层评价，而 analytically 可以是中性的剖析。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: analytical + -ly, the native English -ly from Old English -lice, and the two look-alikes built on logos and on -ics.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：analytical + -ly、来自古英语 -lice 的本族后缀 -ly，以及两个建立在 logos 和 -ics 上的形似词。

normal.en: analytical + -ly: the suffix changes an adjective into a manner adverb, so analytically means 'in that analytical way'.
normal.cn: analytical + -ly：后缀把形容词变成方式副词，所以 analytically 意为“以那种分析的方式”。

normal.en: -ly is native English, from Old English -lice, cognate with lich 'body' and like. It is not a Greek suffix, even when the base is Greek.
normal.cn: -ly 是英语本族后缀，来自古英语 -lice，与 lich“身体”和 like 同源。即使词基是希腊语，它也不是希腊后缀。

normal.en: The base family: analytical 1520s, analysis 1580s, analyze c.1600. The adverb rides on the adjective.
normal.cn: 基础词族：analytical 是 16 世纪 20 年代，analysis 是 80 年代，analyze 约 1600 年。副词依附于形容词。

normal.en: Mathematics separates 'solve analytically' (exact) from 'solve numerically' (approximate).
normal.cn: 数学把“解析地求解”（精确）与“数值地求解”（近似）分开。

normal.en: analogically is built on logos 'ratio'; analytics is built on -ics. Neither contains lysis 'a loosening'.
normal.cn: analogically 建立在 logos“比例”上；analytics 建立在 -ics 上。两者都不含 lysis“松开”。

abstract.en: Picture a hand loosening a knot: the rope does not disappear, it separates into strands that can be followed one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在松开一个结：绳子没有消失，而是分成可以逐根追踪的股。

abstract.en: The same loosening can be done in thought, in argument, in a lab, in a text or in an equation. The adverb says the action is done that way, not that the topic is analysis.
abstract.cn: 同一种松开可以在思考、论证、实验室、文本或方程中进行。副词说的是动作以这种方式完成，而不是话题属于分析。

abstract.en: In mathematics the manner becomes a choice of route: exact derivation through the structure, instead of walking numerically toward an answer.
abstract.cn: 在数学里，这种方式变成路线选择：顺着结构作精确推导，而不是用数值一步步逼近答案。

examples.en: She prefers to think analytically before making a decision.
examples.cn: 她喜欢在作决定之前先分析性地思考。

examples.en: The two compounds were compared analytically in the same laboratory.
examples.cn: 这两种化合物在同一实验室里经过分析比较。

examples.en: The model can be solved analytically, which makes it useful for teaching.
examples.cn: 这个模型可以解析求解，因此很适合教学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安纳利替扣里」——安纳利把扣子拆开后，一颗一颗地查进去 → analytically 以分析的方式

root: 由形容词 analytical 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，字面是“以分析的方式”；analytical 又来自希腊语 analytikos“善于拆解的”，其词基 analyein 意为“松开、拆解”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of analytically, all one manner: something is done by loosening a whole and working through its parts. The field can be a problem, an argument, a lab sample, a discipline, a listener, a text, a philosophical tradition or an equation.
sensesIntro.cn: analytically 的九个义项都来自同一种方式：把整体松开，再顺着各部分去做。领域可以是问题、论证、实验室样品、学科、听者、文本、哲学传统或方程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a knot is loosened and its strands are followed one by one.
core.cn: 核心意象：把结松开，再一股一股地顺着查下去。

branches.en: GENERAL MANNER: the method itself, the order of taking a problem apart, and the dissecting texture of a text.
branches.cn: 一般方式：方法本身、拆解问题的顺序，以及文本的剖析质地。

branches.en: REASONING AND THE MIND: explicit steps in argument, and a listener who separates claims from evidence.
branches.cn: 推理与头脑：论证中的明确步骤，以及把论断与证据分开的听者。

branches.en: DISCIPLINES: a sample tested in the lab, and a text studied from an analytical perspective.
branches.cn: 学科：实验室里被检测的样品，以及从分析视角被研究的文本。

branches.en: PHILOSOPHY: concepts are clarified by separating a word into its uses before a question is answered.
branches.cn: 哲学：在回答问题之前，先把一个词分成各种用法以澄清概念。

branches.en: MATHEMATICS: the manner becomes a route, exact derivation instead of numerical approximation.
branches.cn: 数学：方式变成路线，精确推导而非数值近似。

intro.en: Analytically is analytical + -ly, and analytical is analytic + -al. The Greek-Latin core is ana- 'up, back' + lysis 'a loosening'; the English -ly is a native adverbial suffix from Old English -lice. So the word mixes a borrowed Greek base with a native English ending, which is why its form is so regular.
intro.cn: analytically 是 analytical + -ly，而 analytical 是 analytic + -al。希腊—拉丁内核是 ana-“向上、向后”加 lysis“松开”；英语的 -ly 是来自古英语 -lice 的本族副词后缀。因此这个词是 borrowed 的希腊词基加本族英语词尾，这也解释了它为何形式如此规则。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is analyticus (Medieval Latin) and analysis (from Greek). The deepest elements, analyein and lysis, are Greek. There is no separate Latin adverb here: the -ly ending is English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁来源是 analyticus（中世纪拉丁语）与 analysis（来自希腊语）。最深层的成分 analyein 与 lysis 是希腊语。这里没有独立的拉丁副词：-ly 词尾是英语的。

items.meaningCN: 以分析的方式（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: They reviewed the data analytically.
items.exampleCN: 他们以分析的方式审查了数据。

items.meaningCN: 分析的；使用分析的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: An analytical reading reveals the hidden premise.
items.exampleCN: 分析性的阅读揭示了隐藏的前提。

items.example: Analytic geometry is taught in the first year.
items.exampleCN: 解析几何在第一年讲授。

items.meaning: the breaking up of a whole into parts
items.meaningCN: 把整体分解成部分；分析
items.example: The analysis revealed three separate causes.
items.exampleCN: 分析揭示了三个各自独立的成因。

items.meaning: to break something down to understand it
items.example: The software analyzes the sentence structure.
items.exampleCN: 该软件分析句子结构。

items.example: The analyst wrote a short report.
items.exampleCN: 分析师写了一份简短报告。

items.meaningCN: 数据分析（作为实践或领域）
items.example: Analytics showed a drop in traffic.
items.exampleCN: 数据分析显示流量下降。

items.structure: Old English -lice < Proto-Germanic *-liko-, cognate with lich and like
items.meaning: adverbial suffix meaning 'in the manner of'
items.meaningCN: 副词后缀，意为“以……的方式”（本族英语成分）
items.example: The suffix turns analytical into analytically.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 analytical 变成 analytically。

items.meaning: by analogy; a different root from analytically
items.meaningCN: 以类比的方式（来自 logos，与 analytically 不同源）
items.example: The two cases were treated analogically.
items.exampleCN: 两个案例被以类比的方式处理。

latinEntries.structure: Latin from Greek analysis, ana- + lysis
Greek verb: ana- (up, back) + lyein (to unfasten)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 松开；释放；使自由（希腊语来源）

definition_zh: 股东；持有公司股份的人或机构
definition_en: a person or organization that owns shares in a company
core_image: 公司被切成许多等份，一只手握住其中一份并举起表决卡
scene: 年度股东大会开始前，一位持有公司股份的人翻看表决材料，抬头询问董事会为何没有派发利润。 The shareholder asked the board why profits were not paid out.
sceneCN: 这里指「持有公司股份的人或机构」，对应第 1 个义项：公司股份的持有人；句意为这位股东问董事会为什么利润没有分派出去。画面要点：会议室长桌、表决材料、持股凭证。

pos.zh: 股东；股份持有人（可指个人、基金或其他机构）

collocations.zh: 多数股东；持股过半的股东
积极干预公司治理的股东

derivatives.zh: 多处持股；持有的股份总额

senses.title: Owner of part of a company
senses.titleCN: 持有公司一部分股份的人
senses.definition: a person who owns one or more shares in a company
senses.definitionCN: 持有一家公司一份或多份股份的人
senses.example: Every shareholder receives a copy of the annual report.
senses.exampleCN: 每位股东都会收到一份年度报告。
senses.why: Share names a divided portion of something and holder names the one who keeps it, so the word literally means the keeper of a portion of the company.
senses.whyCN: share 指从整体中分出的一份，holder 指持有者，所以这个词字面上就是「公司某一份的持有者」。

senses.title: Holder of a controlling stake
senses.titleCN: 持股足以控制公司的股东
senses.definition: a shareholder whose stake is large enough to direct the company
senses.definitionCN: 持股比例大到足以左右公司决策的股东
senses.example: The controlling shareholder can appoint most of the board.
senses.exampleCN: 控股股东能够任命董事会的大部分成员。
senses.why: The same ownership relation is read by weight: when the held portion passes a threshold, the keeper of that portion gains the power to steer the whole.
senses.whyCN: 同样的持有关系按分量来读：当握有的那一份越过某个门槛，这一份的持有者就获得了左右整体的权力。

senses.title: Holder of a small stake
senses.definition: a shareholder whose stake is too small to influence control
senses.definitionCN: 持股比例较小、无法左右控制权的股东
senses.example: Minority shareholders joined forces to block the sale.
senses.exampleCN: 少数股东联合起来阻止这笔出售。
senses.why: Minority keeps the core meaning and adds scale: the portion is real but its weight is light, so the owner has a claim without command.
senses.whyCN: minority 保留核心义而补充了分量：那一份确实存在，但分量很轻，于是持有者有收益主张却没有指挥权。

senses.title: Institution as owner
senses.titleCN: 以机构身份持股的股东
senses.definition: a fund, pension scheme, insurer or other organization that holds shares
senses.definitionCN: 基金、养老金、保险公司等持有股份的组织
senses.example: Institutional shareholders pressed for clearer climate disclosures.
senses.exampleCN: 机构股东要求更清晰的气候信息披露。
senses.why: The holder here is not a single person but an organization acting as one legal owner, so the core sense is applied to a collective body.
senses.whyCN: 这里的持有者不是单个自然人，而是作为一个法律主体行事的组织，核心义因此落在一个集体身上。

senses.title: Private individual as owner
senses.titleCN: 以个人身份持股的股东
senses.definition: an ordinary private investor who owns shares directly
senses.definitionCN: 直接持有股份的普通个人投资者
senses.example: Retail shareholders often hold only a few dozen shares.
senses.exampleCN: 个人股东往往只持有几十股。
senses.why: Retail marks the opposite of institutional: the same legal relation is held in a private hand and on a small scale.
senses.whyCN: retail 标出与机构相反的一面：同样的法律关系握在私人手里，规模也小。

senses.title: Owner as a claim on value
senses.definition: the owner whose financial interest a company is said to serve
senses.definitionCN: 公司被说成应当为其财务利益服务的持股方
senses.example: The takeover was justified as a way to maximize shareholder value.
senses.exampleCN: 这场收购被辩解为最大化股东价值的手段。
senses.why: Once ownership is abstracted from a person to a financial claim, the shareholder becomes a stand-in for the value that the portion represents.
senses.whyCN: 当所有权从具体的人抽象成一项财务主张，股东就成了那一份所代表价值的代称。

senses.title: Voter in corporate governance
senses.titleCN: 在公司治理中投票的股东
senses.definition: a shareholder exercising voting rights at a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 在股东会议上行使表决权的持股人
senses.example: Shareholders voted against the proposed pay package.
senses.exampleCN: 股东投票否决了拟议的薪酬方案。
senses.why: A share carries a vote as well as a dividend, so the keeper of a portion also becomes a participant in deciding how the company is run.
senses.whyCN: 股份除了带来股息，也带来表决权，因此这一份的持有者同时成为公司如何运转的决策参与者。

senses.title: Activist owner pressing for change
senses.titleCN: 积极推动公司改变的股东
senses.definition: a shareholder who publicly campaigns to change company policy or leadership
senses.definitionCN: 公开推动公司改变政策或领导层的股东
senses.example: An activist shareholder nominated three new directors.
senses.exampleCN: 一位积极股东提名了三位新董事。
senses.why: Here the voting and value senses combine: the owner uses the stake as leverage to force a change rather than merely to receive a return.
senses.whyCN: 这里投票义与价值义合并：持有者把股份当作杠杆去迫使改变，而不只是领取回报。

intro.en: Shareholder is an English compound of share and holder, built from Old English material rather than borrowed from Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: shareholder 是 share 与 holder 构成的英语复合词，用的是古英语材料，而非借自拉丁语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Scearu meant a division, portion or allotted part, and it is generally thought to be related to scieran 'to cut, shear', so a share is literally a piece cut off from a whole.
items.cn: scearu 意为「划分、份额、分得的部分」，一般认为是 scieran「切、剪」的同族词，因此「一份」本义就是从整体上切下来的一块。

items.en: Healdan meant to hold, keep or watch over, and its agent form holder named the one who keeps something in hand.
items.cn: healdan 意为「持有、保管、看守」，其表人形式 holder 指把某物握在手中的人。

items.en: By the Middle English period holder was a settled noun for a person who possesses land, an office or an object.
items.cn: 到中古英语时期，holder 已经是稳定的名词，指拥有土地、职位或物品的人。

items.en: Joint-stock companies divided their capital into transferable portions, and the compound shareholder named the person who kept one of those portions. The first recorded uses are dated to the early eighteenth century.
items.cn: 合股公司把资本分成可转让的份额，复合词 shareholder 便用来指持有其中一份的人。已知最早用例一般定在十八世纪早期。

items.en: Industrial finance widened the word to institutions and private savers alike, and later governance debates added the controlling, minority and activist readings.
items.cn: 工业化金融把这个词扩展到机构与个人储蓄者，后来的治理讨论又添上控股、少数与积极干预等读法。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds close to shareholder but differs in formation; the second group shares the idea of owning a stake without being the same word.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或构成上与 shareholder 相近，但构词不同；第二组同样表示「持有份额」，却不是同一个词。

entries.definition: A near synonym built on stock rather than share; American English prefers it, but the two words describe the same legal position.
entries.definitionCN: 用 stock 而非 share 构成的近义说法；美式英语更常用它，但两个词描述的是同一种法律地位。

entries.definition: Originally the holder of a bet or a stake in a wager, now any party affected by a company; a stakeholder need not own a single share.
entries.definitionCN: 原指赌注的持有者，现指受公司影响的任何一方；利益相关者未必持有一股股份。

entries.definition: A rarer synonym formed with owner; it stresses ownership rather than the act of holding.
entries.definitionCN: 较少见的同义说法，用 owner 构成，强调所有权而不是「持有」这个动作。

entries.definition: A farmer who works land for a share of the crop; the share here is harvest, not capital, and the word has no connection with company ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 按收成份额耕种他人土地的人；这里的 share 指收成而非资本，与公司所有权无关。

entries.definition: Anyone who puts money into an asset hoping for a return; an investor may hold bonds or property and need not own shares.
entries.definitionCN: 把资金投入资产以求得回报的人；投资者可能持有债券或房产，未必持有股份。

entries.definition: A descriptive phrase for a holder of equity, used when the legal nature of the ownership matters more than the person.
entries.definitionCN: 对权益持有者的描述性说法，用于强调所有权的法律性质而非持有人本身。

entries.definition: In company law, especially British usage, a member is a person entered on the register of members, which in practice means a shareholder.
entries.definitionCN: 在公司法、尤其是英式用法中，member 指登记在公司成员名册上的人，实务上就是股东。

entries.definition: A party who acts for itself in a transaction, as opposed to an agent; the word marks a role in the deal, not ownership of shares.
entries.definitionCN: 在交易中代表自己行事的一方，与代理人相对；它标出交易角色，而不表示持有股份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Share plus holder: the person who holds one of the cut portions of a company.
normal.cn: share 加 holder：持有公司被切出的其中一份的人。

normal.en: The Old English noun behind share meant a division or allotted part, so ownership is pictured as holding a cut slice.
normal.cn: share 背后的古英语名词本义是划分或分得的部分，所以所有权可以想成握着一片切下来的份。

normal.en: Stockholder is the American twin; both point to the same register of owners.
normal.cn: stockholder 是美式英语里的对应词；两者指向同一份所有者名册。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the word by size and by owner type: majority, minority, controlling, institutional, activist.
normal.cn: 固定搭配按规模与持有人类型给这个词分类：多数、少数、控股、机构、积极干预。

normal.en: A shareholder owns shares; a stakeholder merely has something at stake, which is the distinction to keep in mind.
normal.cn: shareholder 拥有股份；stakeholder 只是有利益牵涉，这个区别要记牢。

abstract.en: Picture a company as a pie cut into equal slices, with one slice wrapped in a document and kept in a pocket.
abstract.cn: 把公司想成一块切成等份的饼，其中一份用文件包好，收在口袋里。

abstract.en: Picture a voting card whose weight is set by how many slices the hand already holds.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表决卡，它的分量由那只手已经握住的份数决定。

abstract.en: Picture a claim on a stream of future profit, drawn as a thin line running from the company to a waiting hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一项对未来利润的权利，画成一条从公司流向等待之手的细线。

examples.en: The largest shareholder blocked the merger at the annual meeting.
examples.cn: 最大股东在年度会议上阻止了这次合并。

examples.en: Shareholders expect the dividend to rise with profits.
examples.cn: 股东期待股息随利润一同提高。

examples.en: A pension fund can be a patient shareholder for many years.
examples.cn: 养老基金可以多年做一位有耐心的股东。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「share（一份）+ holder（持有者）」——持有公司一份的人 → 股东

root: share 出自古英语 scearu「划分、份额」，一般认为是 scieran「切、剪」的同族词；holder 由 hold「持有」加表人后缀构成。整个词是英语本族复合词，不来自拉丁语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses unfold from one relation: a person keeps a divided portion of a company, and that portion is then read by weight, by owner type, by value, by vote and by pressure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由同一种关系展开：一个人持有公司被分出的一份，这一份再按分量、持有人类型、价值、表决与施压等角度被读出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a company cut into equal slices, one slice held in a hand together with a voting card.
core.cn: 核心意象：公司被切成等份，一只手握着其中一份，同时拿着表决卡。

branches.en: BASE RELATION: the word itself is simply the keeper of one cut portion of the company.
branches.cn: 基础关系：这个词本身就是公司某一份的持有者。

branches.en: WEIGHT OF THE SLICE: a large portion can steer the whole, while a small portion can only object.
branches.cn: 那一份的分量：大份能左右整体，小份只能表示反对。

branches.en: WHO HOLDS IT: the same portion can rest in an organization or in a private hand.
branches.cn: 由谁持有：同一份既可以归机构，也可以归个人。

branches.en: VALUE CLAIM: ownership abstracted into the financial interest that the company is told to serve.
branches.cn: 价值主张：所有权被抽象为公司被要求去服务的财务利益。

branches.en: VOICE AND PRESSURE: the voting card turns the held portion into a say in how the company is run.
branches.cn: 表决与施压：表决卡把握有的那一份变成对公司运转的发言权。

intro.en: Shareholder is made of native English pieces, so its family is built by compounding and by the agent suffix rather than by Latin derivation.
intro.cn: shareholder 由英语本族成分构成，因此它的词族靠复合与表人后缀扩展，而不是靠拉丁语派生。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word lies behind this compound. Latin-based finance vocabulary enters English separately through words such as equity, capital and dividend.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词背后没有拉丁词。拉丁来源的金融词汇是通过 equity、capital、dividend 等词另行进入英语的。

items.structure: share (Old English noun, a division or portion)
items.meaning: a portion cut from a whole
items.example: Each child took a share of the fruit.
items.exampleCN: 每个孩子都分到了一份水果。

items.structure: hold (Old English verb, to keep or watch over)
items.example: She held the deed in her hand.
items.exampleCN: 她把契据握在手里。

items.structure: -er (Old English agent suffix, one who does or keeps)
items.example: The keeper of the key opened the door.
items.exampleCN: 拿钥匙的人打开了门。

items.meaning: the keeper of a portion of a company
items.example: A shareholder may vote at the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 股东可以在会议上投票。

items.meaning: the state or amount of holding shares
items.example: Her shareholding rose above ten percent.
items.exampleCN: 她的持股比例升到百分之十以上。

items.meaning: several blocks of shares held in different companies
items.meaningCN: 在不同公司持有的多笔股份
items.example: He declared all his shareholdings.
items.exampleCN: 他申报了自己全部持股。

items.meaning: the same legal owner, named through stock
items.meaningCN: 同一种法律所有者，只是用 stock 构成
items.example: Stockholders approved the new board.
items.exampleCN: 股东们批准了新董事会。

items.meaning: a party with an interest at stake
items.example: Local residents are stakeholders in the plan.
items.exampleCN: 当地居民是该计划的利益相关方。

items.meaningCN: 强调所有权的较少见同义说法
items.example: Shareowners received the voting papers.
items.exampleCN: 股份所有者收到了表决文件。

derivatives.zh: 多处持股；持有的股份总额

definition_zh: 核实；验证；查证；确认；证明为真；身份核验；合规审查；（哲学）证实原则
definition_en: the act of checking or proving that something is true, accurate, or genuine
core_image: 一枚印章落在核对过的文件末尾，旁边是逐条打勾的清单
scene: 审核员把每一张发票与合同逐条对照，确认金额和日期都能对上，才在末页盖章。 Before payment, the clerk carried out a careful verification of every invoice against the contract.
sceneCN: 这里指逐条核对材料是否真实、准确（第 1 个义项：核实、查证）；句意为付款前职员把每张发票与合同仔细核对了一遍。场景图取象：核对完的文件末尾落下一枚印章。

pos.zh: 核实；验证；查证（不可数，指过程时多用单数）
证明为真的证据或确认结论
身份、证件、账户的核验
（哲学）证实原则；证实主义的核心概念

derivatives.zh: 核实；证实（由「真」与「做」两个拉丁词根合成，字面即「使之成真」）
可核实的（加表示「能够被……」的形容词后缀，指可以被查证）
可核实性（在形容词后加表示「性质」的名词后缀）
核验者；验证程序（加表示「施动者」的名词后缀）
已核实的；经确认的（动词过去分词转为形容词，指核验已经完成）
证实主义（在 verification 后加表示「学说」的后缀，指以能否证实判断意义的主张）

senses.title: The act of checking
senses.definition: the act of checking whether a statement, figure or account is true and accurate
senses.definitionCN: 检查某一说法、数字或账目是否真实准确的行为
senses.example: Verification of the figures took three days.
senses.exampleCN: 核对这些数字花了三天。
senses.why: The word joins 'true' and 'make', so the act is making sure a claim really is true.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「真」与「做」合在一起，动作就是确保某个说法确实为真。

senses.title: Formal confirmation
senses.definition: official confirmation that a document, claim or record meets a required standard
senses.definitionCN: 官方确认某份文件、声明或记录达到了规定标准
senses.example: The certificate requires verification by a public notary.
