senses.exampleCN: 这份证书需要由公证人正式确认。
senses.why: Institutions need a stamp as well as a check, and the word covers both the check and the resulting confirmation.
senses.whyCN: 机构既要查也要盖章，这个词同时涵盖查验与由此得到的确认。

senses.title: Evidence that proves
senses.definition: a piece of evidence or a statement that establishes something as true
senses.definitionCN: 能证明某事为真的证据或说法
senses.example: His notes served as verification of the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笔记成了这一说法的凭据。
senses.why: The noun can name the proof itself, not only the act of producing it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也能指证据本身，而不只是取得证据的动作。

senses.title: Checking who you are
senses.definition: the process of confirming a person's identity, account or credentials before granting access
senses.definitionCN: 在给予权限之前确认某人身份、账户或凭证的程序
senses.example: Two-step verification blocked the stolen password.
senses.exampleCN: 两步核验挡住了被盗的密码。
senses.why: Digital accounts made this the everyday sense: a second check that the person is who the password says.
senses.whyCN: 数字账户使这一义项成为日常用法：再查一次，看人是否真如密码所称。

senses.title: Test against reality
senses.definition: confirmation of a scientific claim by independent observation, measurement or experiment
senses.definitionCN: 通过独立观察、测量或实验来确认某一科学主张
senses.example: Independent verification is the price of a published result.
senses.exampleCN: 独立验证是一项结果得以发表的代价。
senses.why: Science separates the claim from the claimant by asking another laboratory to check it.
senses.whyCN: 科学把主张与主张者分开，办法是让另一个实验室去查。

senses.title: Proof that software obeys its spec
senses.definition: the process of showing that a program or system has been built according to its stated requirements
senses.definitionCN: 证明某个程序或系统是按其声明的需求建成的过程
senses.example: Verification caught the error before the release.
senses.exampleCN: 验证在发布前抓住了这个错误。
senses.why: Engineering distinguishes building the thing right from building the right thing, and calls the first verification.
senses.whyCN: 工程学把「把东西做对」与「做对的东西」分开，前者称为验证。

senses.title: Audit of accounts
senses.definition: a formal audit of records, accounts or compliance with rules
senses.definitionCN: 对记录、账目或规则遵守情况的正式审查
senses.example: The agency ordered verification of the charity's spending.
senses.exampleCN: 主管机构下令核查该慈善机构的开支。
senses.why: Public money brings a legal duty to check, and the word acquired an administrative weight.
senses.whyCN: 公共资金带来核对的法定义务，这个词因此带上行政分量。

senses.title: Fact-checking before print
senses.definition: the editorial process of checking names, dates and quotations before publication
senses.definitionCN: 发表前核对人名、日期与引文的编辑程序
senses.example: The magazine's verification desk flagged two dates.
senses.exampleCN: 杂志的核实台标出了两个日期问题。
senses.why: Publishing houses built a desk for this work, and the word named both the desk and its task.
senses.whyCN: 出版社为此设了专岗，这个词既指这个岗位，也指它的工作。

senses.title: The verification principle
senses.definition: the philosophical rule that a statement is meaningful only if it can be checked by experience
senses.definitionCN: 一种哲学主张：一个陈述只有能被经验检验才有意义
senses.example: The verification principle turned out to be too strict for its own rule.
senses.exampleCN: 证实原则对自己那条规则来说过于严格。
senses.why: Early twentieth-century philosophy tried to make meaning a testable property, and gave the word this narrow sense.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪初的哲学想把意义变成可检验的属性，于是给了这个词一个狭窄的义项。

intro.en: Verification is built from the Latin verus 'true' and facere 'to make', through Medieval Latin verificare. The chain is well documented and the only uncertain point is the exact date of its English entry.
intro.cn: verification 由拉丁语 verus「真」与 facere「做」构成，经由中世纪拉丁语 verificare 而来。词源链记录充分，唯一不确定的是它进入英语的确切年代。

items.en: Verus meant true or genuine, and it stands behind verity, veracity and the English word very.
items.cn: verus 意为真实的、真正的，还构成 verity、veracity 以及英语的 very。

items.en: The verb facere, to make or do, supplies the second half of the compound and the -fication ending.
items.cn: 动词 facere 意为做、造，提供复合词的后半与 -fication 这一词尾。

items.en: Verificare meant to make true or to prove true, a word of the schools rather than of everyday speech.
items.cn: verificare 意为使之成真或证明为真，是学院用语而非日常口语。

items.en: The noun entered English in the late Middle Ages, first in learned and legal writing; the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词在中世纪晚期进入英语，最早见于学术与法律文本；确切年代不确定。

items.en: From the seventeenth century it spread into experiment and jurisprudence, where a claim must be checked by evidence.
items.cn: 十七世纪以后，它扩展到实验与法学领域，那里主张必须靠证据核查。

items.en: In the last decades it became a household word through codes, passwords and two-step checks.
items.cn: 近几十年，它靠验证码、密码与两步核验成了家常词汇。

note.en: The first group shares the true-making root or merely looks close; the second group contains the neighbouring checks that are often confused with verification.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「使真」词根，或只是字形相近；第二组是常与「验证」混淆的邻近概念。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun: to check or prove that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词：核查或证明某事为真。

entries.definition: Truthfulness, especially of a person or account; it shares verus but not facere.
entries.definitionCN: 真实性、诚实，尤指人或陈述；共享「真」词根，不含「做」。

entries.definition: An old word for truth itself, built on the same Latin adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指真理本身的古词，由同一个拉丁形容词构成。

entries.definition: The art of turning prose into verse; it looks close but comes from versus, a turning of the plough.
entries.definitionCN: 把散文写成诗句的技艺；字形相近，却来自「犁沟转向」之意的 versus。

entries.definition: Abusive speech that lowers someone's name; its first element means cheap or base.
entries.definitionCN: 贬损他人名誉的辱骂；其前一部分意为低贱。

entries.definition: Checking that a system meets the user's real need, as opposed to its written specification.
entries.definitionCN: 检查系统是否满足使用者的真实需要，与书面规格相对。

entries.definition: A statement or act that makes something formally certain.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事在形式上确定的说法或举动。

entries.definition: Proving that a person or object is genuine, especially in computing.
entries.definitionCN: 证明人或物为真品，尤用于计算机领域。

entries.definition: Formal granting of a certificate after an authority has checked a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 主管机构查过标准后正式发给证书。

entries.definition: The journalistic routine of confirming details before publication.
entries.definitionCN: 发表前核对细节的新闻例行工作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real true-making root, the real derivative family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「使真」词根、真实派生词族与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Verus is true and facere is make, so verification is literally the making true of a claim.
normal.cn: 前者为真，后者为做，合起来字面就是使一个说法成真。

normal.en: The same true root gives verity and veracity, while the make root gives -fication in dozens of words.
normal.cn: 同一个「真」词根给出 verity 与 veracity，「做」词根则在许多词里留下 -fication 词尾。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: identity verification, independent verification, verification code.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：身份核验、独立核实、验证码。

normal.en: The verb is verify, the adjective verifiable, the person verifier.
normal.cn: 动词是 verify，形容词是可核实的，执行者是核验者。

normal.en: A verified document carries a stamp; a verification is the check that earns the stamp.
normal.cn: 已核实的文件带着印章，核验就是挣来这枚印章的检查。

abstract.en: Verification is distrust put to work in an orderly way.
abstract.cn: 核验是把不信任按规矩使出来。

abstract.en: It does not create truth; it only refuses to accept a claim until the claim can be checked.
abstract.cn: 它并不制造真理，只是在说法可被核对之前拒绝接受它。

abstract.en: A society that stops verifying slowly loses the difference between a claim and a fact.
abstract.cn: 一个不再核验的社会，会慢慢失去主张与事实之间的区别。

examples.en: Verification of the sample took longer than the test itself.
examples.cn: 样本核验比测试本身花的时间还长。

examples.en: The bank asks for a second verification before large transfers.
examples.cn: 大额转账前银行要求再做一次核验。

examples.en: Independent verification is what turns an announcement into a result.
examples.cn: 独立验证才能把一则宣告变成一个结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「维瑞菲克申」——把「真」做出来，逐条打勾盖章：核实、验证

root: 中世纪拉丁语 verificare「使之成真、证明为真」← 拉丁语 verus「真」＋ facere「做、造」；verus 另构成 verity、veracity 与 very，facere 构成 -fication 系列。进入英语的确切年代不确定，义项扩展至科学、法律与数字身份。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow the same act: a check, a formal confirmation, the proof itself, an identity check, a test against reality, proof of a specification, an audit, editorial fact-checking, and a philosophical principle.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一个动作：核对、正式确认、凭据本身、身份核验、用事实检验、对规格的证明、账目审查、刊前核实，以及一条哲学原则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a checked list with ticks beside every line, and a stamp waiting at the end.
core.cn: 核心意象：每行都打了勾的清单，末尾等着落下一枚印章。

branches.en: THE CHECK AND ITS PROOF: the act of testing a claim, and the evidence that the test produced.
branches.cn: 检查及其凭据：检验主张的动作，以及检验得出的证据。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL SEAL: confirmation by an authority, and the audit that must come before it.
branches.cn: 官方印章：主管者的确认，以及确认之前必须做的审查。

branches.en: THE IDENTITY CHECK: the second step that proves a person is who the account says.
branches.cn: 身份核验：证明人如其账户所称的第二步。

branches.en: THE TEST OF A CLAIM: independent experiment, a program checked against its specification, and a page checked before print.
branches.cn: 对主张的检验：独立实验、按规格检查的程序，以及付印前核对过的稿件。

branches.en: THE PRINCIPLE: meaning itself is said to require a possible check.
branches.cn: 那条原则：意义本身被要求可以被检验。

intro.en: Verification is a compound of two productive Latin pieces, and its endings still build abstract nouns in English.
intro.cn: verification 由两个能产的拉丁构件合成，其词尾在英语中仍能造抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin verus and facere are the two sources; the noun ending came through Medieval Latin -ficatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 verus 与 facere 是两个来源，名词词尾经由中世纪拉丁语的 -ficatio 而来。

items.example: The noun names both the act and its outcome.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指动作，也指结果。

items.example: It also stands behind verity and very.
items.exampleCN: 它还构成 verity 与 very。

items.example: It is the source of the -fy and -fication endings.
items.exampleCN: 它是 -fy 与 -fication 词尾的来源。

items.example: It builds classification, simplification and purification.
items.exampleCN: 它构成分类、简化与提纯等词。

items.example: It builds verify, clarify and amplify.
items.exampleCN: 它构成核实、澄清与放大等动词。

items.example: The adjective sets the standard for a good claim.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词为好的主张立下标准。

items.meaning: one who or that which checks
items.example: The ending marks the person or the tool.
items.exampleCN: 词尾标出人或工具。

items.example: The abstract noun names a property rather than an act.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词指属性而非动作。

latinEntries.meaning: to make true; to prove true
latinEntries.example: Medieval Latin verificare means to make true.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 verificare 意为使之为真。

latinEntries.example: Latin verus means true, and gives veracity and verdict.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 verus 意为真的，并给出 veracity 与 verdict。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb facere (fac-, factum; to make)
latinEntries.example: Latin facere means to make or do.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 facere 意为做、造。

definition_zh: 财务风险；金融风险
definition_en: the risk of losing money through financial transactions, markets or obligations
core_image: 一张资产负债表上有一处正在渗水的裂缝
scene: 货币危机之后，银行重新审查资产负债表，评估汇率波动与坏账可能带来的损失。 The bank reviewed its financial risk after the currency crisis.
sceneCN: 这里指「金融风险」，对应第 1 个义项：因金融交易、市场或债务而蒙受损失的可能；句意为货币危机之后，银行重新审查了自身金融风险。画面要点：资产负债表、汇率曲线、风险审查章。

pos.zh: 财务风险；金融风险（可数指具体一类风险）

senses.title: Exposure to monetary loss
senses.titleCN: 蒙受金钱损失的可能性
senses.definition: the possibility of losing money through financial activities
senses.definitionCN: 因金融活动而损失金钱的可能性
senses.example: The audit found serious financial risk in the subsidiary.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现该子公司存在严重的金融风险。
senses.why: Financial narrows risk to money, so the broad chance of harm becomes a chance of loss measured in currency.
senses.whyCN: financial 把风险收窄到金钱，于是广义的受害概率变成以货币计量的损失概率。

senses.title: Credit risk
senses.definition: the risk that a borrower or counterparty fails to pay
senses.definitionCN: 借款人或交易对手无法付款的风险
senses.example: Credit risk rose as small firms struggled.
senses.exampleCN: 小企业陷入困境，信用风险随之上升。
senses.why: One source of loss is another party's failure, so the general exposure is narrowed to who owes the money.
senses.whyCN: 损失的一个来源是对方违约，于是普遍敞口被收窄到「谁欠着钱」。

senses.title: Market risk
senses.definition: the risk that prices, rates or indices move against a position
senses.definitionCN: 价格、利率或指数朝持仓不利方向变动的风险
senses.example: Market risk dominates a trading book.
senses.exampleCN: 市场风险在交易账簿中占主导。
senses.why: Another source is the market itself, where prices move without anyone defaulting.
senses.whyCN: 另一个来源是市场本身：价格会变动，却没有任何人违约。

senses.title: Liquidity risk
senses.definition: the risk of being unable to meet obligations when they fall due
senses.definitionCN: 到期无法履行义务的风险
senses.example: Liquidity risk can sink a solvent bank.
senses.exampleCN: 流动性风险能拖垮一家仍有偿付能力的银行。
senses.why: The danger is not lack of assets but lack of ready cash, so the word focuses on timing rather than value.
senses.whyCN: 危险不是没有资产，而是没有随时可用的现金，所以这个词聚焦于时点而非价值。

senses.title: Operational risk
senses.definition: the risk of loss from failed processes, people, systems or fraud
senses.definitionCN: 流程、人员、系统失败或欺诈造成损失的风险
senses.example: Operational risk includes errors and internal theft.
senses.exampleCN: 操作风险包括差错与内部盗窃。
senses.why: The source moves inside the firm: the machinery and people meant to handle money can themselves fail.
senses.whyCN: 来源移到公司内部：本应处理金钱的机械与人员本身也会失灵。

senses.title: Currency risk
senses.definition: the risk that exchange rates change the value of foreign payments or assets
senses.definitionCN: 汇率变动改变外币付款或资产价值的风险
senses.example: Exporters face currency risk on every contract.
senses.exampleCN: 出口商在每份合同上都面临汇率风险。
senses.why: When money itself changes price across borders, even a safe asset can lose value at home.
senses.whyCN: 当货币本身在跨境之间改变价格，连安全的资产也可能在本国贬值。

senses.title: Systemic risk
senses.definition: the risk that one failure spreads through the whole financial system
senses.definitionCN: 单一失败蔓延至整个金融体系的风险
senses.example: Regulators watch systemic risk across banks.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者监测跨银行的系统性风险。
senses.why: The unit of danger grows from a firm to the system, so a local loss becomes a threat to everyone.
senses.whyCN: 危险的单位从一家机构扩大到整个体系，局部的损失于是成为对所有人的威胁。

senses.title: Risk to capital and earnings
senses.definition: the risk that a firm's capital or earnings fall below what is required
senses.definitionCN: 公司资本或盈利跌破要求水平的风险
senses.example: The quarterly report modelled financial risk against capital.
senses.exampleCN: 季度报告以资本为基准对金融风险作了建模。
senses.why: Risk management compares possible losses with the buffer available, so the exposure is read as a threat to solvency.
senses.whyCN: 风险管理把可能损失与可用缓冲相比较，于是敞口被读成对偿付能力的威胁。

intro.en: Financial risk joins financial, from a French word for settling a debt, with risk, a Romance loan whose deeper origin is disputed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: financial risk 把 financial 与 risk 组合起来：前者出自法语表示结清债务的词，后者是来源有争议的罗曼语借词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Finis meant an end or boundary, and it built words about ending, limiting and settling.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或边界，构成了一批表示结束、限定与结清的词。

items.en: Finer meant to settle a debt or bring a matter to an end, from the same notion of a boundary being closed.
items.cn: finer 意为结清债务或把事办完，来自同一个「划上边界」的观念。

items.en: Finance named the payment or settlement of a debt, and English borrowed it for money management in general.
items.cn: finance 指债务的支付或结清，英语借来表示一般意义上的资金管理。

items.en: The adjective financial was formed to describe matters of money, revenue and funding.
items.cn: 形容词 financial 用来描述金钱、收入与筹资事务。

items.en: Risk came through French and Italian; its deeper origin is source uncertain, with a Greek reef explanation and a Latin cutting explanation both unproven.
items.cn: risk 经法语与意大利语而来；更深来源不确定，暗礁说与切掉说都未获证明。

items.en: Twentieth-century regulation split financial risk into credit, market, liquidity, operational, currency and systemic types.
items.cn: 二十世纪监管把金融风险分成信用、市场、流动性、操作、汇率与系统性等类型。

note.en: The first group is built from the same finance root and is easily confused; the second group names particular risks or wider dangers.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「财务」词根上，容易混淆；第二组指具体风险或更广的危险。

entries.definition: The management of money, or to provide funds; it is the field, not the danger within it.
entries.definitionCN: 资金管理，或提供资金；它是领域，而不是领域内的危险。

entries.definition: Relating to money; it describes the kind of risk but does not by itself mean risk.
entries.definitionCN: 与金钱有关的；它描述风险的种类，本身并不表示风险。

entries.definition: A person who deals in large sums or arranges funding; it is a role, not a danger.
entries.definitionCN: 处理大额资金或安排融资的人；它是角色，不是危险。

entries.definition: A sum paid as a penalty, or excellent; the penalty sense comes from the idea of settling a matter, not from finance itself.
entries.definitionCN: 罚款，或优秀的；罚款义出自「把事结清」的观念，而非金融本身。

entries.definition: The risk that a borrower defaults; it is one component of financial risk, not the whole category.
entries.definitionCN: 借款人违约的风险；它是金融风险的一个组成部分，而非整个类别。

entries.definition: The risk of loss from price movements; like credit risk, it is a part of the wider financial category.
entries.definitionCN: 价格变动造成损失的风险；与信用风险一样，是更广类别的一部分。

entries.definition: The size of a position affected by a factor; financial risk is the possibility, exposure is the measured amount.
entries.definitionCN: 受某因素影响的持仓规模；金融风险是可能性，敞口是被计量的数额。

entries.definition: The state of being unable to pay debts; it is a result that financial risk may produce, not the risk itself.
entries.definitionCN: 无力偿还债务的状态；它是金融风险可能导致的结果，而非风险本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real settling root of finance, the disputed origin of risk, and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「结清」词根、来源有争议的 risk，以及真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Finance began as settling a debt; adding risk turns settlement into possible loss.
normal.cn: finance 最初指结清债务；加上 risk，结清就变成可能的损失。

normal.en: The phrase covers subtypes: credit, market, liquidity, operational, currency and systemic.
normal.cn: 这个短语涵盖多个子类：信用、市场、流动性、操作、汇率与系统性。

normal.en: Credit risk asks who may not pay; market risk asks what prices may do; liquidity risk asks when cash may fail.
normal.cn: 信用风险问谁可能不付钱；市场风险问价格可能怎么走；流动性风险问现金何时会断。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: financial risk management, exposure, systemic financial risk.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：金融风险管理、风险敞口、系统性金融风险。

normal.en: Operational risk comes from inside, while systemic risk grows until it reaches everyone.
normal.cn: 操作风险来自内部，系统性风险则扩大到波及所有人。

abstract.en: Picture a balance sheet with one seam leaking, and no one yet knows how far the leak will spread.
abstract.cn: 想象一张资产负债表上有一道缝在渗水，还没人知道会渗多远。

abstract.en: Picture six pipes feeding one tank, each with its own valve that could fail.
abstract.cn: 想象六条管道通向同一只水箱，每条都有自己的阀门可能失灵。

abstract.en: Picture a single bank's stumble drawn as a crack running through a whole wall of banks.
abstract.cn: 想象一家银行的失足被画成一道裂纹，贯穿整面由银行砌成的墙。

examples.en: The treasurer monitors financial risk every week.
examples.cn: 财务主管每周监测金融风险。

examples.en: Diversification lowers financial risk without removing it.
examples.cn: 分散化降低金融风险，但不能消除它。

examples.en: A sudden currency fall can turn a safe loan into financial risk.
examples.cn: 货币骤然下跌能把一笔安全贷款变成金融风险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「金钱上的裂缝」——账面上有一处可能漏水 → 金融风险

root: financial 出自法语 finance「债务的结清、支付」，再上溯到拉丁语 finis「终点、边界」；risk 经法语与意大利语而来，更早来源不确定。两者合指因金融活动蒙受损失的可能。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the general chance of monetary loss and then divide it by source: borrower, market, timing, operations, currency and the whole system, ending with capital adequacy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般的金钱损失概率开始，再按来源划分：借款方、市场、时点、操作、货币与整个体系，最后落在资本充足性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance sheet with one seam leaking, and no one knows how far the leak will spread.
core.cn: 核心意象：资产负债表上有一道缝在渗水，没人知道会渗多远。

branches.en: THE WHOLE EXPOSURE: every financial activity carries a chance of monetary loss.
branches.cn: 整体敞口：每一项金融活动都带有金钱损失的可能。

branches.en: CREDIT: the borrower or counterparty may fail to pay.
branches.cn: 信用：借款人或交易对手可能不付钱。

branches.en: MARKET AND CAPITAL: prices move against positions, and losses eat into the capital buffer.
branches.cn: 市场与资本：价格朝持仓不利方向走，损失侵蚀资本缓冲。

branches.en: LIQUIDITY: the money exists but not at the moment it is due.
branches.cn: 流动性：钱存在，却不在到期的那一刻可用。

branches.en: OPERATIONS, CURRENCY AND SYSTEM: internal failure, exchange-rate shifts and contagion each add a source.
branches.cn: 操作、货币与体系：内部失灵、汇率变动与传染各自增添一个来源。

intro.en: Financial risk joins a Latin-derived adjective about settling accounts with a Romance noun for danger.
intro.cn: financial risk 把表示结清账目的拉丁来源形容词，与表示危险的罗曼语名词组合起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis 'end, boundary' gives finance, final, finish and infinite; the first element of this phrase belongs to that family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis「终点、边界」衍生 finance、final、finish 与 infinite；这个短语的前半属于该词族。

items.example: The root marks a limit.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根标示界限。

items.example: She studied finance at university.
items.exampleCN: 她在大学学习金融。

items.example: The firm faced financial trouble.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司面临财务困难。

items.example: The project is financially sound.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目在财务上是稳健的。

items.meaning: a person who handles large funds
items.example: A financier backed the railway.
items.exampleCN: 一位金融家资助了这条铁路。

items.example: The financing took six months.
items.exampleCN: 融资花了六个月。

items.meaning: to replace a loan with a new one
items.example: They refinanced the mortgage.
items.exampleCN: 他们重组了按揭贷款。

items.example: The bank measured financial risk.
items.exampleCN: 银行衡量了金融风险。

items.example: The report lists five financial risks.
items.exampleCN: 报告列出五种金融风险。

items.example: Risk rose after the crisis.
items.exampleCN: 危机之后风险上升。

definition_zh: 校准；标定；刻度设定；（判断）校准
definition_en: the act or process of adjusting an instrument or scale so that its readings match a known standard
core_image: 一把标准尺贴在仪器刻度旁，把每一格推到正确的位置
scene: 这里指「校准」。 Before each experiment, the team runs a full calibration of the spectrometer against a known sample.
sceneCN: 这里 calibration 是「校准」（第 1 个义项：用已知标准调整仪器）；句意：每次实验前，团队都用已知样本对光谱仪做一次完整校准。场景要点：标准样本、仪器刻度盘、记录笔，每一格被对齐到已知值。

pos.zh: 校准；标定；刻度设定；（判断）校准

forms.label: 复数（多次校准或多项校准值）

senses.title: Adjusting an instrument to a standard
senses.titleCN: 仪器校准：把读数对齐已知标准
senses.definition: the act of checking and adjusting an instrument so that its readings agree with a known standard
senses.definitionCN: 检查并调整仪器，使其读数与已知标准一致的行为
senses.example: The calibration of the thermometer is repeated every year.
senses.exampleCN: 这支温度计每年都要重新校准。
senses.why: Caliber named the bore of a gun. Calibrate first meant to measure that bore, then to fix any scale against a standard, and -ion names the process.
senses.whyCN: caliber 原本指炮管口径。calibrate 最初表示测定这个口径，后来表示让任何刻度对齐标准，-ion 命名这个过程。

senses.title: The state of being in adjustment
senses.definition: the condition of an instrument whose readings are known to be accurate
senses.definitionCN: 仪器读数已知准确的状态
senses.example: The gauge is out of calibration and must not be used.
senses.exampleCN: 这只仪表已经失准，不能使用。
senses.why: The result of the act is a state. English uses the same -ion noun for both the process and the standing condition it leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 动作的结果是一种状态。英语用同一个 -ion 名词既指过程，也指过程留下的持续状态。

senses.title: Setting the divisions of a scale
senses.titleCN: 刻度设定：决定每一格站在哪里
senses.definition: the marking or fixing of the divisions of a scale
senses.definitionCN: 标记或确定刻度上各分格的位置
senses.example: The calibration of the axis places zero at the freezing point.
senses.exampleCN: 这条轴的刻度设定把零点放在冰点。
senses.why: A scale is a row of marks. Calibration decides where each mark sits, so the noun also names the layout of the divisions rather than the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 刻度是一排标记。校准决定每个标记的位置，所以名词也指分格的排布，而不只是仪器。

senses.title: The reference relationship
senses.titleCN: 校准曲线：把信号与真值绑在一起
senses.definition: the established relationship between an instrument's signal and the true value
senses.definitionCN: 仪器信号与真实值之间建立起来的关系
senses.example: The concentration was read from the calibration curve.
senses.exampleCN: 浓度是从校准曲线上读出的。
senses.why: Once each mark is tied to a standard, the whole set of marks forms a curve or table. The noun is transferred from the act to the reference object produced by it.
senses.whyCN: 每个标记一旦绑定到一个标准，整套标记就构成一条曲线或一张表。名词于是从动作转到动作产生的参照物。

senses.title: Fine adjustment of a device
senses.titleCN: 设备调校：让参数回到工作区间
senses.definition: the tuning of a device or system so that it performs within its intended range
senses.definitionCN: 调整设备或系统，使其在预期范围内工作的过程
senses.example: Sensor calibration improved the camera's low-light performance.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器校准改善了相机的弱光表现。
senses.why: Modern devices have many parameters, not one scale. The word widens from a single needle to any setting that must be brought into line.
senses.whyCN: 现代设备有许多参数，而不只是一根指针。这个词从单根刻度扩展到任何需要被对齐的设置。

senses.title: Checking a model against data
senses.titleCN: 模型校准：让模型输出贴合观测
senses.definition: the process of testing and adjusting a model so that its output matches observations
senses.definitionCN: 检验并调整模型，使其输出与观测相符的过程
senses.example: Model calibration against field data reduced the error.
senses.exampleCN: 依据野外数据进行的模型校准降低了误差。
senses.why: A model is treated like an instrument: it produces readings, so it can be calibrated. The standard is now observed data rather than a physical gauge.
senses.whyCN: 模型被当作仪器：它会产生读数，因此可以被校准。此时的标准是观测数据，而不是物理量具。

senses.title: Calibration of confidence
senses.titleCN: 判断校准：自信程度与实际水平对得上吗
senses.definition: the accuracy with which a person's stated confidence matches actual performance
senses.definitionCN: 一个人表达的自信程度与其实际表现相符的准确度
senses.example: Forecasters studied the calibration of their confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 预报员研究了自己信心的校准程度。
senses.why: This is the metaphor at its most abstract: confidence is a scale, and calibration measures whether its marks match reality.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个隐喻最抽象的用法：自信是一条刻度，校准衡量的是刻度是否与真实相符。

senses.title: Measuring a bore
senses.titleCN: 口径测定：最早的字面义
senses.definition: the original sense: determining the caliber, or inside diameter, of a gun barrel
senses.definitionCN: 最初的字面义：测定炮管口径，即内直径
senses.example: The calibration of the barrel decided which shot would fit.
senses.exampleCN: 炮管的口径测定决定了哪种炮弹能装进去。
senses.why: The oldest literal sense measured a bore. Later senses keep the shape of measuring against a fixed width, which is why the word can still mean 'set to a standard'.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的字面义是测量孔径。后来的义项保留了“对着固定宽度测量”的形状，因此这个词仍能表示“对准标准”。

senses.title: Bringing standards into line
senses.titleCN: 标准对齐：让两套规范可比
senses.definition: the adjustment of standards, expectations, or policies so that they agree
senses.definitionCN: 调整标准、预期或政策，使其一致
senses.example: The two agencies agreed on a calibration of their safety standards.
senses.exampleCN: 两个机构就安全标准的对齐达成一致。
senses.why: Institutions also have scales. When separate standards must be made comparable, the instrument image is applied to rules and expectations.
senses.whyCN: 机构也有自己的刻度。当不同的标准需要变得可比时，仪器的意象就被用到规则和预期上。

intro.en: Calibration is a 19th-century derivative of calibrate, which was formed from caliber. The history of caliber itself is disputed, and the often-repeated Arabic-Greek chain is not established.
intro.cn: calibration 是 19 世纪由 calibrate 派生的名词，而 calibrate 又由 caliber 构成。caliber 本身的历史存在争议，常被转述的“阿拉伯—希腊”链条并未得到确证。

items.en: French calibre, recorded by the mid-16th century and perhaps in the late 15th, named the inside diameter of a gun barrel. English borrowed it as caliber in the 1580s.
items.cn: 法语 calibre 在 16 世纪中期有记录，也许可早到 15 世纪晚期，指炮管的内直径。英语在 16 世纪 80 年代把它借入为 caliber。

items.en: It is often said that calibre goes back to Arabic qalib 'a mold for casting'. Standard references repeat this with caution: Barnhart notes that Spanish and Italian forms appear too late to serve as intermediate links, and no documentary evidence supports the Arabic route.
items.cn: 常有人说 calibre 可追溯到阿拉伯语 qalib“铸造用的模具”。通行词源资料转述时都带保留：Barnhart 指出西班牙语和意大利语形式出现太晚，无法充当中间环节；也没有文献证据支持这条阿拉伯路径。

items.en: A still deeper link to Greek kalapous 'wooden shoe' is sometimes proposed. It is speculative and not accepted in standard etymological references, so it should be treated as uncertain rather than as fact.
items.cn: 偶尔还有人把它更往上联系到希腊语 kalapous“木鞋”。这属于推测，通行词源资料并不接受，因此应当作存疑处理，不能当作事实。

items.en: A rival 19th-century explanation derives calibre from Medieval Latin qua libra 'of what weight', from quis 'which' and libra 'balance'. This is also a hypothesis, not a settled fact.
items.cn: 19 世纪还有一种竞争性解释，认为 calibre 来自中古拉丁语 qua libra“按什么重量”，由 quis“哪一个”和 libra“天平”构成。这同样只是假说，并非定论。

items.en: Calibrate was formed in English in 1839 from caliber + -ate, meaning 'determine the caliber of'. By 1869 it also meant 'determine the relative value of the parts of an arbitrary scale'.
items.cn: calibrate 于 1839 年在英语中由 caliber + -ate 构成，意为“测定……的口径”。到 1869 年，它也指“确定任意刻度上各部分的相对数值”。

items.en: Calibration is recorded in 1854 as the noun of action of calibrate. The sense moved from measuring a bore to setting any scale, then to adjusting instruments, models, and even human confidence. The deeper origin of caliber remains uncertain.
items.cn: calibration 于 1854 年作为 calibrate 的行为名词出现。词义从测量口径扩展到设定任何刻度，再扩展到调整仪器、模型，甚至人的信心。caliber 的更早来源仍然存疑。

note.en: The look-alikes are the measuring and counting words that share the cal- shape; the near-meaning group contains words for adjustment and checking against a standard.
note.cn: 形近词是共享 cal- 外形的测量与计数词；近义词组则包含调整和对照标准检查类的词。

entries.definition: the inside diameter of a gun barrel, or the level of someone's ability. It is the noun from which calibrate was formed, not the act of adjusting.
entries.definitionCN: 炮管口径，或某人的能力水准。它是 calibrate 所由构成的名词，不是调整行为本身。

entries.definition: an instrument for measuring external or internal diameters. It is a measuring device, while calibration is the adjustment of a scale.
entries.definitionCN: 测量外径或内径的量具。它是测量工具，而 calibration 是对刻度的调整。

entries.definition: the act or result of computing with numbers. It shares the cal- beginning but comes from calculus 'pebble', not from caliber.
entries.definitionCN: 用数字计算的行为或结果。它共享 cal- 开头，但来自 calculus“石子”，并非来自 caliber。

entries.definition: to adjust an instrument against a standard. It is the verb; calibration adds -ion and names the act or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 对照标准调整仪器。它是动词；calibration 加 -ion，表示行为或结果。

entries.definition: a change made to fit a condition or purpose. It is broader than calibration and does not require a known standard.
entries.definitionCN: 为适应某条件或目的而作的改变。它比 calibration 宽泛，不要求有已知标准。

entries.definition: the adjustment of an instrument or system for best performance, especially by changing frequency. Calibration aims at accurate readings rather than optimal performance.
entries.definitionCN: 为获得最佳性能而调整仪器或系统，尤指改变频率。calibration 追求读数准确，而不是性能最优。

entries.definition: making things conform to one shared standard, often across an industry. It is a collective process; calibration is usually a local measurement adjustment.
entries.definitionCN: 使事物符合一个共同标准，常跨行业进行。它是集体过程；calibration 通常是局部的测量调整。

entries.definition: the act of checking that something is true or accurate. It tests the reading but does not necessarily adjust the instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 检查某事物是否真实或准确的行为。它检验读数，但未必调整仪器。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real gun-bore origin, the real suffix and the real laboratory collocations of calibration.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的炮口径来源、真实的后缀，以及 calibration 真实的实验室搭配。

normal.en: caliber = the bore of a gun. Calibration began as measuring that fixed width, then became setting any scale to a standard.
normal.cn: caliber 就是炮管口径。calibration 从测量这个固定宽度开始，后来变成把任何刻度对准标准。

normal.en: calibrate + -ion: the verb names the adjusting, and the noun names the act or the state it produces.
normal.cn: calibrate + -ion：动词命名调整动作，名词命名行为或它产生的状态。

normal.en: Out of calibration is the standard warning that an instrument's readings can no longer be trusted.
normal.cn: out of calibration 是标准警示语：仪器的读数不再可信。

normal.en: A calibration curve is the visible result of calibration: a line tying signal to true value.
normal.cn: calibration curve 是校准的可视结果：一条把信号与真值绑在一起的线。

normal.en: Calibration and calculation look alike but have different roots: caliber is a bore, calculus is a pebble.
normal.cn: calibration 与 calculation 形似，但词根不同：caliber 是口径，calculus 是石子。

abstract.en: Picture a standard ruler laid beside a dial: every mark on the dial is pushed until it lines up.
abstract.cn: 想象一把标准尺贴在刻度盘旁：盘上的每个标记都被推到对齐的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with a known weight on one side: the needle is moved until it reads that weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一台秤的一边放着已知重量的砝码：指针被调到能读出这个重量。

abstract.en: Picture a metronome set to 100 beats: the setting is not the music, but it makes the music trustworthy.
abstract.cn: 想象把节拍器设到每分钟 100 拍：这个设定不是音乐，却让音乐变得可信。

examples.en: The laboratory keeps a log of every calibration performed on its balances.
examples.cn: 实验室为天平所做的每一次校准都保留记录。

examples.en: Without regular calibration, the sensor's readings drift away from the true value.
examples.cn: 如果不定期校准，传感器的读数就会偏离真实值。

examples.en: The forecasters measured the calibration of their confidence over a full year.
examples.cn: 预报员用整整一年时间测量自己信心的校准程度。

dict_mnemonic.text: “卡里布瑞申”——卡（ca）里（li）布（bra）瑞（tion），用卡尺卡住标准布一量，刻度就准了 → calibration 校准

root: 英语 caliber/calibre“炮口径”（16 世纪经法语 calibre 借入），calibrate“测定口径、校准”+ -ion；calibre 更深来源存疑：阿拉伯 qalib“模具”说缺乏证据，另有中古拉丁 qua libra“按何重量”说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all repeat one gesture: a reading is brought into line with a fixed reference, whether the scale belongs to an instrument, a model, a standard, or a person's confidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都在重复同一个动作：让读数与一个固定参照对齐——无论这条刻度属于仪器、模型、标准，还是人的信心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a standard laid against a scale, with every mark pushed into line.
core.cn: 核心意象：把标准贴到刻度上，把每个标记推到对齐的位置。

branches.en: ACT AND STATE: the adjustment and the trustworthy condition it leaves behind are the same noun.
branches.cn: 行为与状态：调整动作和它留下的可信状态，由同一个名词表示。

branches.en: THE SCALE ITSELF: fixing where the divisions sit produces the reference curve used for later readings.
branches.cn: 刻度本身：确定分格的位置，就产生了供后续读数使用的参照曲线。

branches.en: SYSTEMS AND STANDARDS: device parameters and institutional rules are both brought into line.
branches.cn: 系统与标准：设备参数和机构规则，都被调到一致。

branches.en: MODELS AND MINDS: a model's output and a person's confidence can both be checked against reality.
branches.cn: 模型与心智：模型的输出和人的信心，都可以对照现实来检验。

branches.en: THE ORIGINAL BORE: the oldest sense measured a gun barrel, and its shape survives in every later use.
branches.cn: 最初的口径：最古老的义项测量炮管，这个形状留在后来每一种用法里。

intro.en: Calibration is built from an English verb and a Latin suffix: calibrate + -ion. The productive step is -ion; the base calibr- is frozen inside caliber, whose own origin is disputed.
intro.cn: calibration 由英语动词加拉丁后缀构成：calibrate + -ion。有能产性的一步是 -ion；词基 calibr- 凝固在 caliber 内部，而 caliber 本身的来源存在争议。

latinIntro.en: There is no certain Latin ancestor for calibr-. The two rival explanations are Arabic qalib 'mold' and Medieval Latin qua libra 'of what weight'. The Latin side of the second hypothesis is listed below; it is a hypothesis, not an established root.
latinIntro.cn: calibr- 没有确证的拉丁祖先。两种竞争性解释是阿拉伯语 qalib“模具”和中古拉丁语 qua libra“按什么重量”。下面列出第二种假说中的拉丁成分；它只是假说，不是已确立的词根。

items.meaning: the act or result of calibrating
items.meaningCN: 校准；标定（-ion 表示行为）
items.example: The calibration of the instrument is complete.
items.exampleCN: 仪器的校准已经完成。

items.meaning: to determine a caliber; to adjust a scale against a standard
items.meaningCN: 测定口径；校准（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: They calibrated the sensor before the test.
items.exampleCN: 测试前他们对传感器做了校准。

items.meaning: the inside diameter of a barrel; degree of quality
items.example: The rifle is of a small caliber.
items.exampleCN: 这支步枪口径较小。

items.meaning: same as caliber; also used figuratively for quality
items.meaningCN: caliber 的英式拼写；也用于比喻“水准”
items.example: The committee is looking for someone of her calibre.
items.exampleCN: 委员会正在找像她这种水准的人。

items.structure: probably from caliber, with a variant ending
items.meaningCN: 卡尺；测径器（可能由 caliber 变体而来）
items.example: Use the caliper to measure the pipe's diameter.
items.exampleCN: 用卡尺测量管子的直径。

items.meaningCN: 重新校准（re- 表示“再次”）
items.example: The machine recalibrates itself after each restart.
items.exampleCN: 每次重启后机器都会自动重新校准。

items.meaningCN: 重新校准（再次进行的校准）
items.example: A recalibration was needed after the move.
items.exampleCN: 搬动之后需要重新校准。

items.meaning: a device or person that calibrates
items.meaningCN: 校准器；校准员（-or 表示施动者）
items.example: The calibrator generates a known signal.
items.exampleCN: 校准器会生成一个已知信号。

items.meaningCN: 已校准的；标定过的（-ed 构成分词形容词）
items.example: All calibrated instruments are stored separately.
items.exampleCN: 所有已校准的仪器都单独存放。

items.meaning: of a smaller caliber than the standard
items.meaningCN: 次口径的；小于标准口径的（sub- 表示“低于”）
items.example: The training round uses a subcaliber insert.
items.exampleCN: 训练弹使用一个次口径内衬。

latinEntries.structure: libra (Latin noun: balance, pair of scales; pound)
latinEntries.meaning: a balance or unit of weight; the weight element in the rival qua libra hypothesis
latinEntries.meaningCN: 天平；重量单位；竞争性 qua libra 假说中的“重量”成分

latinEntries.meaning: 'of what weight'; Mahn's 19th-century alternative source for caliber, not proven
latinEntries.meaningCN: “按什么重量”；Mahn 在 19 世纪提出的 caliber 替代来源，未获确证

latinEntries.meaning: a standard measure; related measuring vocabulary, but not the source of caliber
latinEntries.meaningCN: 标准量度；属于测量词汇的对照项，但不是 caliber 的来源

definition_zh: 代谢的；新陈代谢的；与代谢速率、通路或代谢疾病相关的
definition_en: relating to metabolism, or to the rate, pathways and disorders of the body's chemical turnover
core_image: 一条环形流水线被画上刻度盘，盘上指针上下移动，旁边贴着「这条线的状态」的标签
scene: 这里指「代谢的」。 Metabolic rate falls at night, so the body burns less fuel while asleep.
sceneCN: 这里 metabolic 指「代谢速率的」（第 2 个义项：修饰速率，说明周转的快慢）；夜间速率下降，睡眠时消耗的燃料更少。图中可辨识物件：环形流水线、刻度盘、上下摆动的指针、状态标签。

pos.zh: 代谢的；新陈代谢的（多作定语，修饰 rate、pathway、disease 等）

senses.title: Of metabolism as a whole
senses.definition: relating to metabolism in general
senses.definitionCN: 与新陈代谢整体相关
senses.example: Metabolic processes keep the cell's chemistry in balance.
senses.exampleCN: 代谢过程使细胞的化学保持平衡。
senses.why: the -ic suffix turns the process into a relational adjective, so the word first means 'of metabolism'.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ic 把过程变成关系形容词，因此这个词首先意为「代谢的」。

senses.title: The speed of the loop
senses.definition: describing the rate at which the body's turnover runs
senses.definitionCN: 描述身体周转运行的速率
senses.example: A higher metabolic rate lets a small mammal stay warm in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 较高的代谢率让小型哺乳动物在冬天保持体温。
senses.why: once physiologists measured the loop, the adjective attached to its speed, not only to its existence.
senses.whyCN: 当生理学家开始测定这条环路，这个形容词便附着在它的速度上，而不只是它的存在。

senses.title: A route inside the map
senses.definition: describing one route or step within the network of reactions
senses.definitionCN: 描述反应网络中的某条路线或某个步骤
senses.example: Glycolysis is a metabolic pathway shared by almost all cells.
senses.exampleCN: 糖酵解是几乎所有细胞共有的代谢通路。
senses.why: the loop is drawn as many routes, so the adjective also marks a single path through the map.
senses.whyCN: 这条环路被画成许多路线，因此这个形容词也标记地图中的单条路径。

senses.title: Disorder of the turnover
senses.definition: describing disease caused by a fault in metabolism
senses.definitionCN: 描述由代谢缺陷引起的疾病
senses.example: Phenylketonuria is a metabolic disease found at birth screening.
senses.exampleCN: 苯丙酮尿症是一种在新生儿筛查中发现的代谢病。
senses.why: when one route fails, the whole body feels it, so the adjective names a clinical class.
senses.whyCN: 当某条路线失灵，全身都会受影响，因此这个形容词命名一个临床类别。

senses.title: What the loop leaves behind
senses.titleCN: 代谢废物的：周转的残余
senses.definition: describing substances produced as by-products of metabolism
senses.definitionCN: 描述作为代谢副产物产生的物质
senses.example: The kidneys clear metabolic waste such as urea.
senses.exampleCN: 肾脏清除尿素等代谢废物。
senses.why: every route has leftovers, so the adjective also qualifies what must be removed rather than what is used.
senses.whyCN: 每条路线都有残余，因此这个形容词也限定必须被清走的东西，而不是被使用的东西。

senses.title: Of the enzymes that run it
senses.titleCN: 代谢酶的：驱动周转的催化者
senses.definition: describing the enzymes and controls that keep the routes running
senses.definitionCN: 描述维持路线运行的酶与调控
senses.example: Metabolic enzymes are often the target of drugs.
senses.exampleCN: 代谢酶常是药物的靶点。
senses.why: since the loop is run by catalysts, the adjective extends to the machinery that drives it.
senses.whyCN: 由于环路由催化剂驱动，这个形容词便延伸到驱动它的机器。

senses.title: Busy tissue
senses.definition: describing tissue or an organ with a high turnover, such as liver or muscle in exercise
senses.definitionCN: 描述周转旺盛的组织或器官，如肝脏或运动中的肌肉
senses.example: The liver is the most metabolically active organ per gram.
senses.exampleCN: 按每克计，肝脏是代谢最活跃的器官。
senses.why: high turnover is a visible property of a tissue, so the adjective can describe a state rather than a process.
senses.whyCN: 高周转是组织可见的属性，因此这个形容词可以描述一种状态，而非一个过程。

senses.title: The clustered clinical picture
senses.titleCN: 代谢综合征的：成组出现的临床征象
senses.definition: describing the cluster of obesity, high blood sugar, high lipids and hypertension
senses.definitionCN: 描述肥胖、高血糖、高血脂与高血压成组出现的情形
senses.example: Metabolic syndrome raises the risk of diabetes and heart disease.
senses.exampleCN: 代谢综合征提高糖尿病与心脏病的风险。
senses.why: modern medicine grouped several signs under one name, so the adjective came to label that cluster.
senses.whyCN: 现代医学把若干征象归在一个名下，这个形容词便用来标记那一组。

intro.en: Metabolic is metabolism plus the relational suffix -ic, from Latin -icus and Greek -ikos. The base came from Greek metabolē 'a change'.
intro.cn: metabolic 是 metabolism 加关系后缀 -ic，后者出自拉丁 -icus 与希腊 -ikos；词基来自希腊 metabolē「变化」。

items.en: metabolē 'a change, a turning over' comes from meta- 'over' plus ballein 'to throw'; English metabolism was first a general word for change.
items.cn: metabolē「变化、翻转」由 meta-「越过」加 ballein「投掷」构成；英语 metabolism 最初泛指变化。

items.en: Greek -ikos formed adjectives of relation, and Latin took it as -icus; English keeps both as -ic.
items.cn: 希腊 -ikos 构成关系形容词，拉丁语吸收为 -icus；英语保留为 -ic。

items.en: The adjective appears in nineteenth-century physiology once metabolism was fixed as the body's chemical turnover; the first citation is approximate.
items.cn: 当 metabolism 被固定为体内化学周转后，该形容词于 19 世纪生理学文献中出现；最早书证年代为约数。

items.en: Twentieth-century medicine produced metabolic disease, metabolic syndrome and metabolic rate as standard labels.
items.cn: 20 世纪医学产生了 metabolic disease、metabolic syndrome、metabolic rate 等标准标签。

items.en: Biochemistry in the same century mapped the routes and fixed metabolic pathway as a term.
items.cn: 同一世纪的生物化学绘出路线图，并固定了 metabolic pathway 这一术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): ballein has no agreed pre-Greek origin and the Indo-European forms behind it are reconstructions; the earliest citation of the adjective is also not recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：ballein 在希腊语之前的来源无共识，其印欧形式属重构；该形容词的最早书证亦无确切记录。

note.en: Group one holds words of the same family or of a look-alike prefix; group two holds adjectives used in the same physiological sentences.
note.cn: 第一组是同族词或前缀形近词；第二组是出现在同一类生理学句子中的形容词。

entries.definition: The process itself. Metabolic qualifies a rate, route or disease, and cannot replace the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程本身；metabolic 只限定速率、路线或疾病，不能替代名词。

entries.definition: To act on a substance, as in 'the liver metabolizes the drug'. It names an action, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指对物质起作用，如「肝脏代谢该药」；命名动作，不是性质。

entries.definition: Cancer spread, from meta- plus stasis 'standing'. It shares meta- but not ballein, so it is not a metabolic relative.
entries.definitionCN: 指癌症转移，由 meta- 加 stasis「站立」构成；共享 meta-，但词根不是 ballein，故与 metabolic 不同族。

entries.definition: A product or input of metabolism. It is a countable molecule and never an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指代谢的产物或输入物；是可数分子，从不用作形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to catabolism, the breaking-down reactions. It is a narrower label than metabolic.
entries.definitionCN: 与分解代谢的拆解反应相关；比 metabolic 范围更窄。

entries.definition: Relating to anabolism, the building reactions that consume energy.
entries.definitionCN: 与消耗能量的合成反应相关。

entries.definition: Relating to the chemistry of living things generally; metabolic points specifically at the turnover.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指生物体内的化学；metabolic 特指周转过程。

entries.definition: Describing energy or liveliness; it does not name the body's chemical loop.
entries.definitionCN: 描述能量或活力；不命名体内的化学环路。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: metabolism + -ic: the relational ending of metabolic, catabolic and anabolic.
normal.cn: metabolism + -ic：与 metabolic、catabolic、anabolic 相同的关系词尾。

normal.en: The family runs metabolism, metabolic, metabolize, metabolite, metabolically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 metabolism、metabolic、metabolize、metabolite、metabolically。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: metabolic rate, metabolic pathway, metabolic disease, metabolic syndrome.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：代谢率、代谢通路、代谢病、代谢综合征。

normal.en: The pair is easy: metabolism is the loop, metabolic is the adjective of the loop.
normal.cn: 这组很好分：metabolism 是环路，metabolic 是环路的形容词。

normal.en: Exercise raises metabolic rate, and the liver is the most metabolically active organ by weight.
normal.cn: 运动会提高代谢率，而按重量计肝脏是代谢最活跃的器官。

abstract.en: Picture a dial on a conveyor loop, with a needle showing how fast it turns.
abstract.cn: 想象环形传送带上装一个表盘，指针显示它转得多快。

abstract.en: Picture a map where each route is one coloured line in a single network.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，每条路线都是同一网络中的一条彩线。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger that records both what is spent and what is thrown away.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，既记录花费，也记录丢弃。

examples.en: Metabolic activity in the brain stays high even during sleep.
examples.cn: 睡眠中大脑的代谢活动依然很高。

examples.en: A metabolic disorder was found in the newborn screening.
examples.cn: 新生儿筛查中发现了一种代谢障碍。

examples.en: The drug blocks a metabolic pathway used by the parasite.
examples.cn: 该药阻断寄生虫使用的一条代谢通路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「代谢（metabolism）＋ic」——带代谢属性的 → 代谢的、代谢速率的

root: 希腊 metabolē「变化」（meta- + ballein「投掷」）→ metabolism + 拉丁 -icus / 希腊 -ikos → metabolic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one relational suffix: the whole loop, its speed, one route, its failures, its leftovers, its enzymes, a busy tissue, and a cluster of clinical signs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个表关系的后缀散开：整条环路、它的速度、单条路线、它的故障、它的残余、它的酶、活跃的组织，以及一组临床征象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial mounted on a turning loop, measuring how fast the loop runs.
core.cn: 核心意象：环形传送带上装着表盘，测量环路转得多快。

branches.en: OWNERSHIP: the plainest reading, 'of metabolism'.
branches.cn: 归属：最朴素的义项，「代谢的」。

branches.en: SPEED: the dial reading, the rate of turnover.
branches.cn: 速度：表盘读数，即周转速率。

branches.en: ROUTES AND MACHINERY: a single pathway and the enzymes that run it.
branches.cn: 路线与机器：单条通路，以及驱动它的酶。

branches.en: FAILURE AND RESIDUE: disease when a route breaks, and waste that must be cleared.
branches.cn: 故障与残余：路线断裂时的疾病，以及必须清除的废物。

branches.en: STATE AND SYNDROME: a busy tissue, and several signs grouped under one label.
branches.cn: 状态与综合征：活跃的组织，以及归在一个标签下的若干征象。

intro.en: Metabolic is the Greek-derived noun metabolism plus the relational suffix -ic, from Latin -icus and Greek -ikos.
intro.cn: metabolic 是希腊来源名词 metabolism 加关系后缀 -ic，后者出自拉丁 -icus 与希腊 -ikos。

latinIntro.en: Only the suffix series is Latin-based; the base is the Greek metabolē, and New Latin metabolismus is a Latinized spelling.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后缀系列基于拉丁语；词基是希腊 metabolē，新拉丁语 metabolismus 只是拉丁化拼写。

items.example: Metabolic rate is measured at rest.
items.exampleCN: 代谢率在静息状态下测定。

items.example: The tissue is metabolically quiet.
items.exampleCN: 该组织代谢上很安静。

items.example: Metabolism slows with age.
items.exampleCN: 代谢随年龄减慢。

items.meaning: a substance made or used in metabolism
items.example: The metabolite was excreted in urine.
items.exampleCN: 该代谢产物经尿排出。

items.example: Cells metabolize glucose for energy.
items.exampleCN: 细胞代谢葡萄糖以获得能量。

items.example: Catabolic hormones raise blood sugar.
items.exampleCN: 分解代谢类激素升高血糖。

items.example: Anabolic pathways need ATP.
items.exampleCN: 合成代谢通路需要 ATP。

items.example: The pathway is conserved in bacteria.
items.exampleCN: 该通路在细菌中保守。

items.example: Metabolic syndrome is diagnosed clinically.
items.exampleCN: 代谢综合征以临床方式诊断。

latinEntries.meaning: relating to, of the nature of

definition_zh: 家畜；牲畜（总称）
definition_en: farm animals kept for use or profit, considered together as a group
core_image: 围栏里牛、羊、马、骆驼挤在一起，耳朵上打着标记，栏外是草场
scene: 围栏门打开，牛群与羊群被赶向草场，耳标在阳光下反光，牧人骑着马在后面压阵。 Livestock must be counted before the winter feed is allocated.
sceneCN: 这里指「饲养的家畜整体」（第 1 个义项：牲畜总称）；句意为在分配冬季饲料前必须先清点家畜。

pos.zh: 家畜；牲畜（不可数集合名词）

derivatives.zh: livestock + farming（组合成分）→ 畜牧业（语义偏移：从动物群落到经营行业）
livestock + feed（组合成分）→ 家畜饲料
livestock + producer（组合成分）→ 畜牧生产者
livestock + unit（组合成分）→ 家畜单位（语义偏移：转为统计计量）
livestock + market（组合成分）→ 牲畜市场
livestock + guardian dog（组合成分）→ 护畜犬（语义偏移：指专门守护畜群的犬）

senses.title: Farm animals kept as a group
senses.definition: domesticated animals raised on a farm for food, work, fibre or profit, treated as one category
senses.definitionCN: 为食物、劳作、纤维或利润而在农场饲养的家养动物，作为一个类别看待
senses.example: The farm keeps livestock and grows fodder for them.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场饲养家畜，并为其种植饲料。
senses.why: The compound joins live and stock, so the category is literally living property rather than animals seen one by one.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把 live 与 stock 结合，因此该类别的字面义是「活着的财产」，而非逐只观看的动物。

senses.title: Cattle in a narrow regional use
senses.definition: cattle specifically, in regions where cattle are the dominant farm animal
senses.definitionCN: 在某些地区特指牛，因为牛是当地主要家畜
senses.example: In that county livestock means cattle, not sheep.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个郡，这个词指牛，而非羊。
senses.why: A general category can be narrowed by local practice until the general word names the commonest member.
senses.whyCN: 泛指类别会被地方实践收窄，直到普通词指最常见的成员。

senses.title: Breeding stock
senses.definition: animals kept to produce young rather than to be sold or worked directly
senses.definitionCN: 为繁殖后代而饲养、而非直接出售或役使的动物
senses.example: Half the herd is breeding livestock kept for replacement heifers.
senses.exampleCN: 这群牛有一半是留作补充母牛的种畜。
senses.why: Stock also means a fund or supply, so animals kept to renew the herd are stock in the strict sense.
senses.whyCN: stock 也有「储备、本钱」之义，因此用于更新畜群的动物正是严格意义上的「本钱」。

senses.title: Animals counted as capital
senses.definition: livestock viewed as a financial asset whose value is recorded and insured
senses.definitionCN: 被视为金融资产、需要记账与投保的家畜
senses.example: The bank valued the livestock before approving the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 银行在批准贷款前对牲畜作了估值。
senses.why: The word's second element already means property, so the financial reading was present from the start.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的第二个成分本就意为财产，因此金融读法从一开始就存在。

senses.title: A herd on pasture
senses.definition: the animals while they are grazing or being moved across land
senses.definitionCN: 正在吃草或正被赶过土地的动物群
senses.example: Livestock graze the high pasture from June to September.
senses.exampleCN: 家畜从六月到九月在高地牧场吃草。
senses.why: The category becomes a moving collectivity when the animals are out on the land.
senses.whyCN: 当动物在土地上移动时，这个类别就变成一个移动的集体。

senses.title: Animals inside a mixed farm
senses.titleCN: 混合农场中的家畜环节
senses.definition: livestock as one component of a system that also grows crops
senses.definitionCN: 作为同时种植作物的系统中的家畜环节
senses.example: Mixed farming uses livestock to cycle nutrients back to the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 混合农业利用家畜把养分循环回田里。
senses.why: In a system, livestock is not only animals but a function: manure, traction and demand for fodder.
senses.whyCN: 在系统中，家畜不只是动物，还是一种功能：粪肥、畜力与对饲料的需求。

senses.title: A source of manure and traction
senses.definition: animals valued for dung, ploughing and transport rather than for meat or milk
senses.definitionCN: 因粪肥、耕地与运输而被重视，而非为肉或奶的动物
senses.example: On the small holding, livestock provide both manure and plough power.
senses.exampleCN: 在这块小地上，家畜同时提供粪肥与犁耕动力。
senses.why: Before engines, the living stock was the farm's energy system, and the word carries that memory.
senses.whyCN: 在发动机之前，活的家畜就是农场的能源系统，这个词带着那段记忆。

senses.title: Animals under herd-health control
senses.titleCN: 畜群健康管理中的家畜
senses.definition: the animals considered as a population to be monitored, vaccinated and quarantined
senses.definitionCN: 被视为需要监测、接种与隔离的动物群体
senses.example: Livestock movement is tracked to control disease.
senses.exampleCN: 为控制疫病，家畜的移动受到追踪。
senses.why: Veterinary medicine treats the herd as one unit, so the collective noun becomes a technical subject.
senses.whyCN: 兽医学把畜群当作一个单位，因此这个集合名词成为技术对象。

intro.en: Livestock is an English compound of live, living, and stock, a supply or fund. It names animals as living property and contrasts with dead stock, the tools and goods on a farm. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: livestock 是英语复合词，由 live「活着的」与 stock「储备、本钱」构成。它把动物命名为「活着的财产」，与 dead stock（农具与货物）相对。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stoc meant a tree trunk, a post or a fixed body, and from that came the sense of a stored supply or a fund.
items.cn: stoc 意为树干、柱子或固定主体，由此引申出「储备、本钱」之义。

items.en: Middle English stock covered goods, money and animals kept as a holding, so the word already implied property.
items.cn: 中古英语 stock 涵盖货物、钱与作为资产饲养的动物，因此这个词已含财产之意。

items.en: The compound live stock separated animals from dead stock, the implements and goods that do not breathe.
items.cn: 复合词 live stock 把动物与 dead stock（不会呼吸的器具与货物）区分开来。

items.en: The compound is recorded in English from the sixteenth century, first in estate accounts and farming manuals.
items.cn: 这个复合词在十六世纪的英语中已有记录，最早见于田产账目与农书。

items.en: Modern agriculture made livestock a sector word covering production, feed, units and health control.
items.cn: 现代农业使 livestock 成为部门词，涵盖生产、饲料、计量单位与健康管理。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact moment when live stock became one written word is not documented, and the deeper origin of stock is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：live stock 何时写成一个词没有确切记载，stock 的更早来源也属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words built on stock or live that are easily confused; group two holds collective words for farm animals.
note.cn: 第一组是由 stock 或 live 构成、易混淆的词；第二组是农场动物的集合名词。

entries.definition: A supply of goods, a fund, or shares in a company; livestock is specifically the living part of a farm's stock.
entries.definitionCN: 货物储备、资金或公司股份；livestock 特指农场储备中活的那部分。

entries.definition: Tools, machinery and unsold goods, the non-living property of a farm; it contrasts directly with livestock.
entries.definitionCN: 工具、机械与未售货物，即农场中非活的部分；与 livestock 直接相对。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning living or not yet dead; alone it does not name animals as property.
entries.definitionCN: 意为活着的、尚未死的形容词；单独使用并不指作为财产的动物。

entries.definition: The means by which someone earns a living; it looks like live plus stock but is built from a different second element.
entries.definitionCN: 某人谋生的手段；看起来像 live 加 stock，但第二个成分不同。

entries.definition: Domesticated bovines as a group; livestock is broader and includes sheep, goats, pigs and horses.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的家牛；livestock 范围更广，还包括羊、山羊、猪与马。

entries.definition: A group of animals of one kind kept together; livestock is a category, a herd is a particular gathering.
entries.definitionCN: 同类动物聚在一起的一群；livestock 是类别，herd 是具体的群。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for animals kept on a farm; livestock is its formal and commercial equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 农场饲养动物的日常说法；livestock 是其正式、商业化的对应词。

entries.definition: Animals used to pull ploughs or carts; they are one function of livestock, not the whole category.
entries.definitionCN: 用于拉犁或拉车的动物；它们是家畜的一种功能，而非整个类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: live plus stock: living property, as opposed to dead stock.
normal.cn: live 加 stock：活着的财产，与 dead stock 相对。

normal.en: The family runs livestock, livestock farming, livestock feed, livestock unit, livestock market.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 livestock、livestock farming、livestock feed、livestock unit、livestock market。

normal.en: The word is uncountable: one says livestock, not livestocks.
normal.cn: 这个词不可数：说 livestock，不说 livestocks。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the sector: livestock production, livestock sector, livestock guardian dog.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示部门义：畜牧生产、畜牧部门、护畜犬。

normal.en: The old contrast with dead stock explains why live is inside the word.
normal.cn: 与 dead stock 的旧对照解释了 live 为何在其中。

abstract.en: Picture a farm ledger where animals and tools are written in two separate columns.
abstract.cn: 想象一本农场账簿，动物与工具分列两栏。

abstract.en: Picture a field that eats: the herd is a machine that turns grass into milk and manure.
abstract.cn: 想象一块会吃的田：畜群是一台把草变成奶与粪肥的机器。

abstract.en: Picture a moving warehouse of value, lowing as it crosses the road.
abstract.cn: 想象一座会移动的价值仓库，过马路时发出低鸣。

examples.en: Livestock accounted for half the family's income.
examples.cn: 家畜占了这个家庭收入的一半。

examples.en: The drought forced farmers to sell livestock early.
examples.cn: 干旱迫使农民提前出售家畜。

examples.en: Livestock health checks are required before any animal is moved.
examples.cn: 任何动物移动之前都必须做家畜健康检查。

dict_mnemonic.text: live（活的）+ stock（储备、本钱）→ 活着的本钱，即农场里能繁殖、产奶、干活、卖钱的牲畜总称。

root: live（古英语 libban「活着」）+ stock（古英语 stoc「树干、固定主体」，引申为储备、本钱）；与 dead stock（农具货物）相对，十六世纪起合为一词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one category: animals are first living property, then cattle by region, breeding stock, capital, a grazing herd, a farm function, a source of power and a monitored population.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个类别展开：动物先是活财产，再按地区指牛、种畜、资本、放牧畜群、农场功能、动力来源与被监测的群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a farmyard full of breathing property, each animal carrying a mark that says whose it is.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个装满会呼吸的财产的农家院落，每只动物都带着标记，说明它属于谁。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY: all farm animals, or cattle alone where cattle dominate.
branches.cn: 类别：全部农场动物，或在牛占主导的地方单指牛。

branches.en: THE NEXT GENERATION: animals kept to renew the herd.
branches.cn: 下一代：为更新畜群而留的动物。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: animals with a price and an insurance entry.
branches.cn: 账簿：有价格、有保险条目的动物。

branches.en: THE LAND AND THE SYSTEM: grazing herds and the role animals play in mixed farming.
branches.cn: 土地与系统：放牧的畜群，以及动物在混合农业中的角色。

branches.en: POWER AND CONTROL: manure and traction, then vaccination and quarantine.
branches.cn: 动力与控制：粪肥与畜力，然后是接种与隔离。

intro.en: Livestock is a native English compound, not a Latin derivative; its parts are two old Germanic words, and its family is built by compounding.
intro.cn: livestock 是英语本族复合词，并非拉丁派生词；其组成部分是两个古老的日耳曼词，词族靠复合方式扩展。

latinIntro.en: Neither live nor stock has a reliable Latin relative, so the Latin side is left empty; the word's history is Germanic and English.
latinIntro.cn: live 与 stock 都没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁部分留空；这个词的历史属于日耳曼语与英语。

items.example: The first element separates animals from tools.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分把动物与工具分开。

items.example: The second element supplies the idea of property.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分提供财产之意。

items.example: Livestock wintered in the lower barn.
items.exampleCN: 家畜在低处的棚里过冬。

items.example: Livestock farming replaced the old wool trade.
items.exampleCN: 畜牧业取代了旧的羊毛贸易。

items.meaning: food grown or mixed for animals
items.meaningCN: 为家畜种植或混合的饲料
items.example: Livestock feed prices rose with the drought.
items.exampleCN: 家畜饲料价格随干旱上涨。

items.meaning: a standard measure of grazing demand
items.meaningCN: 衡量放牧需求的标准单位
items.example: One livestock unit equals one mature cow.
items.exampleCN: 一个家畜单位等于一头成年牛。

items.example: The livestock producer sold directly to the butcher.
items.exampleCN: 这位畜牧生产者直接把畜产品卖给屠户。

items.meaning: a place or trade for buying and selling animals
items.meaningCN: 买卖家畜的场所或交易
items.example: The livestock market opens before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 牲畜市场天亮前开市。

items.meaning: a dog bred to protect a herd
items.example: The livestock guardian dog slept among the sheep.
items.exampleCN: 护畜犬睡在羊群中间。
